Inferior surface relates to skin, superficial fascia with platysma, deep fascia, facial vein, cervical facial-nerve branch and submandibular nodes. Medial surface: anteriorly mylohyoid muscle, nerve and artery; centrally hyoglossus with structures on its lateral surface; posteriorly pharyngeal wall separated by glossopharyngeal nerve, styloglossus and stylohyoid ligament. Deep part is between mylohyoid and hyoglossus, extends to posterior sublingual gland, and lies between lingual nerve above and hypoglossal below. The parts unite around posterior mylohyoid border.

questions.text: 46. Regarding the submandibular salivary gland, choose one correct statement:
questions.explanation: The submandibular duct opens on the sublingual papilla beside the frenulum. This is distinct from the many small ducts of the sublingual gland, which open along the sublingual fold.
options: Its superficial part lies above the mylohyoid muscle.
Its deep part lies deep to the hyoglossus muscle.
Its duct opens on top of sublingual papilla.
Its medial surface is related to submandibular fossa on the medial surface of mandible.
Its parasympathetic supply is through the lesser petrosal nerve.

questions.text: 29. A branch from the 1st part of the lingual artery:
questions.explanation: The suprahyoid artery is a small branch of the first part of the lingual artery; the sublingual artery arises farther forward.

questions.text: 37. All of the following lie superficial to hyoglossus muscle EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lingual artery is the exception because it runs deep to hyoglossus; the lingual nerve, ganglion, gland, and hypoglossal nerve lie on the superficial side.

questions.text: 27. Deep to the hyoglossus muscle is the:
questions.explanation: Glossopharyngeal nerve lies deep to hyoglossus, along with lingual artery and hypoglossal nerve in the deep tongue region. The lingual nerve is superficial to the muscle.

questions.text: 50. Submandibular duct opens into:
questions.explanation: The submandibular duct opens on the summit of the sublingual papilla beside the frenulum, not into the vestibule or along the fold.
options: Vestibule of mouth opposite upper second molar.
Vestibule of mouth opposite lower second molar.

questions.text: 43. All is true regarding the digastric muscles EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The digastric tendon is held by a fibrous sling attached to the hyoid; it does not pierce stylopharyngeus, which is a separate pharyngeal elevator.
options: They bound both digastric and submental triangles.
Anterior belly is supplied by mandibular nerve.
Posterior belly is supplied by facial nerve.
The intermediate tendon perforates stylopharyngeus muscle.

questions.text: 53. All of the following are correctly related to the sublingual salivary gland EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lingual nerve lies medial to the sublingual gland rather than laterally. The gland lies between the mandible and genioglossus, resting on mylohyoid.
options: Mucous membrane of floor of mouth superiorly.

questions.text: 39- Structure separating lateral surface of submandibular gland & mandible
questions.explanation: The facial artery grooves the posterior part of the submandibular gland and crosses the mandibular border nearby, separating it from the mandible in this region.

questions.text: 24. A structure deep to the hyoglossus muscle:
questions.explanation: The lingual artery travels deep to hyoglossus, supplying the tongue; the lingual and hypoglossal nerves and submandibular ganglion are superficial to the muscle.

questions.text: 28. The structure deep to the hyoglossus muscle is the:
questions.explanation: Genioglossus lies medial and deep to hyoglossus, forming much of the tongue's bulk. The lingual artery and hypoglossal nerve also pass deep to hyoglossus.

questions.text: 39. Regarding hyoglossus muscle, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hyoglossus is a tongue muscle supplied by CN XII; CN IX is sensory and lies deep to the muscle, so that innervation claim is the exception.
options: It is one of the muscles of the tongue.
It arises from body and greater horns of hyoid bone.
Hypoglossal nerve runs along its lower border.
It is supplied by glossopharyngeal nerve.
Glossopharyngeal nerve lies deep to it.

questions.text: 42. Regarding mylohyoid muscle, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Mylohyoid’s median raphe joins the two sides and anchors to the hyoid, not thyroid cartilage; together the muscles form the muscular floor of mouth.
options: Its median fibrous raphe attaches to thyroid cartilage.
Its posterior fibers insert into hyoid bone.
Its nerve is a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve.

questions.text: 47. Regarding the submandibular salivary gland, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The submandibular gland has a superficial part below mylohyoid and a deep part that hooks around its posterior border into the floor of the mouth; it is not entirely deep to the muscle.
options: Has two lobes, superficial and deep.
Discharges into the mouth via the sublingual papilla.
Lies entirely deep to the mylohyoid.
Receives secretomotor fibers from the submandibular ganglion.

questions.text: 25. The muscle supplied by 2 cranial nerves is the:
questions.explanation: Digastric has two bellies with different innervation: anterior belly by mylohyoid nerve (V3), posterior belly by facial nerve (VII).

questions.text: 52. Submandibular gland receives parasympathetic innervation from:
questions.explanation: Chorda tympani carries facial preganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the submandibular ganglion, where they synapse before reaching the gland.

questions.text: 40. When performing a midline abdominal paracentesis (tapping the abdominal cavity) below the umbilicus, the cannula will pass through the following anatomic structures except:
questions.explanation: At the midline below the umbilicus, a needle passes through linea alba rather than rectus abdominis, which lies on either side. This avoids cutting muscle and its vessels.
options: The transversalis fascia and extraperitoneal fat

questions.text: 11. Which muscle of the anterior abdominal wall arises from the outer surface of the ribs?
questions.explanation: External oblique originates from the outer surfaces of ribs 5–12; internal oblique and transversus arise deeper from fascia, iliac crest, and lower rib structures.

questions.text: 85- Linea semilunaris is the lateral border of which muscle
questions.explanation: The linea semilunaris marks the lateral edge of rectus abdominis, where the aponeuroses of the flat abdominal muscles meet the rectus sheath.

questions.text: 81- Linea alba receive insertion of all the following muscles Except
questions.explanation: The three flat abdominal muscle aponeuroses decussate in the linea alba; rectus abdominis runs within the rectus sheath and attaches to the pubis and costal cartilages instead.

questions.text: 26. The origin of the external oblique muscle is from the:
questions.explanation: External oblique fibers arise from the outer surfaces of ribs 5 through 12, forming the superficial muscular layer of the lateral abdominal wall.

questions.text: 94- intertibercular plane lies opposite to which vertebral level
questions.explanation: The intertubercular (transtubercular) plane crosses the iliac tubercles at about L5, a useful landmark for abdominal surface anatomy.

questions.text: 6. Which muscle in the anterior abdominal wall IS NOT inserted into the linea alba?
questions.explanation: Rectus abdominis lies in the rectus sheath and attaches to the pubis and costal cartilages, rather than inserting into the midline linea alba like the flat-muscle aponeuroses.

questions.text: ANA6: The superficial fatty layer of the abdominal fascia is called:
questions.explanation: Camper fascia is the fatty superficial layer of the membranous superficial fascia; Scarpa fascia is the deeper membranous layer.

questions.text: 31. The following statements concerning the superficial fascia of the anterior abdominal wall are true except:
questions.explanation: Camper’s fatty layer continues into the superficial fatty fascia of the thigh, whereas Scarpa’s membranous layer continues into Colles’ fascia of the perineum.
options: It has a superficial fatty layer and a deep membranous layer
Scarpa's fascia fuses with the fascia lata just below the inguinal ligament
Camper's fascia is continuous with the Colles' fascia in the perineum
It is continuous with the dartos muscle in the wall of the scrotum
It does not contribute to the femoral sheath

questions.text: 32. Which of the following structures lies at the level of the subcostal plane?
questions.explanation: The inferior mesenteric artery typically arises from the abdominal aorta at L3, close to the subcostal plane. The plane itself passes through the lower border of the tenth costal cartilages.

questions.text: 100- Floor of lumbar triangle is by which
questions.explanation: The floor of the inferior lumbar triangle is internal oblique, with latissimus dorsi and external oblique forming its borders.

questions.text: 40. The body of the fourth lumbar vertebra lies at the same level as the:
questions.explanation: The abdominal aorta usually bifurcates at L4; the superior mesenteric artery origin is higher, around L1.
options: Origin of the superior mesenteric artery.

questions.text: 29. The aponeurosis of the transversus abdominis muscle contributes to:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is formed by fused aponeurotic fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis, reinforcing the medial posterior wall of the inguinal canal.

questions.text: 171-intertubercular plane lies at which vertebral
questions.explanation: The intertubercular plane joins the iliac tubercles and crosses the upper L5 body. Do not confuse it with the higher intercristal plane, used to identify the lumbar puncture level.

questions.text: 75- pyramidalis muscle is supplied by
questions.explanation: Pyramidalis receives motor fibers from the subcostal nerve (T12), consistent with its position in the lower anterior abdominal wall.

questions.text: 85. The external oblique muscle:
questions.explanation: External oblique receives segmental motor supply from the lower six thoracic nerves, including the subcostal nerve (T12), which also supplies the abdominal wall skin.
options: Inserts on the internal surfaces of the seventh through twelfth costal cartilages
Makes up the entire rectus sheath inferior to the umbilicus
Originates on the pubic symphysis and pubic crest
Is innervated by the inferior six thoracic spinal nerves (intercostals nerves and subcostal nerves)

questions.text: 93. The median, medial and lateral umbilical folds of the anterior abdominal wall are formed respectively by the:
questions.explanation: The median umbilical fold overlies urachus, medial folds over obliterated umbilical arteries, and lateral folds over inferior epigastric vessels.
options: Urachus, obliterated umbilical arteries and inferior epigastric arteries
Urachus, obliterated umbilical arteries and veins
Urachus, obliterated umbilical arteries and superficial epigastric arteries

questions.text: 33. Which of the following correctly describes pyramidalis muscle:
questions.explanation: Pyramidalis is a small, variable muscle within the rectus sheath, anterior to the lower rectus abdominis; its absence is common.
options: It is a large pyramidal well developed muscle.
It is contained within the rectus sheath.
It is posterior to the rectus abdominis.
It is supplied by the 10th thoracic nerve.

questions.text: 34. The rectus abdominis muscle:
questions.explanation: Rectus abdominis is paired across the linea alba, has tendinous intersections, receives thoracoabdominal nerve supply, and attaches to the pubis; therefore each listed statement is correct.
options: Is separated from its fellow by the linea alba.
Is attached to the crest of the pubis.

questions.text: 38. The transpyloric plane marks the position of the following:
questions.explanation: The gallbladder fundus commonly meets the transpyloric plane near the right midclavicular line; this plane is at L1 and marks several upper-abdominal structures.

questions.text: The external oblique muscle is characterized by:
questions.explanation: The external oblique aponeurosis forms the superficial inguinal ring, the exit of the inguinal canal; its fibers run inferomedially.
options: Forms the anterior layer of the neurovascular plane.
Its fibers are directed downward laterally and anteriorly.
The lateral border intersects with 9th rib.

questions.text:
The plane which passes from the midpoint of the clavicle to a point midway between the anterior superior iliac spine
and the pubic symphysis is:
questions.explanation: The lateral vertical (midclavicular) plane descends from the clavicular midpoint to the midinguinal point, halfway between the ASIS and pubic symphysis.

questions.text: 25. The external oblique muscle of the anterior abdominal wall and its fascia contribute to all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is formed by internal oblique and transversus aponeuroses, not external oblique; external oblique forms the inguinal ligament, anterior sheath, superficial ring, and external spermatic fascia.

questions.text: 23. Concerning the anterior abdominal wall, all the following statements are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Scarpa’s fascia attaches to fascia lata just inferior to the inguinal ligament, so it is not attached directly to the ligament as stated.
options: Is innervated mainly by the lower thoracic nerves.
Lymphatics from skin above umbilicus drain into axillary lymph nodes.
Veins from skin below umbilicus drain mainly into great saphenous vein.
Membranous layer of its superficial fascia is attached below to inguinal ligament.

questions.text: 9. The tendinous intersections of the rectus abdominis muscles are:
questions.explanation: Rectus tendinous intersections are firmly attached to the anterior layer of the rectus sheath, while they are not fixed as firmly posteriorly.
options: Adherent to the anterior wall of the rectus sheath.
Adherent to the posterior wall of the rectus sheath.

questions.text: 32. The rectus sheath contains the following structure except:
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres runs in the free edge of the falciform ligament, not inside the rectus sheath; rectus, pyramidalis, epigastric vessels, and thoracoabdominal nerves can lie in the sheath.

questions.text: 77. The area around the umbilicus receives sensory innervation from the:
questions.explanation: The umbilicus is the T10 dermatome landmark, carried by the anterior ramus of T10; this helps localize abdominal pain and sensory loss.
options: Anterior branch of the ventral ramus of the spinal nerve T10

questions.text: 84- lower border of the posterior wall of Rectus sheath is anatomically known as
questions.explanation: The arcuate line marks the lower limit of the posterior rectus sheath; below it, no aponeurosis passes behind rectus.

questions.text: 92- skin of anterior abdominal wall below Umblicus drain its lymph into
questions.explanation: Superficial lymphatics below the umbilicus descend to superficial inguinal nodes, while lymphatics above it generally drain to axillary nodes.

questions.text: 89- anterior wall of Rectus sheath between xiphoid & umblicus formed by
questions.explanation: Above the umbilicus, the external oblique aponeurosis and anterior lamina of internal oblique form the anterior rectus sheath; the posterior lamina of internal oblique and transversus aponeurosis form its back wall.

questions.text: 1. Which of the following lies in front of the lower part of the rectus abdominis muscle?
questions.explanation: Pyramidalis lies anterior to the lower rectus within the rectus sheath and tenses the linea alba; epigastric vessels and nerves are deeper/posterior.

questions.text: 40. The vessels and nerves supplying the anterior abdominal wall course:
questions.explanation: The thoracoabdominal nerves and accompanying vessels travel in the neurovascular plane between internal oblique and transversus abdominis before entering the rectus sheath.
options: Between the external and the internal oblique muscles.
Between the internal oblique and the transversus abdominis.

questions.text: 22. The skin of the abdominal wall at level of umbilicus is supplied by:
questions.explanation: The umbilical skin corresponds to the T10 dermatome, a useful surface landmark. Visceral afferents from the midgut also commonly refer pain to this level.

questions.text: 15. The anterior wall of the rectus sheath between the xiphoid process & the umbilicus is formed by the aponeurosis of:
questions.explanation: Above the arcuate line, external oblique and the anterior lamina of internal oblique form the anterior rectus sheath; posterior internal oblique and transversus form its back.

questions.text: 20. Nerves that enter the rectus sheath do not include:
questions.explanation: Thoracoabdominal nerves T7–T11 and subcostal T12 enter the rectus sheath; L1 branches supply the lower abdominal wall but do not enter the sheath.

questions.text: 114. Inferior to the arcuate line, which of the following structures lies posterior to the rectus muscle?
questions.explanation: Below the arcuate line, the rectus muscle rests directly on transversalis fascia, with no posterior aponeurotic rectus sheath behind it.

questions.text: 78. Inferior the arcuate line, which of the following structures lies posterior to the rectus muscle?
questions.explanation: Below the arcuate line all three aponeuroses pass anterior to rectus, leaving only transversalis fascia and peritoneum posteriorly.
options: Aponeurosis of internal oblique and tranversus abdominis

questions.text: 18. The branch of the internal iliac artery that anastomoses with the inferior epigastric artery is the:
questions.explanation: The obturator artery gives a pubic branch that can connect with the pubic branch of the inferior epigastric artery, an important collateral route near the femoral canal.

questions.text: 90- which is Not content of Rectus sheath
questions.explanation: The iliohypogastric nerve courses in the abdominal wall outside the rectus sheath; the sheath contains rectus, pyramidalis when present, epigastric vessels, and terminal thoracoabdominal nerves.

questions.text: 38. As regards inferior epigastric artery, all the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac just above the inguinal ligament, then ascends medial to the deep ring and joins the superior epigastric.
options: It arises from internal iliac artery.
It passes medial to deep inguinal ring.
It enters rectus sheath by piercing fascia transversalis.
It anastomoses with the superior epigastric artery.

questions.text: 36. Enclosed within the sheath of the rectus abdominis muscle:
questions.explanation: The rectus sheath is built from the flat-muscle aponeuroses and encloses rectus abdominis, vessels, nerves, and sometimes pyramidalis; the listed neighboring lines and fascia are not sheath contents.

questions.text: 119-End of posterior wall of rectus sheath at level of
questions.explanation: The posterior rectus sheath ends at the arcuate line. Below it, all three flat-muscle aponeuroses pass anterior to rectus, leaving transversalis fascia posteriorly.

questions.text: 21. The lower border of the posterior wall of the rectus sheath is called:
questions.explanation: The arcuate line is the lower border of the posterior rectus sheath; below it, rectus lies directly on transversalis fascia.

questions.text: 87- lateral thoracic vein drain into
questions.explanation: The lateral thoracic vein drains into the axillary vein, returning blood from the lateral thoracic wall and breast region.

questions.text: 39. The inferior epigastric artery arises from:
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery branches from the external iliac artery just above the inguinal ligament and ascends behind rectus to anastomose with the superior epigastric artery.

questions.text: 93- superfecial epigastric artery is branch from
questions.explanation: The superficial epigastric artery arises from the femoral artery just below the inguinal ligament and ascends in superficial fascia.

questions.text: 76- inferior epigastric artery is abranch from
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac artery just above the inguinal ligament and ascends behind rectus abdominis.

questions.text: 66. Below the arcuate line, which of the following structures lies posterior to the rectus muscle?
questions.explanation: Below the arcuate line, the posterior covering of rectus is transversalis fascia (and deeper extraperitoneal tissue and peritoneum), because the aponeuroses all pass anteriorly.

questions.text: 88- skin around umblicus is supplied by
questions.explanation: The umbilicus is the T10 dermatome, so its surrounding skin sensation is carried by the tenth thoracic spinal nerve.

questions.text: Illustrate the lymphatic drainage of the anterior abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: Superficial lymph follows skin territories: above the umbilicus toward axillary nodes and below it toward superficial inguinal nodes; deep drainage follows vessels to parasternal, external iliac, and para-aortic nodes.
questions.modelAnswer:
Lymphatic drainage → Superficial (superficial fascia) → Above umbilicus → Pectoral L.N
Lymphatic drainage → Superficial (superficial fascia) → Below umbilicus → Superficial inguinal
Lymphatic drainage → Deep (deep arteries) → Parasternal
Lymphatic drainage → Deep (deep arteries) → Paraaortic
Lymphatic drainage → Deep (deep arteries) → External iliac

questions.text: 86- inferior epigastric artery is branch from
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac artery and ascends superomedially toward the rectus sheath; it forms a landmark for direct versus indirect hernias.

questions.text: 14. The vessels and nerves of the anterior abdominal wall are deep to:
questions.explanation: The neurovascular plane lies between internal oblique and transversus abdominis, placing segmental nerves and vessels deep to internal oblique.

questions.text: 35. Regarding rectus sheath, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves run in the abdominal wall and do not enter the rectus sheath; the sheath contains thoracoabdominal nerves and epigastric vessels.
options: It is formed by the aponeurosis of the 3 lateral abdominal muscles.
Its anterior wall is attached to the rectus abdominis.
It contains superior and inferior epigastric arteries.
It contains iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves.
The rectus sheath is separated from its fellow by the linea alba.

questions.text: What are contents of the rectus sheath
questions.explanation: The rectus sheath encloses rectus abdominis and sometimes pyramidalis, the superior and inferior epigastric vessels, and lower thoracoabdominal nerves. Its posterior wall is absent below the arcuate line.
questions.modelAnswer: Rectus abdominis, pyramidalis, superior and inferior epigastric vessels, terminal T7–T11 and T12 nerves.

questions.text: 82- Neurovascular plane of anterior abdominal wall lies between
questions.explanation: Thoracoabdominal nerves and vessels travel between internal oblique and transversus abdominis, the neurovascular plane of the abdominal wall.

questions.text: 17. Which of the following IS NOT a content of the rectus sheath?
questions.explanation: The ilioinguinal nerve travels in the lower abdominal wall and inguinal canal, not the rectus sheath; thoracoabdominal nerves and the subcostal nerve do enter it.

questions.text: 28. The skin of the umbilicus receives its sensory innervation from:
questions.explanation: T10 is the umbilical dermatome: sensory fibers from skin at the navel enter the spinal cord at that segment.

questions.text: 7. A structure present in posterior wall of the inguinal canal:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon reinforces the medial posterior wall of the inguinal canal; transversalis fascia forms most of that wall.

questions.text: 30. The cremaster muscle is usually a continuation of the:
questions.explanation: The cremaster develops mainly from internal oblique muscle fibers as they arch over the spermatic cord; the transversus abdominis contributes little or no covering.

questions.text: 71- internal spermatic fascia derived from
questions.explanation: The transversalis fascia continues through the deep inguinal ring and forms the internal spermatic fascia as it accompanies the cord into the canal.

questions.text: 29. In both sexes, the inguinal canal is formed by:
questions.explanation: The inguinal canal develops along the processus vaginalis pathway of gonadal descent; in females the corresponding processus usually regresses.
options: The contraction of the cremaster muscle

questions.text: 89. Position of the deep inguinal ring relative to the inferior epigastric vessels is:
questions.explanation: The deep inguinal ring is an opening in transversalis fascia lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; indirect hernias enter there.

questions.text: 54. All of the following structures concerning the spermatic cord are true except:
questions.explanation: The spermatic cord has three coverings: internal spermatic fascia, cremasteric muscle/fascia, and external spermatic fascia. The tunica vaginalis surrounds the testis, not the cord as a fifth sheath.
options: It extends from the deep inguinal ring to the scrotum
It is covered by five layers of spermatic fascia
It contains lymph vessels that drain the testis

questions.text: 10. Which of the following IS NOT in the posterior wall of the inguinal canal?
questions.explanation: The pectineal ligament supports the floor/medial inguinal region rather than forming the canal’s posterior wall; transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon do.

questions.text: 35. The spermatic cord contains the following structures except:
questions.explanation: The spermatic cord contains testicular and deferential structures plus autonomic fibers; scrotal arteries and veins supply the scrotal wall and are not cord contents.

questions.text: 43. The posterior wall of the inguinal canal is formed of:
questions.explanation: The posterior inguinal wall combines transversalis fascia with medial reinforcement from conjoint tendon and reflected inguinal ligament.
options: Reflected part of the inguinal ligament.

questions.text: 73- cremasteric muscle derived from
questions.explanation: Cremaster fibers are derived from internal oblique and descend with the spermatic cord, forming a muscle-and-fascia covering.

questions.text: 58. To pass a needle into the cavity of the tunica vaginalis in the scrotum, the following structures have to be pierced except:
questions.explanation: To enter the tunica vaginalis cavity, the needle crosses the scrotal coverings and parietal tunica vaginalis. Tunica albuginea is the fibrous capsule of the testis and should not be pierced.

questions.text: 72- which of the following nerves pass through deep inguinal ring
questions.explanation: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve enters the deep ring and accompanies the spermatic cord; the ilioinguinal nerve enters the canal through the abdominal wall instead.

questions.text: 60. Regarding hernias in the inguinal region
questions.explanation: A direct hernia pushes through the weakened posterior wall medial to the inferior epigastric vessels; an indirect hernia enters lateral to them at the deep ring.
options: The sac of an indirect hernia lies posterior to the spermatic cord
The sac of a direct hernia lies lateral to the internal ring
The sac of a direct hernia lies medial to the inferior epigastric vessels
The sac of a direct inguinal hernia usually comes down to the scrotum
The sac of the femoral hernia has a wide neck

questions.text: 99- skin of scrotum is supplied by which spinal cord segment
questions.explanation: L1 contributes sensation to the anterior scrotum through ilioinguinal and genitofemoral pathways; posterior scrotal skin is supplied by S2–S4 pudendal branches.

questions.text: 107. Which of the following structures forms the floor (inferior border) of the inguinal canal:
questions.explanation: The inguinal ligament forms the canal’s floor, spanning from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle.

questions.text: 42. The anterior wall of the inguinal canal is formed of:
questions.explanation: External oblique aponeurosis forms the anterior wall of the inguinal canal; internal oblique reinforces its lateral part. The medial wall is reinforced by conjoint tendon.
options: Aponeurosis of internal abdominal oblique muscle.

questions.text: 1-  The external oblique muscle shares in the inguinal canal in:
questions.explanation: External oblique aponeurosis forms the anterior wall and its rolled lower edge forms the inguinal ligament, the canal floor.

questions.text:
Regarding the compensatory mechanisms protecting the inguinal canal, internal oblique muscle is responsible for
which of the following mechanisms
questions.explanation: Internal oblique fibers arch over the canal and contract like a shutter, narrowing its roof during increased abdominal pressure.

questions.text: 57. All of the following statements concerning the an indirect inguinal hernia are true except:
questions.explanation: An indirect hernia enters lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels at the deep ring, so a sac neck medial to those vessels describes a direct hernia instead.
options: It is the most common form of abdominal hernia
The neck of the hernial sac lies medial to the inferior epigastric artery
The sac is the remains of the processus vaginalis
The hernial sac can extend into the scrotum
At the superficial inguinal ring, the hernial sac lies above and medial to the pubic tubercle

questions.text: 26. Which of the following statements regarding the superficial inguinal ring is incorrect?
questions.explanation: The superficial ring is a gap in external oblique aponeurosis; internal spermatic fascia comes from transversalis fascia at the deep ring, not the superficial ring.
options: It is a perforation in the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle
Its greatest width lies above and medial to the pubic tubercle
It is strengthened posteriorly by the conjoint tendon
The internal spermatic fascia is attached to its margins
In males, it allows passage of the spermatic cord and the ilioinguinal nerve

questions.text: 79- conjoint tendon is supplied by
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon combines the lower internal oblique and transversus abdominis aponeuroses. Its L1 nerve supply is associated with the ilioinguinal nerve, which is important during inguinal hernia surgery.

questions.text: 98- internal spermatic fascia derived from
questions.explanation: The internal spermatic fascia is a continuation of transversalis fascia pulled through the deep inguinal ring by the descending testis.

questions.text: Describe boundaries of Hasselbach triangle and its clinical importance
questions.explanation: Hesselbach triangle is bounded by rectus laterally, inferior epigastric vessels laterally, and inguinal ligament inferiorly; direct hernias protrude through its weak floor.
questions.modelAnswer: Medial: lateral rectus-abdominis border; lateral: inferior epigastric artery; inferior: inguinal ligament. Floor: transversalis fascia behind conjoint tendon. Direct inguinal hernia protrudes through this triangle, particularly its weaker lateral part.

questions.text: 55. All the following structures are present in the inguinal canal in the male except:
questions.explanation: The deep circumflex iliac artery runs along the iliac crest and does not enter the spermatic cord; cord contents include testicular vessels, vas deferens, and genital branch of genitofemoral nerve.
options: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve

questions.text: 82. The conjoint tendon (falx ingunalis) is formed by the:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon (inguinal falx) reinforces the medial posterior canal wall and is formed by the aponeuroses of internal oblique and transversus abdominis.
options: Transverse abdominis muscle or its aponeurosis
Internal abdominal oblique muscle or its aponeurosis

questions.text: 41. The following statements are correct regarding and inguinal hernia except:
questions.explanation: Indirect hernias enter lateral to the inferior epigastric artery at the deep ring; lacunar ligament can strangulate a femoral hernia, not an indirect inguinal sac.
options: The inferior epigastric artery lies medial to the neck of an indirect inguinal hernia
An inguinal hernia is more common than a femoral hernia in females
A direct inguinal hernia is more common in elderly men than in boys
The opening of the sac of a direct inguinal hernia is wide
The contents of an indirect inguinal hernia may be strangulated against the lacunar ligament

questions.text:
Fusion of the inferior fibers of the internal oblique and tranversus abdominis muscle result in a broad lamina which
inserts into the pubic crest. This lamina is the:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is the fused aponeurotic contribution of internal oblique and transversus abdominis to the pubic crest and pecten.

questions.text: 70- Regarding deep inguinal ring Select the incorrect statement
questions.explanation: The deep ring is an opening in transversalis fascia for the spermatic cord or round ligament; the ilioinguinal nerve enters the canal by piercing internal oblique and exits the superficial ring.
options: lies 1/2 inch above mid inguinal point
its margins gives origin of internal spermatic fascia

questions.text:
Question 23:A 40-year-old man discovered a swelling in his right grion that bulges
out on coughing. His doctor noticed that the swelling did not reach the scrotum. He
also noticed and old appendicectomy scar. He told the patient that a fault in the
appendicectomy might have caused his grion swelling.
questions.explanation: A bulge that stays above the ligament and does not reach the scrotum supports a direct hernia through weakened posterior wall. Injury to L1 iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal nerves can weaken abdominal muscle support.

subQuestions.text: a. From your anatomical knowledge, which type of inguinal hernia the patient is having? Explain the reason for your diagnosis.
subQuestions.explanation: The swelling above the inguinal ligament that does not descend into the scrotum is consistent with a direct hernia through the weakened medial posterior wall; the old scar alone does not establish causation.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Direct inguinal hernia → Because it bulges by pushing the fascia trans; but never
descends to the scrotum.

subQuestions.text: b. What had probably been injured during the appendicectomy? How could it lead to this hernia?
subQuestions.explanation: The appendicectomy incision may have injured iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal nerves supplying internal oblique and transversus abdominis. Weakening these muscles can reduce support of the posterior inguinal canal wall and favor a groin hernia.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
The iliohypogastric& the ilioinginal nerves (L1). → As they supply the internal
oblique & the transversus abdominis muscles that form the conjoint tendon (The
strongest part of the posterior wall of inguinal canal support the weak medial
part of it

questions.text: 79. Which layer of the spermatic cord is derived from the internal oblique muscle of the abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: Internal oblique contributes cremasteric muscle and fascia around the cord; external oblique gives external spermatic fascia and transversalis fascia gives internal spermatic fascia.

questions.text: 16. A direct inguinal hernia:
questions.explanation: Direct hernias protrude through the medial posterior inguinal wall, so they lie medial to the inferior epigastric vessels rather than passing through the deep ring.
options: Lies inferior to the inguinal ligament.
Lies lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.
Lies medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.

questions.text: 45. Nerve passing through the superficial inguinal ring:
questions.explanation: The ilioinguinal nerve traverses the inguinal canal and exits through the superficial ring; it does not enter through the deep ring.

questions.text: 96. Select the one best answer:
questions.explanation: The canal’s lateral opening is the superficial ring, a defect in external oblique aponeurosis; the deep ring is in transversalis fascia.
options: The superior epigasrtic artery is a branch of the external iliac artery
The anterior portion of the rectus sheath is formed by the aponeurosis of the external abdominal oblique and transverses abdominis muscle
The inguinal canal terminates at the superficial inguinal ring ( a defect in the external abdominal oblique muscle)
The conjoint tendon consists of lower fibers of the external abdominal muscle and the inguinal ligament
The internal spermatic fascia is derived from the internal oblique muscle

questions.text: 4. A structure that shares in the formation of the anterior wall, posterior wall & roof of the inguinal canal is the:
questions.explanation: Internal oblique contributes to the anterior wall, roof, and posterior wall of the canal, especially as its fibers arch and join the conjoint tendon medially.

questions.text: 44. As regards the deep inguinal ring all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The deep inguinal ring is lateral to the inferior epigastric artery. A ring medial to those vessels would not be the normal entry for an indirect hernia.
options: Lies medial to inferior epigastric artery.
It is present in the fascia transversalis.
Lies about half an inch above the midinguinal point.
Its margin gives attachment to internal spermatic fascia.

questions.text: 53. In the female, the inguinal canal contains the following structures except the:
questions.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery lies next to the deep ring but is not a content of the female canal; the round ligament and ilioinguinal nerve do pass through.
options: Lymph vessels from the fundus of the uterus

questions.text: 78- cremasteric muscle is supplied by
questions.explanation: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve carries the motor limb of the cremasteric reflex; the ilioinguinal nerve supplies nearby skin sensation.

questions.text: Describe boundaries of inguinal canal and structures passing through it
questions.explanation: The canal is an oblique passage with external oblique aponeurosis anteriorly, transversalis fascia posteriorly, inguinal ligament as its floor, and arching internal oblique/transversus fibers as its roof. Its contents are spermatic cord (or round ligament) and ilioinguinal nerve.
questions.modelAnswer: Anterior wall: external oblique aponeurosis throughout, internal oblique in lateral third. Posterior wall: transversalis fascia throughout, conjoint tendon in medial half and reflected inguinal ligament in medial fourth. Roof: lower arched fleshy internal-oblique fibres. Floor: concave inguinal ligament throughout and lacunar ligament medially. Contents: spermatic cord in male or uterine round ligament in female, and ilioinguinal nerve entering by piercing internal oblique and leaving through superficial ring.

questions.text: 77- which of the following structures has tripple relation with inguinal canal
questions.explanation: Internal oblique contributes to the anterior wall, roof, and floor of the canal, giving it relationships on three sides.

questions.text: 67. Which of the following structures of the spermatic cord is derived from the internal oblique muscle?
questions.explanation: The cremaster muscle and fascia are derived from internal oblique; external oblique contributes the external spermatic fascia, while transversalis fascia forms the internal spermatic fascia.

questions.text: 51. The following structures form the walls of the inguinal canal except the:
questions.explanation: The inguinal canal's floor is the inguinal ligament, while its anterior and posterior walls are formed chiefly by external oblique aponeurosis and transversalis fascia. The lacunar ligament is chiefly a boundary of the femoral ring.

questions.text: 30. T lacunar ligament:
questions.explanation: The lacunar ligament forms the medial boundary of the femoral ring; its sharp free edge is clinically relevant because femoral hernias can be strangulated there.
options: Part of the posterior wall of the rectus sheath
Not continuous with the inguinal ligament
An important medial relation to the femoral ring of the femoral sheath
Attached to the inferior ramus of the pubis

questions.text: 54. The deep inguinal ring is an opening in the:
questions.explanation: The deep inguinal ring is a defect in transversalis fascia, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, through which the spermatic cord or round ligament enters the canal.

questions.text: 68- deep inguinal ring is an opening into
questions.explanation: The deep inguinal ring is an opening in transversalis fascia, through which indirect hernias enter the canal.

questions.text: 74- reflected ligament belongs to
questions.explanation: The reflected inguinal ligament is a medial extension of external oblique aponeurotic fibers that curve back toward the linea alba.

questions.text: 19. Which one of the following muscles shares in 3 boundaries of inguinal canal?
questions.explanation: Internal oblique contributes fibers to the anterior wall, roof, and floor, so it shares in three canal boundaries.

questions.text: 37. Regarding the inguinal canal, choose one correct statement:
questions.explanation: The ilioinguinal nerve enters the canal through the abdominal wall and exits the superficial ring; it does not enter via the deep ring with the spermatic cord.
options: Its posterior wall is formed by the transversus abdominis muscle.
A direct inguinal hernia passes through the deep ring of the canal.
Its roof is formed by the fascia transversalis.
Its anterior wall is formed by the conjoint tendon.

questions.text: 28. The falx inguinalis (conjoint tendon) is made up of contributions from:
questions.explanation: Internal oblique and transversus abdominis aponeuroses unite medially as the conjoint tendon, supporting the posterior wall near the superficial ring.
options: The internal oblique and transversus abdominis.
The internal oblique and external oblique.
The transversus abdominis and external oblique.
All of the above named muscles.
None of the above named muscles.

questions.text:
Question 17: A 75 year old man with chronic cough noticed that a bulge was
developing in his left groin. On examination, an elongated swelling was seen above
the medial end of the left inguinal ligament. When the patient coughed, the swelling
enlarged but did not descend into the scrotum.
questions.explanation: An older man with chronic cough, an upper-medial groin bulge, and no scrotal descent fits a direct hernia; it passes through Hesselbach triangle. Its borders are rectus edge, inferior epigastric vessels, and inguinal ligament; posterior wall is transversalis fascia reinforced medially by conjoint tendon/reflected ligament.

subQuestions.text: a. What is the possible diagnosis of this swelling?
subQuestions.explanation: A medial groin bulge above the ligament that enlarges with cough but does not descend into the scrotum favors a direct hernia through Hesselbach’s triangle.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: The diagnosis is left direct inguinal hernia.

subQuestions.text: b. Give reasons for your diagnosis
subQuestions.explanation: Older age weakens the abdominal wall, while chronic cough repeatedly raises intra-abdominal pressure. Together they promote a direct inguinal hernia through the medial posterior wall, matching the groin bulge.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Reasons: Old age and chronic cough.

subQuestions.text: c. Mention the borders of the inguinal triangle
subQuestions.explanation: Hesselbach triangle is bounded medially by the lateral rectus border, laterally by inferior epigastric vessels, and inferiorly by inguinal ligament; direct hernias pass through it.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
The borders of inguinal triangle are:
1. Medially: lateral border of the rectus abdominis
2. Laterally: inferior epigastric artery
3. Inferiorly: inguinal ligament

subQuestions.text: d. Mention structures forming posterior wall of the inguinal canal
subQuestions.explanation: The posterior wall is transversalis fascia throughout, strengthened medially by the conjoint tendon; the prior case’s medial, non-scrotal bulge fits weakness of this wall.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Structures forming posterior wall of the inguinal canal:
1. Fascia transversals: along its whole length
2. Conjoint tendon: in its medial half
3. Reflected part of the inguinal ligament

questions.text: 83- medial wall of femoral ring
questions.explanation: The lacunar ligament forms the medial boundary of the femoral ring; the other boundaries are inguinal ligament anteriorly, pectineal ligament posteriorly, and femoral vein laterally.

questions.text: Which of the following structures shares in the posterior wall of inguinal canal:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon reinforces the medial posterior canal wall; transversalis fascia forms the wall throughout.

questions.text: 31. The cremaster muscle is innervated by which of the following nerves:
questions.explanation: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve supplies cremaster muscle and mediates the cremasteric reflex.

questions.text: 2. Describe the boundaries & the contents of the inguinal canal.
questions.explanation: The canal runs obliquely from deep ring to superficial ring; its anterior wall is external oblique aponeurosis (reinforced laterally by internal oblique), posterior wall transversalis fascia (reinforced medially by conjoint tendon), roof arching internal oblique/transversus fibers, and floor inguinal ligament. It transmits the spermatic cord or round ligament and ilioinguinal nerve.
questions.modelAnswer: Anterior wall: external oblique aponeurosis throughout, internal oblique in lateral third. Posterior wall: transversalis fascia throughout, conjoint tendon in medial half and reflected inguinal ligament in medial fourth. Roof: lower arched fleshy internal-oblique fibres. Floor: concave inguinal ligament throughout and lacunar ligament medially. Contents: spermatic cord in male or uterine round ligament in female, and ilioinguinal nerve entering by piercing internal oblique and leaving through superficial ring.

questions.text: 69- which of the following is Not component of posterior wall of inguinal canal
questions.explanation: The inguinal ligament forms the canal floor, not its posterior wall, which is transversalis fascia reinforced medially by conjoint tendon.

questions.text: 27. Fusion of the inferior fibres of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles result in a broad lamina which inserts into the public crest. This lamina is the:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is the medial aponeurotic fusion of internal oblique and transversus abdominis, strengthening the posterior wall near the pubic crest.

questions.text: 80. Which of the following statements about indirect inguinal hernia is false?
questions.explanation: An indirect hernia passes through the deep ring and lies above the inguinal ligament; a swelling below the ligament suggests femoral hernia. Indirect hernias may descend into the scrotum, but need not.
options: They enter the abdominal wall lateral to the inferior epigastric artery
They are more common in the males than in females
They follow the path of the inguinal canal
They often result from a patent processus vaginalis
They involve and outpouching of gut below the inguinal ligament

questions.text: 56. All of the following statements concerning the conjoint tendon are true except:
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is fused internal oblique/transversus aponeurosis attached to pubic crest and pecten; it reinforces the posterior wall but does not continue into the inguinal ligament.
options: It is attached to the pubic crest and the pectineal line
It is formed by the fusion of the aponeuroses of the transverses abdominis and internal oblique muscles
It is attached medially to the linea alba
It is continuous with the inguinal ligament
It may bulge forward in a direct inguinal hernia

questions.text: 41. The floor of the inguinal canal is made by the:
questions.explanation: The inguinal ligament forms the canal’s floor, supporting its contents as they travel from deep to superficial ring.

questions.text: 97- Regarding cremasteric muscle choose the incorrect statement
questions.explanation: The cremaster receives motor supply from the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1–L2), not ilioinguinal nerve; ilioinguinal fibers provide sensation to upper medial thigh and anterior scrotum.
options: its contraction leads to closure of superfecial inguinal ring

questions.text: ANA10: Structures in the right free border of lesser omentum include:
questions.explanation: In the free edge of the lesser omentum, bile duct is anterior/right, hepatic artery anterior/left, and portal vein posterior, so all listed positions are correct.
options: Bile duct anterior and to the right
Hepatic artery anterior and to the left

questions.text: 101-greater omentum doesn’t share in which wall of lesser sac
questions.explanation: The greater omentum contributes to the inferior wall of the lesser sac as its layers descend and fold back; the superior wall is mainly the caudate lobe and diaphragm.

questions.text: 5. A perforating gastric ulcer in the posterior wall of stomach may erode:
questions.explanation: The splenic artery runs along the posterior stomach bed, close to the posterior wall of the stomach. A chronic posterior ulcer can penetrate the lesser sac and erode it, causing severe hemorrhage.

questions.text: 53. Which one of the following structures is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: Ascending colon is secondarily retroperitoneal because its mesentery fuses to the posterior abdominal wall; liver, spleen, stomach, and transverse colon are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: 13. A finger in the epiploic foramen would be related superiorly to:
questions.explanation: The epiploic foramen is bounded superiorly by the caudate process of the liver, posteriorly by the IVC, anteriorly by the portal triad, and inferiorly by the first duodenum.

questions.text: ANA9: The following structures lie in the stomach bed, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The gallbladder is not part of the stomach bed; it lies against the liver. The stomach bed consists of structures posterior to the stomach across the lesser sac.

questions.text: 17. Which one of the following vessels is present in the gastrosplenic ligament?
questions.explanation: The left gastroepiploic artery runs in the gastrosplenic ligament from splenic artery to greater curvature; other gastroepiploic vessels follow different routes.

questions.text: The greater sac is divided into the supracolic and infracolic compartments by:
questions.explanation: The transverse mesocolon separates the supracolic compartment containing stomach and liver from the infracolic compartment containing most small bowel.

questions.text: 1. Mention the surface anatomy of the pylorus. How to identify the pylorus during surgery.
questions.explanation: The pylorus lies near the transpyloric plane at L1, slightly right of midline. In surgery its thick muscular ring and prepyloric vein help identify it when external landmarks are limited.
questions.modelAnswer: Pylorus lies half an inch right of the median plane at transpyloric plane (L1), anteriorly related to quadrate liver lobe. During surgery identify its palpable thick circular sphincter, pyloric constriction and prepyloric vein of Mayo crossing its front between right gastric and right gastroepiploic veins.

questions.text: 99. The posterior limit of the omental (epiploic) foramen is:
questions.explanation: The inferior vena cava forms the posterior boundary of the epiploic foramen; lesser-omental edge is anterior, caudate lobe superior, and duodenum inferior.
options: The free border of the lesser omentum

questions.text: Mention the relation between the abdominal organs and peritoneum.
questions.explanation: Peritoneal covering distinguishes intraperitoneal organs suspended by mesenteries from primarily retroperitoneal organs covered only anteriorly; some organs are secondarily retroperitoneal after fusion during development.
questions.modelAnswer:
•   The abdominal organs can be divided anatomically by their relationship to the peritoneum. There are two main groups: intraperitoneal and
retroperitoneal organs.
•    Intraperitoneal organs are enveloped by visceral peritoneum, which covers the organ both anteriorly and posteriorly. Examples include the
stomach, liver and spleen.
•    Retroperitoneal organs that peritoneum only covers their anterior surface:
1.  Suprarenal Gland
2.  Aorta/IVC
3.  Duodenum (except the proximal 2cm, the duodenal cap)
4.  Pancreas (except the tail)
5.  Ureters
6.  Colon (ascending and descending parts)
7.  Kidneys
8.  esophagus

questions.text: List the contents of the mesentery
questions.explanation: The mesentery is the double peritoneal fold suspending jejunum and ileum; its root carries their vessels, lymphatics, nodes, nerves, and connective tissue between the bowel and posterior wall.
questions.modelAnswer:
a.   Jejunum and ileum which run in the free border.
b.   Superior mesenteric blood vessels with sympathetic plexus of nerves.
c.   Jejunal and ileal branches of superior mesenteric artery and accompanying veins.
d.   Extra-peritoneal fatty tissue.
e.   Mesenteric lymph nodes and vessels (Lacteals).

questions.text: 51. The following are peritoneal ligaments EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Ligamentum teres is the fibrous remnant of the umbilical vein in the falciform ligament, not a peritoneal fold/ligament itself.

questions.text: 124- gastrosplenic ligament contains which of the following
questions.explanation: Short gastric vessels pass between the stomach fundus and spleen within the gastrosplenic ligament; the splenic vessels and pancreatic tail instead travel in the lienorenal ligament.

questions.text: 2. Which of the following is the posterior boundary of epiploic foramen?
questions.explanation: The inferior vena cava forms the posterior boundary of the epiploic foramen. The hepatoduodenal ligament with portal triad is anterior, caudate lobe superior, and first duodenal part inferior.

questions.text: 19. The parasympathetic nerve supply to the stomach is derived from:
questions.explanation: Vagal trunks provide the stomach’s parasympathetic supply, increasing motility and secretion; splanchnic nerves carry sympathetic fibers.

questions.text: 70. Which of the following organs is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: Most of the pancreas is secondarily retroperitoneal, while its tail reaches the splenic hilum within the lienorenal ligament; spleen, stomach, and jejunum are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: 133-greater omentum related to all wall of lesser sac Except
questions.explanation: The greater omentum contributes to the anterior and inferior boundaries of the lesser sac, but does not reach its superior boundary beneath the liver and diaphragm.

questions.text:
Question 14:In an operation for treatment of chronic gastric ulcer, it was found that
the posterior wall of the patient's stomach was stuck to his posterior abdominal wall.
questions.explanation: A chronic posterior gastric ulcer can adhere to the stomach bed—pancreas, diaphragm, transverse mesocolon, left kidney/suprarenal and spleen—and erode the splenic artery. Gastric supply follows right/left gastric, right/left gastroepiploic, and short gastric arteries.

subQuestions.text: a. Which structures lie behind the stomach and can be involved in the disease?
subQuestions.explanation: The posterior stomach rests on the stomach bed across the lesser sac, including pancreas, left kidney and suprarenal gland, diaphragm, spleen, and transverse mesocolon; adhesions can involve these structures.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
The stomach bed (left kidney and left suprarenal gland, ant surface of pancreas, left
crus of diaphragm, transverse mesocolon)

subQuestions.text: b. Name a large artery that runs behind the stomach and maybe eroded by the chronic ulcer?
subQuestions.explanation: The splenic artery courses tortuously along the upper border of the pancreas behind the stomach. A posterior gastric ulcer may erode it through the stomach bed.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: The artery is splenic artery from the coeliac trunk

subQuestions.text: c. Enumerate the arteries which supply the stomach?
subQuestions.explanation: The stomach is supplied by right/left gastric along the lesser curve, right/left gastroepiploic along the greater curve, and short gastric arteries to the fundus.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Arteries supply the stomach: Left and right gastric, left and right gastroepiploic &
short gastric .

questions.text: 49. The following structures form anterior wall of lesser sac EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The quadrate lobe is not a boundary of the lesser sac; superiorly, the caudate lobe and diaphragm bound it. The anterior wall includes the lesser omentum, stomach, and anterior layers of greater omentum.

questions.text: 123- Regarding stomach choose the incorrect statement
questions.explanation: The pylorus lies on the transpyloric plane to the right of the midline, not to the left. The stomach's position varies with posture and filling, but this landmark is used clinically.
options: its fundus is mainly supplied by short gastric vessels
separated from structures of stomach bed by lesser sac
its anterosuperior surface is related to anteriorabdominal wall
its pyloric end lies at level of transpyloric plane Lt to mid line

questions.text: 1. Enumerate peritoneal folds of stomach & mention its embryological origin.
questions.explanation: The stomach’s lesser omentum derives from ventral mesogastrium; greater omentum and gastrosplenic/gastrophrenic folds derive from dorsal mesogastrium.
questions.modelAnswer: Lesser omentum derives from ventral mesogastrium; greater omentum, gastrophrenic ligament and gastrosplenic ligament derive from dorsal mesogastrium.

questions.text: 143- gastrosplenic ligament contains
questions.explanation: The left gastroepiploic artery runs from splenic artery branches through the gastrosplenic ligament along the stomach’s greater curvature.

questions.text: 145- which is Not content within lienorenal ligament
questions.explanation: The lienorenal ligament carries splenic vessels and the pancreatic tail; the gastrosplenic carries short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels. The gastroduodenal artery runs outside these ligaments.

questions.text: 12. Lymphatics from the fundus of the stomach drain into the:
questions.explanation: Fundic lymph follows short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels toward pancreaticosplenic nodes, rather than pyloric or hepatic nodes.

questions.text: 21. The gastrosplenic ligament contains the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic tail lies in the lienorenal ligament beside splenic vessels, not in the gastrosplenic ligament, which carries short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels.

questions.text: GIVE A SHORT NOTE ON THE GREATER SAC.
questions.explanation: The greater sac is the main peritoneal cavity, extending from diaphragm into the pelvis. The transverse mesocolon divides it into supracolic and infracolic compartments.
questions.modelAnswer:
•   The greater sac extends from the diaphragm to the pelvic cavity.
•       It is divided into the supracolic and infracolic compartments by the transverse mesocolon.
•    The supracolic compartment is found superior to the transverse mesocolon, and contains the liver, stomach and spleen.
•   The infracolic compartment is inferior to the transverse mesocolon.
•    Looking from the anterior aspect, it is divided by the root of the mesentery of the small intestine into the right and left infracolic spaces.
•   The infracolic compartment contains the small intestine, ascending colon and descending colon.

questions.text: 128- Efferent lymphatics from stomach fundus drains directly into
questions.explanation: Fundal lymphatics follow short gastric and left gastroepiploic routes to pancreaticosplenic nodes.

questions.text: Enumerate structures pass in the right free border of the lesser omentum?
questions.explanation: The right free margin of the lesser omentum encloses the portal triad: bile duct to the right, proper hepatic artery to the left, and portal vein posteriorly.
questions.modelAnswer:
1- Bile duct (anterior to the right)
2- Hepatic artery (anterior to the left)
3-  Portal vein (posteriorly)

questions.text: 28. The anterior end of the normal spleen reaches the:
questions.explanation: In the normal spleen, its anterior end reaches approximately the midaxillary line along the tenth rib. A normal spleen is not palpable below the costal margin.

questions.text: 24. Which one of the following structures does not share in the formation of the stomach bed?
questions.explanation: The stomach bed includes diaphragm, transverse mesocolon, pancreas, left kidney/suprarenal and spleen; the right kidney is not behind the stomach.
options: Upper part of the front of right kidney.

questions.text: 21. All statements about transverse mesocolon are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The transverse mesocolon divides the infracolic space into right and left compartments; it does not divide the greater sac into supracolic and infracolic regions.
options: Is attached to anterior border of pancreas.
Is adherent to back of greater omentum.
Contains anastomotic branches between superior and inferior mesenteric arteries.
Divides the greater sac into right and left infracolic compartments.

questions.text: 47. One of the following structures is completely invested by peritoneum:
questions.explanation: The sigmoid colon is mobile and invested by peritoneum, suspended by its sigmoid mesocolon. Most retroperitoneal colon segments are fixed secondarily and not completely covered.

questions.text: 48. Which of the following structures is considered to be retroperitoneal:
questions.explanation: Most of the duodenum is secondarily retroperitoneal after its mesentery fuses with the posterior wall; only the proximal first part is mobile.

questions.text: 12. Which boundary of the lesser sac DOES NOT include the greater omentum?
questions.explanation: The greater omentum hangs below the stomach, contributing to the lesser sac’s inferior boundary; it does not form the superior boundary.

questions.text: 135- posterior wall of lesser sac Not include
questions.explanation: The lesser omentum is anterior to the lesser sac; the posterior wall is formed by peritoneum over the pancreas, kidneys, and other stomach-bed structures.

questions.text: Which of the following organs is considered a retroperitoneal organ:
questions.explanation: Kidney is retroperitoneal, lying behind parietal peritoneum; stomach, spleen, and small intestine are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: 102. Which of the following is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: The head of pancreas is secondarily retroperitoneal, fixed against the posterior abdominal wall; the spleen, stomach, jejunum, and transverse colon are intraperitoneal.

questions.text:
A 39-year-old female is brought to the emergency room after a motor vehicle collision. CT of abdomen reveals a
hematoma of a retroperitoneal origin. Injury of which of the following organs is responsible for such a condition?
questions.explanation: The pancreas is mostly secondarily retroperitoneal, so trauma can cause bleeding into the retroperitoneum. Spleen, stomach, liver, and transverse colon are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: What are contents of lesser omentum
questions.explanation: The lesser omentum carries gastric vessels/nodes and its free right edge contains the portal triad: bile duct anterior-right, hepatic artery anterior-left, portal vein posterior.
questions.modelAnswer: Right and left gastric vessels with accompanying lymph nodes near lesser curvature; portal vein posteriorly, bile duct anterior/right and hepatic artery anterior/left in free right margin; autonomic nerves, lymphatics and extraperitoneal fat.

questions.text: 8. A posterior relation of the epiploic foramen is the:
questions.explanation: The IVC lies directly posterior to the epiploic foramen, with the portal triad anterior and caudate lobe superior.

questions.text: 110-when you put your index finger in the winslow foramen Which structure is felt just anterior to your finger
questions.explanation: The portal triad lies in the hepatoduodenal ligament immediately anterior to a finger passed through the epiploic foramen; the IVC is posterior to the finger.

questions.text: 134- all the following structures are completly covered by peritoneum Except
questions.explanation: Most of the duodenum is secondarily retroperitoneal; transverse colon, ileum, and appendix are covered by visceral peritoneum.

questions.text: 12. Which of the following structures is NOT present within the lesser omentum?
questions.explanation: The IVC is posterior to the foramen and outside the lesser omentum; the hepatoduodenal ligament carries portal vein, bile duct, hepatic artery, and lymphatics.

questions.text: Q1. List three Retroperitoneal organs
questions.explanation: Kidneys, suprarenal glands, and ureters lie behind the peritoneum. This position distinguishes them from mobile intraperitoneal viscera such as spleen and stomach.
questions.modelAnswer: Kidneys, suprarenal glands and ureters.

questions.text: 132- when the surgeon puts his index finger into winslow forearm which structure could be felt just superior to his finger
questions.explanation: The caudate lobe/process lies superior to the epiploic foramen; the IVC is posterior, lesser omentum anterior, and first duodenal part inferior.

questions.text: 7. The ligament that contains the splenic artery is:
questions.explanation: The splenic artery travels with the pancreatic tail in the lienorenal ligament, which spans between spleen and left kidney.

questions.text: 15. The main ligament supporting the spleen is the:
questions.explanation: The phrenicocolic ligament supports the spleen's lower pole like a shelf. The splenorenal ligament attaches the hilum and carries splenic vessels and pancreatic tail.

questions.text: 37. The following statements regarding the peritoneum are incorrect except:
questions.explanation: Anterior abdominal-wall parietal peritoneum has somatic innervation from lower thoracic and L1 nerves, so it is sharply pain-sensitive; visceral peritoneum follows autonomic afferents.
options: The parietal peritoneum is only sensitive to stretch
The parietal peritoneum lining the anterior abdominal wall is innervated by the lower six thoracic and the first lumbar spinal nerves
The visceral peritoneum is innervated by the posterior primary rami of the twelfth thoracic and the lumbar spinal nerves
The visceral peritoneum is sensitive to pain, temperature and touch
The peritoneum lining the lesser sac has no nerve supply

questions.text: 22. The lienorenal ligament contains:
questions.explanation: The lienorenal ligament carries splenic vessels and the pancreatic tail, with surrounding extraperitoneal tissue, as these structures pass toward the splenic hilum.

questions.text: 50. The structures that bound the epiploic foramen include all the followings EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The hepatic vein is not a boundary of the epiploic foramen. Its four borders are portal triad anteriorly, IVC posteriorly, caudate lobe superiorly, and first duodenum inferiorly.

questions.text: What are contents of mesentery
questions.explanation: The mesentery suspends jejunum and ileum and carries SMA/SMV branches, autonomic plexus, lymphatics, nodes, and fat.
questions.modelAnswer: Jejunum/ileum in free margin, superior mesenteric vessels with sympathetic plexus, jejunal/ileal branches and veins, extraperitoneal fat, mesenteric nodes and lymph vessels.

questions.text: 17. The following statements concerning the pyloric sphincter are correct except:
questions.explanation: The pylorus is typically at the transpyloric plane near L1, not L3; the marked level can shift with posture and gastric filling.
options: It receives its motor innervation from the sympathetic autonomic nerves
It lies on the level of the third lumbar vertebrae
It is inhibited by the impulses passing down the vagus nerve
It is formed by a thickening of the circular layer of smooth muscle in the stomach wall
The cavity of the pylorus is called the pyloric canal

questions.text: 184-Which of the following structures is often referred to as the “abdominal policeman”
questions.explanation: The greater omentum can adhere to inflamed areas and wall them off, limiting spread of infection; this protective behavior earned it the name “abdominal policeman.”

questions.text: 48. The lesser sac separates the back of the stomach from:
questions.explanation: The left crus forms part of the stomach bed behind the stomach; the lesser sac separates them, while right kidney and IVC lie farther right.

questions.text: Boundaries of epiploic foramen and structures passing through
questions.explanation: The epiploic foramen is the passage between sacs; its portal-triad-containing anterior boundary, IVC posterior boundary, caudate lobe above, and duodenum below are key surgical landmarks.
questions.modelAnswer: Epiploic foramen connects greater and lesser sacs: anteriorly free lesser-omental margin (portal vein, bile duct and hepatic artery); posteriorly IVC; superiorly caudate liver process; inferiorly first duodenal part. It transmits communication between the sacs; listed portal triad lies in its anterior boundary.

questions.text: 26. Which of the following is NOT in contact with the spleen?
questions.explanation: The spleen contacts the stomach, left kidney, left colic flexure, and diaphragm, but not the liver, which lies on the right side of the upper abdomen.

questions.text: Rational, peritonitis is more common in females
questions.explanation: The female peritoneal cavity communicates with the exterior through uterine tubes, uterus, and vagina, allowing ascending infection; the male cavity is closed.
questions.modelAnswer: Female peritoneal cavity communicates externally through uterine tubes, uterus and vagina; male cavity is closed. This communication permits ascending infection into the peritoneum.

questions.text: ANA9: The following structures lie in the stomach bed, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The stomach bed includes the left kidney, pancreas, spleen, and diaphragm across the lesser sac; the gallbladder lies anteriorly beneath the liver, not behind the stomach.

questions.text: 2. List the contents of the lesser omentum.
questions.explanation: The lesser omentum's free right edge contains the portal triad: bile duct anterior-right, proper hepatic artery anterior-left, and portal vein posterior. Gastric vessels run along its lesser-curvature attachment.
questions.modelAnswer: Right and left gastric vessels with accompanying lymph nodes near lesser curvature; portal vein posteriorly, bile duct anterior/right and hepatic artery anterior/left in free right margin; autonomic nerves, lymphatics and extraperitoneal fat.

questions.text: 25. Which of the following is NOT related to the posterior wall of the stomach:
questions.explanation: The left gastric artery runs along the lesser curvature rather than behind the stomach; the diaphragm, splenic artery, left kidney, and suprarenal gland are posterior relations.

questions.text: Boundaries of lesser sac
questions.explanation: The lesser sac lies behind the stomach and lesser omentum and in front of the pancreas and posterior stomach bed. It communicates with the greater sac through the epiploic foramen.
questions.modelAnswer: Anterior (below upward): anterior two greater-omental layers; posterior stomach/first duodenal inch peritoneum; lesser omentum; caudate liver. Posterior: posterior two greater-omental layers and peritoneum over stomach bed. Upper: posterior lesser-omental reflection onto diaphragm. Lower: inferior greater-omental margin. Left: left greater-omental margin, gastrosplenic and lienorenal ligaments above. Right: right greater-omental margin below; epiploic foramen above first duodenum.

questions.text: 18. Which of the following statements, concerning the lesser omentum, is true?
questions.explanation: The common bile duct runs in the free right edge of the lesser omentum with hepatic artery and portal vein; the other listed claims misplace attachments or contents.
options: It extends from greater curvature of stomach to duodenum.
The common bile duct runs in its free edge.
It contains the anterior and posterior vagal trunk.

questions.text: 18. The following structures form the boundaries of the entrance into the lesser sac (epiploic foramen) except:
questions.explanation: The epiploic foramen’s superior boundary is the caudate process, not the quadrate lobe; the other listed structures form anterior, posterior, and inferior boundaries.
options: The first part of the duodenum

questions.text: Mention structures form the stomach bed
questions.explanation: The stomach bed comprises diaphragm, spleen, left kidney and suprarenal gland, pancreas, splenic artery, and transverse mesocolon/colon, separated from the stomach chiefly by the lesser sac.
questions.modelAnswer: Left crus of diaphragm, part of left kidney, left suprarenal gland, splenic artery, anterior pancreas, transverse mesocolon and transverse colon if mesocolon is short; separated by lesser sac. Spleen is also included in the book list but separated by greater-sac peritoneum.

questions.text: 2. The impression located below the hilum of the spleen is:
questions.explanation: The renal impression lies below the splenic hilum where the spleen rests against the left kidney; the gastric impression is medial and superior.

questions.text: 29. Regarding the spleen, all the following statements are correct EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The spleen lies left of the stomach and is not a posterior relation of the liver; its gastric, diaphragmatic, renal, and colic impressions define its neighboring organs.
options: The diaphragm separates it from the lung and 9th-11th ribs.
It forms posterior relation to the liver.
Anteriorly it is in relation to the fundus of the stomach.
The hilum of the spleen is related to the tail of the pancreas.
It is supplied by the splenic artery from the celiac trunk.

questions.text: 23. Regarding the stomach, select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: The stomach lies anterior to the spleen, separated by the lesser sac and associated peritoneal folds. Its left-sided fundus is adjacent to the spleen rather than behind it.
options: Is supplied posteriorly mainly by left vagus nerve.
Its right border is known as its greater curvature.
Its venous drainage passes equally to portal and systemic venous systems.
It lies anterior to the spleen.
Its cardiac orifice is closely related to the aorta.

questions.text: 146- pyloric end of stomach located at which level
questions.explanation: The pylorus is conventionally placed at the transpyloric plane, around L1. Its level varies with posture and stomach filling.

questions.text: 3. List the components of the stomach bed.
questions.explanation: The stomach bed is a set of posterior relations separated from the stomach by the lesser sac, chiefly pancreas, left kidney and suprarenal gland, diaphragm, splenic artery, and transverse mesocolon.
questions.modelAnswer: Left crus of diaphragm, part of left kidney, left suprarenal gland, splenic artery, anterior pancreas, transverse mesocolon and transverse colon if mesocolon is short; separated by lesser sac. Spleen is also included in the book list but separated by greater-sac peritoneum.

questions.text: 22. Which of the following structures may be eroded by a perforating gastric ulcer on the posterior wall of the stomach?
questions.explanation: The splenic artery lies in the stomach bed behind the posterior stomach surface, so a posterior-wall ulcer may erode it and produce major hemorrhage.
options: The second part of the duodenum
The quadrate lobe of the liver

questions.text: 110. Which of the following statements regarding the abdomen is false?
questions.explanation: Falciform ligament develops from ventral mesogastrium; dorsal mesogastrium forms the greater omentum and related ligaments.
options: The falciform ligament is a dorsal mesentery
The bile duct enters the duodenum through the major duodenal papilla
The gastric arteries run parallel to the lesser curvature of the stomach
The epiploic foramen (of Winslow) is the opening into the lesser sac
The hepatic veins drain into the inferior vena cava

questions.text: 5. The inferior boundary of the epiploic foramen is:
questions.explanation: The first part of the duodenum lies immediately below the epiploic foramen and forms its inferior boundary.

questions.text: 6. Which of the following IS NOT related to the posterior surface of the stomach?
questions.explanation: The left gastric artery runs along the lesser curvature rather than forming a posterior-surface relation. The posterior stomach faces the lesser sac and the stomach bed.

questions.text: What are the boundaries of lesser sac?
questions.explanation: The lesser sac lies behind the stomach, with greater-omental layers contributing to its lower walls and stomach-bed structures behind.
questions.modelAnswer:
Anterior wall:
Upper part
1.  Lesser omentum.
2.  Caudate lobe of the liver.
3.  Peritoneum covering the posterior surface of stomach & 1st inch of duodenum.
lower part :
Anterior 2 layers of greater omentum.

Posterior wall:
Upper part formed of structures forming the stomach bed.
Lower part formed by the posterior 2 layers of greater omentum

Upper border:
Formed by reflection of peritoneum of the posterior layer of lesser omentum on to the diaphragm.

Lower border:
Formed by the inferior margin of the greater omentum.

Left border:
Formed by the left margin of greater omentum & its upper part is formed by gastro-splenic & lienorenal ligaments.

Right border:
Formed by reflection of peritoneum from the back of the 1st part of duodenum on to the front of neck of pancreas.

questions.text: 68. Which of the following organs does not receive its blood supply from the celiac trunk?
questions.explanation: Jejunum is supplied by jejunal branches of the superior mesenteric artery; the celiac trunk supplies foregut organs such as stomach, liver, spleen, and gallbladder.

questions.text: 49. The following statements regarding the celiac plexus are true except :
questions.explanation: The celiac plexus surrounds the celiac trunk and contains sympathetic and parasympathetic fibers. Vagal preganglionics pass through without synapsing until they reach enteric ganglia in target organs.
options: The celiac plexus is not a purely sympathetic plexus
The celiac plexus does not surround the celiac artery
The celiac ganglia are made of nerve cell bodies and nerve fibers
Parasympathetic preganglionic fibers pass through the plexus, generally synapsing with postganglionic neurons within the walls of the organs they innervate
