Sympathetic preganglionic fibers to the celiac plexus originate from the thoracic spinal segments and travel in thoracic splanchnic nerves

questions.text: 165- during splenectomy which structure is liable to be injured while ligature of splenic artery
questions.explanation: The pancreatic tail reaches the splenic hilum within the lienorenal ligament, placing it at risk during splenic-vessel ligation.

questions.text: 131- Regarding arteries of stomach select the correct statement
questions.explanation: Short gastric arteries from the splenic artery supply the fundus; left and right gastric arteries run along the lesser curvature, while gastroepiploic vessels follow the greater curvature.
options: gastroepiploic vessles runs along lesser curveture
fundus of stomach is supplied by short gastric vessles
splenic artery separated from stomach by greater sac
Rt gastroepiploic artery is abranch from splenic artery

questions.text: 16–20. Match the viscus in the left column with its arterial blood source in the right column:
questions.explanation: These arterial matches follow embryologic territories: appendix and third duodenum receive SMA supply; sigmoid colon receives IMA; pancreatic body receives splenic branches from the celiac trunk; gallbladder receives cystic artery from the hepatic system.

subQuestions.text: Vermiform appendix.
subQuestions.explanation: The vermiform appendix is supplied through the ileocolic branch of the superior mesenteric artery, reflecting its midgut origin.

subQuestions.text: 3rd part of duodenum.
subQuestions.explanation: The third part of the duodenum is supplied by inferior pancreaticoduodenal branches of the superior mesenteric artery, reflecting its midgut blood supply.

subQuestions.text: Sigmoid colon.
subQuestions.explanation: The sigmoid colon is hindgut-derived and supplied by sigmoid branches of the inferior mesenteric artery. The celiac trunk supplies foregut organs, while SMA supplies midgut.

subQuestions.text: Body of pancreas.
subQuestions.explanation: The body of pancreas receives much of its arterial supply from pancreatic branches of the splenic artery, a celiac trunk branch.

subQuestions.text: Gall bladder.
subQuestions.explanation: The gallbladder receives its cystic artery from the right hepatic artery, usually a branch of the common hepatic artery from the celiac trunk.

questions.text: 45. A direct branch of the common hepatic artery is:
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery is a direct branch of the common hepatic artery and descends behind the first part of the duodenum before dividing into key branches.

questions.text: 162- which of the following arteries is Not abranch from hepatic artery
questions.explanation: Short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery; right gastric, supraduodenal, and gastroduodenal branches arise from hepatic arterial routes.

questions.text: 76. Which of the following is false about the normal pattern of arterial blood supply to the stomach:
questions.explanation: The pylorus receives supply from the right gastric and gastroduodenal arteries; the left gastric chiefly supplies the lesser curvature and does not directly supply the pylorus.

questions.text: 50. As regards the blood supply of the stomach, choose the correct statement:
questions.explanation: Short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery and pass through the gastrosplenic ligament to the fundus; left and right gastric arteries run along the lesser curvature.
options: It is derived entirely from superior mesenteric artery.
The gastroepiploic arteries supply the lesser curvature.
The right gastric artery supplies the cardiac end.
The left gastroepiploic artery arises directly from the coeliac trunk.
The short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery.

questions.text: 1. Which artery of stomach is directly derived from the coeliac trunk?
questions.explanation: The left gastric artery arises directly from the celiac trunk and supplies the lesser curvature; most other gastric arteries branch from hepatic or splenic branches.

questions.text: 127- We can say hepatic artery proper after the exit of which artery
questions.explanation: The common hepatic artery becomes the proper hepatic artery after giving off the gastroduodenal artery; right gastric branches may arise variably.

questions.text: 47. Which of the following arteries is NOT derived from the hepatic artery (either directly or from one of its branches):
questions.explanation: Short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery, a celiac trunk branch, rather than the hepatic artery tree. They supply the gastric fundus.

questions.text: 83. Which of the following supply the lesser curvature of the stomach?
questions.explanation: Right and left gastric arteries run along and anastomose on the lesser curvature; short gastric arteries supply the fundus and gastroepiploics the greater curve.

questions.text: 1–5. Match the structure in the left column with its arterial supply in the right column:
questions.explanation: The matches follow foregut–midgut–hindgut arterial territories: splenic artery to pancreas/body, left gastric to esophagus, short gastrics to fundus, middle colic to transverse colon, and superior rectal to upper anal canal.

questions.text: 42. The coeliac artery contributes to the blood supply of the following EXCEPT the:
questions.explanation: The third part of the duodenum is midgut-derived and receives inferior pancreaticoduodenal branches of the SMA. Celiac branches supply the foregut-derived proximal duodenum.

questions.text: 14. The term hepatic artery proper is given to hepatic artery after giving:
questions.explanation: The common hepatic artery becomes the hepatic artery proper after the gastroduodenal artery branches off; right gastric may arise later from the proper artery.

questions.text: 39. In a patient with cancer of the stomach who requires a total gastrectomy, the following arteries must be ligated except:
questions.explanation: Gastrectomy requires control of gastric arteries, but the common hepatic artery must remain patent because it supplies liver and biliary tree beyond the stomach.
options: The left and right gastroepiploic arteries

questions.text: 49. Regarding the coeliac trunk:
questions.explanation: The celiac trunk supplies the gallbladder indirectly through common/proper hepatic and usually right hepatic branches, which give rise to the cystic artery.
options: Arises from abdominal aorta at level of L2 vertebra.
Gives the right gastric artery as a direct branch.
Gives indirect supply to gall bladder.

questions.text: 16. Arterial supply to the fundus of the stomach is derived from:
questions.explanation: Short gastric arteries from the splenic artery reach the fundus through the gastrosplenic ligament, supplying the stomach’s dome.

questions.text: 79-The portion of the hepatic artery extending between the celiac trunk and gastroduodenal artery is known as
questions.explanation: The common hepatic artery is the segment from the celiac trunk to the gastroduodenal artery; beyond that branch point it is called proper hepatic artery.

questions.text: Enumerate the anterior and posterior relations of the neck of pancreas
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms immediately posterior to the pancreatic neck where the splenic and superior mesenteric veins unite. The pylorus and gastroduodenal artery lie anteriorly.
questions.modelAnswer: Anterior: pylorus; gastroduodenal artery passes in front of head–neck junction. Posterior: union of superior mesenteric and splenic veins forming portal vein.

questions.text: 129- artery that runs posterior to 1st part of dudenum
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery descends behind the first part of the duodenum, where a posterior ulcer can erode it and cause severe bleeding.

questions.text: 30. The vessel that crosses anterior to third part of duodenum is:
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric artery descends anterior to the third part of duodenum, creating a compression point in superior mesenteric artery syndrome.

questions.text: 27. During a splenectomy (removal of spleen), which of the following structures is most likely to be encountered:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic tail reaches the splenic hilum, so it is encountered during splenectomy and can be injured during hilar dissection. The other listed retroperitoneal structures are farther away.

questions.text: 121-All of the followings lie posterior to head of pancreas and its uncinate process except
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck, not behind the head or uncinate process; aorta, IVC, bile duct, and renal vessels are posterior relations.

questions.text: ANA12: A tumor in the tail of pancreas will affect which one of the following organs?
questions.explanation: The pancreatic tail reaches the splenic hilum in the lienorenal ligament, so a tail tumor can directly involve the spleen or its vessels.

questions.text: 37. Regarding the pancreas, all are true EXCEPT:

options: It lies transversely across the posterior abdominal wall.
Its secretion is drained by the main and accessory ducts.

It is related anteriorly to the greater sac of peritoneum.

questions.text: 38. The following structures lie behind head of pancreas or its uncinate process EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms behind the neck of pancreas rather than behind its head/uncinate process; the other listed vessels can lie posterior to those parts.

questions.text: 148- Regarding 1st part of dudenum select the wrong statement
questions.explanation: The second inch of the first duodenal part is fixed and posteriorly related to structures such as the IVC and portal triad, not the neck of pancreas.

its 1st inch is completely covered by peritoneum
its 2nd inch is related posterior to Neck of pancreas

questions.text: 31. The following statements about the first part of duodenum are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The first duodenal part lies anterior to the caudate lobe, not in direct relation to it; it forms the inferior boundary of the epiploic foramen and is crossed posteriorly by the gastroduodenal artery.
options: Ends at the neck of the gall bladder.
Lesser omentum is attached to its proximal half.
Forms the lower boundary of epiploic foramen.
It is related posteriorly to gastroduodenal artery.
Is related anteriorly to caudate lobe of the liver.

questions.text: 121. Which is incorrect regarding the pancreas:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic tail enters the lienorenal ligament at the splenic hilum; the gastrosplenic ligament carries short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels.

The congenital malformation known as annular pancreas arises because of malrotation of the ventral bud of the pancrease
It is supplied by the arterial blood via the celiac, superior mesenteric and splenic arteries
The tip of the tail lies in the gastrosplenic ligament

questions.text: ANA11: Which one of the following forms superior relation of the 2nd inch of the first part of the duodenum?
questions.explanation: The epiploic foramen lies just above the first part of the duodenum, making it a superior relation of that segment.

questions.text: 90. Regarding the pancreas:
questions.explanation: Most of the pancreas is secondarily retroperitoneal; the tail is mobile within the lienorenal ligament and is intraperitoneal. This explains the organ's otherwise fixed posterior position.
options: Exocrine secretions are released into the interstitial spaces
The pancreas is invested by a prominent and distinct connective tissue capsule
The pancreas is retroperitoneal except for the tail which is intraperitoneal
Centroaciner cells appear acidophilic when stained by routine hematoylin and eosin methods due to the high number of secretory vesicles

questions.text: 102-perforated dudenal ulcer could affect which of the following vessles
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery passes behind the first duodenal part, so a posterior penetrating ulcer can damage it.

questions.text: 26–30. Match the viscus in the left column with its related vessel in the right column:
questions.explanation: The left gastric artery supplies the lesser curvature, the right renal vessels lie behind the second duodenal part, and the SMV meets the splenic vein behind the pancreatic neck; the SMA relates to the uncinate process.

questions.text: 39. The neck of pancreas is related posteriorly to:
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, making it the key posterior relation and a surgical landmark.

questions.text: 15. Which of the following statements is (are) correct regarding the duodenum?
questions.explanation: The common bile duct opens into the descending second part at the major papilla; duodenal blood supply is shared by celiac and SMA branches.
options: The duodenum receives its entire blood supply from the superior mesenteric artery
The first part of the duodenum is completely retroperitoneal
The bile duct enters the second (vertical) portion of the duodenum
The lymph from the fourth part of the duodenum drains into the celiac nodes
The tip of the appendix cannot reach down into the pelvic cavity

questions.text: 23. A structure that lies anterior to the neck of pancreas is the following:
questions.explanation: The pylorus lies anterior to the pancreatic neck; posteriorly, the SMV and splenic vein unite to form the portal vein.

questions.text: 33. While passing behind the neck of the pancreas, the common bile duct is related posteriorly to:
questions.explanation: The IVC lies posterior to the distal common bile duct as it descends behind the first part of the duodenum and along the pancreatic head.

questions.text: 32. The following structures lie posterior to the first part of the duodenum EXCEPT the:
questions.explanation: The gallbladder lies anterior/superior to the first duodenal part; posterior relations include IVC, portal vein, bile duct, and gastroduodenal artery.

questions.text: 11. A perforating peptic ulcer in the 2nd inch of the duodenum may erode:
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery descends posterior to the first duodenal part, so posterior peptic ulcer erosion can cause major bleeding.

questions.text: 69. The common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct empty into the:
questions.explanation: The main pancreatic and common bile ducts unite at the hepatopancreatic ampulla and open at the major duodenal papilla in the second part of the duodenum.

questions.text: 8. The neck of the pancreas is related posteriorly to:
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms immediately behind the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.

questions.text: 9. The length of the duodenum is:
questions.explanation: The duodenum is about 25 cm (10 inches) long, extending from pylorus to the duodenojejunal flexure.

questions.text: 161- select the wrong statement regarding pancreas

its upper border related to splenic artery

questions.text: 3. Which part of the duodenum is related to superior mesenteric artery?

questions.text: 150- uncinate process of pancreas separate between

questions.text: 4. The 3rd part of the duodenum is related posteriorly to:

questions.text: 125- all the following structures are related posterior to 3rd part of dudenum Except
questions.explanation: The SMA crosses anterior to the third part of duodenum; it is not one of its posterior relations, unlike the aorta, IVC, and right psoas.

questions.text: 31. The vessel crossing posterior to the first part of duodenum is:
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery descends behind the first duodenal part, where it can be compressed or eroded by a penetrating ulcer.

questions.text: What are the bare areas of the duodenum?

It has 2 bare areas (the 1st one in the middle of its 2nd part formed by crossing of the transverse colon, while the 2nd one formed by crossing of

questions.text: 6–10. Match the structure in the left column with its matching vessel in the right column:
questions.explanation: The matches use fixed landmarks: portal triad occupies the lesser omentum edge, splenic artery tracks along pancreas, renal vessels relate to descending duodenum, and SMV joins splenic vein behind pancreatic neck.

questions.text: List/Enumerate the following: The anterior and posterior relations of the neck of pancreas (1mark)
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms immediately posterior to the neck when the superior mesenteric vein joins the splenic vein; the pylorus and gastroduodenal artery lie in front.
questions.modelAnswer: Anterior: pylorus of stomach; gastroduodenal artery descends in front of the head–neck junction. Posterior: superior mesenteric and splenic veins unite to form the portal vein.

questions.text: 40. The body of the pancreas lies in front of the following structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic body lies anterior to aorta, SMA, left psoas, and left suprarenal region, but not the lower L4 vertebra.

questions.text: 104. A posterior ulcer of the first part of the duodenum may penetrate the wall and erode an artery running behind it, causing severe internal haemorrhage. This artery is likely to be:
questions.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery lies behind the first part of the duodenum and is vulnerable to a posterior ulcer, explaining severe hemorrhage.

questions.text: 100. Indicate the correct statement:
questions.explanation: The uncinate process projects medially behind the SMA and SMV, which separate it from the pancreatic head. This relationship matters during pancreatic surgery.
options: The pancreas is located in the epigastric and right hypochondriac regions
The pancreas is divided into head, neck and tail
The uncinate process projects medially behind the superior mesenteric vessels
The posterior surface of the head of the pancreas is related to the left crus
The posterior aspect of the neck of the pancreas is covered with peritoneum and is adjacent to the pylorus

questions.text: 4. List the structures related to 1st part of duodenum.
questions.explanation: The first duodenal inch lies against liver and peritoneum anteriorly, lesser sac/pancreatic neck posteriorly, lesser omentum above, and greater omentum below. The second inch relates to gallbladder/liver, pancreatic head, and posterior portal structures including CBD/GDA.

Second inch: quadrate liver lobe and gallbladder neck anteriorly; portal vein, common bile duct and gastroduodenal artery anterior to IVC posteriorly; epiploic foramen superiorly and pancreatic head inferiorly.

questions.text: 41. The uncinate process of pancreas lies behind:
questions.explanation: The uncinate process hooks posterior to the superior mesenteric vessels, which pass between it and the pancreatic neck.

questions.text: 33. The posterior surface of the second part of the duodenum is related to all but which one of the following:
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric vessels cross anterior to the third part of the duodenum, not behind the second part. The posterior surface of D2 relates to kidney and major vessels.

questions.text: 123. The duodenum:
questions.explanation: The bile duct passes behind the first part of the duodenum before entering its second part; other options misstate the third-part relations, blood supply, folds, or peritoneal status.
options: Has the common bile duct passing posterior to its first part
Has posterior relationships in its third part with the inferior vena cava, abdominal aorta and the common bile duct
Receives artrial blood from the superior pancreaticoduodenal, inferior pancreaticoduodenal and inferior mesenteric artery

questions.text: 36. Third part of the duodenum crosses in front of the following Structures EXCEPT the:

questions.text: 126- Neck of pancrease is related posteriorly to
questions.explanation: The portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, explaining why it is vulnerable during neck dissection.

questions.text: 155- Which of the following arteries related posterior to 2nd inch of dudenum

questions.text: 34. Regarding the duodenum, select the correct answer:

questions.text: 60. The secondary palate is derived from:

questions.text: 16. Which of the following is a derivative of dorsal mesentery?
questions.explanation: Greater omentum develops from dorsal mesogastrium, while lesser omentum and falciform ligament arise from ventral mesogastrium.

questions.explanation: Greater omentum and the splenic ligaments derive from dorsal mesogastrium; the lesser omentum develops from ventral mesogastrium.

questions.text: 24. Regarding the foregut select an untrue statement:

It is connected to midgut by anterior intestinal portal.
It is supplied by superior mesenteric artery.

questions.explanation: The primary palate, including the premaxillary region, arises from the intermaxillary segment formed by fusion of medial nasal prominences.

questions.text: 31. The falciform ligament is derived from the:

2. Discuss the embryonic development of tongue.
questions.explanation: Tongue mucosa develops from multiple pharyngeal arches: the anterior two-thirds mainly from the first arch and posterior tongue from third/fourth arch swellings. Occipital myotomes form its muscles and carry hypoglossal innervation.
questions.modelAnswer: During week 4, anterior two thirds mucosa develops from the first pharyngeal arch: median tuberculum impar and two lateral lingual swellings, which overgrow it and unite in the midline. A lingulogingival groove deepens to free the tongue except at the frenulum. Posterior third develops from the cranial hypobranchial eminence involving the third arch after exclusion of the second-arch part; its caudal portion forms the epiglottis. The terminal sulcus separates the parts. Vallate papillae migrate forwards and retain glossopharyngeal supply; the posterior tongue/valleculae have vagal superior laryngeal supply. All intrinsic and extrinsic muscles except palatoglossus derive from migrating occipital myotomes and retain hypoglossal supply; palatoglossus derives from the sixth arch. Anomalies include bifid tip, ankyloglossia and microglossia/macrogIossia.

Question 5:A 22-year-old female developed cystic swelling undercover of the
anterior border of sternocleidomastoid muscle .

due to failure of obliteration of the cervical sinus. (it is branchial cyst and not

questions.text: 62- Regarding tongue development select the incorrect statement

questions.text: Enumerate three anomalies of the stomach development.

questions.explanation: The spleen arises in dorsal mesogastrium and remains connected to stomach and posterior wall by the gastrosplenic and lienorenal ligaments.

questions.text: 57. The mucosa of the posterior 1/3 of tongue develops from:
questions.explanation: The posterior third of the tongue develops mainly from the hypobranchial eminence contributed by the third pharyngeal arch; its mucosal sensation is chiefly glossopharyngeal.

questions.text: 157- structure that developed between 2 layers of ventral mesogastrium
questions.explanation: The liver bud grows into the ventral mesogastrium; its remnants include lesser omentum and falciform ligament.

questions.text: 28. The junction of the embryological foregut and midgut is:
questions.explanation: The foregut–midgut boundary is at the major duodenal papilla in the second part of the duodenum, where biliary entry marks the transition.
options: Half-way along the lesser curvature of the stomach.

questions.text:
Previous Essay Questions
3. Discuss the embryonic development of the palate.
questions.explanation: Palatal shelves elevate and fuse with each other, the primary palate, and nasal septum. Failure of these fusion steps produces cleft palate.
questions.modelAnswer: The primitive palate is the disappearing oronasal membrane. Definitive palate develops during weeks 5–12: primary palate (premaxilla) from the intermaxillary segment of frontonasal prominence; secondary palate from two maxillary palatine shelves. Initially vertical beside the tongue, the shelves elevate horizontally, grow together, and fuse from anterior to posterior with each other, primary palate and nasal septum from week 9 to week 12. Secondary palate forms posterior two thirds of hard palate, soft palate and uvula; incisive foramen marks the junction. Clefts posterior to it arise from failure of shelf fusion; anterior clefts arise from deficient mesenchyme in maxillary prominence/intermaxillary segment.

questions.text: 15. A new born baby had an attack of vomiting after each suckling. What is the most-likely anomaly:
questions.explanation: Projectile vomiting after feeds with a palpable epigastric mass in a newborn points to hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

questions.text: 58. Tongue tie develops due to:

options: Failure of fusion of the two lingual swellings.
Failure of fusion of the two parts of the tongue.
Failure of separation of epiglottis from posterior 1/3 of tongue.

questions.text: The development of the palate starts during which week of development:

questions.text: 111-which is a derivative of intermaxillary segment

questions.text: 26. The following are derivatives of foregut EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The distal duodenum is midgut-derived, whereas the proximal duodenum and stomach, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas arise from foregut endoderm.

questions.text: 29. The duodenum is:

Formed from the proximal part of the midgut.
Formed from the terminal part of the foregut.

differentiation of their acini completed after birth
sublingual & submandibular glands appear at 8th week IUL

questions.text: Discuss in brief the development of the tongue:
questions.explanation: Lateral lingual swellings overgrow the tuberculum impar to form the anterior tongue; the hypobranchial eminence forms posterior tongue, and occipital myotomes supply its muscles.
questions.modelAnswer:
Oral part:
A Median swelling appears in the floor of pharynx called tuberculum impar, then another 2 lateral swellings called lateral lingual swellings appear
then approximate till they overlap the tuberculum impar and form the anterior part
Pharyngeal part:
Copula and hypobranchial eminence appear in the floor of the pharynx opposite second & third pharyngeal arches then the hypobranchial
eminence overlaps the copula to form the posterior one third of the tongue. The line of demarcation is sulcus terminalis. The muscles of the tongue
migrate from the occipital myotomes.

questions.text: ANA13: The following are derivatives of the foregut except

questions.text: 1. Give an account on the anatomy of the Portal vein.
questions.explanation: The portal vein collects nutrient-rich blood from gut, spleen, pancreas, and gallbladder, then carries it through the liver before hepatic veins return it to the IVC.
questions.modelAnswer: Portal system drains stomach, intestine to upper anal canal, spleen, pancreas and gallbladder. Portal vein (about 8 cm) forms behind pancreatic neck at L2 by splenic and superior mesenteric union. Ascends anterior to IVC behind pancreatic neck then first duodenum then free lesser-omental margin, to divide at porta hepatis into right/left branches. Anterior relations: pancreatic neck infraduodenally; first duodenum, bile duct and gastroduodenal artery retroduodenally; hepatic artery proper and bile duct supraduodenally. Tributaries: splenic, superior mesenteric, right/left gastric, paraumbilical and cystic veins; cystic joins right branch, paraumbilical left branch. Left branch attaches to ligamentum teres and connects to IVC by ligamentum venosum.

questions.text: 5. Which one of the following is a tributary of splenic vein?

questions.text: ANA14: One of the following structures not a constituent of the porta hepatis:

questions.text: Mention supporting mechanisms of the liver

questions.text: 18. The liver gives attachment to the following EXCEPT:

questions.text: ANA14: One of the following structures not a constituent of the porta hepatis:

questions.text: Mention sites of Porto-systemic anastomosis
questions.explanation: Portal hypertension diverts blood through collateral links at esophagus, rectum, umbilicus, and retroperitoneal surfaces, producing varices and caput medusae.
questions.modelAnswer: Abdominal oesophageal wall: left gastric tributaries with azygos/accessory hemiazygos oesophageal veins. Rectal/anal wall: superior rectal with middle/inferior rectal veins. Umbilicus: paraumbilical with superficial epigastric veins. Bare liver area: intrahepatic portal veins with diaphragmatic veins. Posterior abdominal wall: colic veins with posterior-wall systemic veins. Rarely in liver: left portal branch with patent ductus venosus. Portal hypertension enlarges these collateral channels, producing oesophageal varices, rectal varicosities and caput medusae.

questions.text: 2. Discuss sites of portosystemic anastomosis.
questions.explanation: Portal hypertension diverts blood through portosystemic anastomoses: left gastric to esophageal veins, superior rectal to systemic rectal veins, and paraumbilical to superficial epigastric veins; these collaterals may varix and bleed.
questions.modelAnswer: Abdominal oesophageal wall: left gastric tributaries with azygos/accessory hemiazygos oesophageal veins. Rectal/anal wall: superior rectal with middle/inferior rectal veins. Umbilicus: paraumbilical with superficial epigastric veins. Bare liver area: intrahepatic portal veins with diaphragmatic veins. Posterior abdominal wall: colic veins with posterior-wall systemic veins. Rarely in liver: left portal branch with patent ductus venosus. Portal hypertension enlarges these collateral channels, producing oesophageal varices, rectal varicosities and caput medusae.

questions.text: Case 2: A patient with a long-standing liver disease complained of vomiting of blood. The doctor noticed dilated veins radiating from the patient's umbilicus.
questions.explanation: Portal hypertension opens two portosystemic pathways: left gastric–azygos esophageal varices cause hematemesis, while paraumbilical–superficial epigastric veins dilate as caput medusae.

subQuestions.text: 1. From your anatomical knowledge, what is the source of the vomited blood? Which vessels are involved?
subQuestions.explanation: The umbilical collaterals signal portal hypertension; blood vomiting is most consistent with ruptured lower-esophageal varices where left gastric portal tributaries join azygos-system veins.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: The source of the vomited blood is the varicosed veins in the lower end of the oesophagus. The vessels involved are the tributaries of the left gastric vein (portal) & the oesophageal tributaries of the azygos & the accessory hemiazygos veins.

subQuestions.text: 2. What is the clinical name of the vomiting of the blood?
subQuestions.explanation: Vomiting blood is hematemesis. With chronic liver disease, a common cause is bleeding from esophageal varices produced by portal hypertension.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Haematemesis.

subQuestions.text: 3. What is the name of the veins around the umbilicus? What vessels are involved?
subQuestions.explanation: The dilated umbilical veins are paraumbilical portal tributaries communicating with superficial epigastric systemic veins, producing caput medusae in portal hypertension.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Veins around umbilicus are called paraumbilical veins. Vesels involved are paraumbilical veins (portal) & superficial epigastric vein (systemic).

C4, 5 .

questions.text: Case 3: A 27-year-old man was admitted to the surgical ward with hematemesis (vomiting blood). After resuscitation, clinical investigations had diagnosed portal hypertension.
questions.explanation: Portal hypertension enlarges collaterals: left gastric to azygos-system esophageal veins can bleed; rectal and paraumbilical shunts can also dilate. The portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck and divides at the porta hepatis.

subQuestions.text: 1. Explain the cause of hematemesis in this case.
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension diverts blood through left gastric–esophageal connections to azygos-systemic veins, dilating esophageal veins that can rupture and cause hematemesis.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Cause of haematemesis: in the wall of abdominal oesophagus → tributaries of the left gastric vein (portal) connect with oesophageal tributaries of the azygos and accessory hemiazygos veins (systemic). Engorgement of these anastomotic veins may result in varicosities (oesophageal varices) and even fatal haematemesis (vomiting of blood).

subQuestions.text: 2. List the other sites that could be involved in such case.
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension also distends portal–systemic connections at the rectum and umbilicus, producing rectal varices and caput medusae.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Other sites that could be involved: a. In the rectal and anal canal wall: Connections between the inferior and middle rectal veins, (systemic) and superior rectal vein (portal) may result in varicosities (haemorrhoids or piles) with bleeding per rectum. b. At the umbilicus: Connections between the paraumbilical veins (running on ligamentum teres to left branch of the portal vein) and the superficial epigastric vein (systemic) may produce varicosities of veins radiating from the umbilicus (the caput Medusae).

subQuestions.text: 3. Describe the formation, course & termination of the portal vein.
subQuestions.explanation: The portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins, ascends behind the first duodenum and in the hepatoduodenal ligament, then divides at the porta hepatis.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Portal Vein: Origin: The portal vein is formed behind the neck of the pancreas at the level of L2, by union of superior mesenteric and splenic veins. Course: It ascends in front of IVC upwards & a little to the right first behind the neck of the pancreas next behind the 1st part of the duodenum & lastly in the right free margin of the lesser omentum. It ends in the porta hepatis, by dividing into right and left branches which enter into the corresponding lobes of the liver. Termination: At the porta hepatis the portal vein divides into right and left branches, each enters the corresponding functional lobe of the liver.

questions.text: 8. Von-Kupffer cells of liver are derived from:

questions.text: Question 20:A male farmer patient 35 years old, presented severe bloody vomiting.
questions.explanation: Portal pressure can enlarge esophageal submucosal veins where left gastric tributaries connect with azygos-system veins; rupture causes hematemesis.

subQuestions.text: a. What is the possible reason of that case?
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension redirects blood through esophageal portosystemic channels, enlarging submucosal veins into varices that can rupture and cause hematemesis.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Possible reason: Portal hypertension, esophageal varices, varicose veins

subQuestions.text: b. Mention the anatomical base of this condition?
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension enlarges esophageal venous connections: portal left-gastric tributaries communicate with systemic azygos/hemiazygos veins, creating varices that may bleed.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Anatomical base:Esophagus is partly supplied by portal circulation and partly by
systemic (tributaries of left gastric vein (portal) connect with esophageal tributaries
of the azygous and accessory hemiazygous veins (systemic)) engorgement of these
anastomotic veins may result in varices and even fatal hematemesis (vomiting of
blood).

questions.explanation: The gallbladder lies to the right of the quadrate lobe, not left. Its fundus is near the ninth costal cartilage and it relates to the first duodenum.
options: It lies to the left of quadrate lobe of the liver.
Its fundus lies opposite to the right 9th costal cartilage.
Is supplied by the right phrenic nerve.
Is related to the first part of the duodenum.

questions.text: 4. The stem of liver bud gives rise to the:
questions.explanation: The liver-bud stalk forms extrahepatic bile ducts, including the common bile duct; hepatocyte cords arise from pars hepatica.

questions.text: 11. The common bile duct is located:
questions.explanation: The common bile duct grooves the posterior pancreatic head; it does not lie behind the pancreas itself or IVC.
options: Behind the head of the pancreas.
To the left of the hepatic artery.
In front of the 1st part of the duodenum.

questions.text: 43. All about liver development is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The cranial part of the liver bud is pars hepatica; its caudal diverticulum is pars cystica, which forms gallbladder and cystic duct.
options: Arises at the end of foregut.
Its caudal part is called pars hepatica.
Its blood sinusoids develop from vitelline veins.
Septum transversum forms its capsule and stroma.

questions.text:
Question 21: A 27 years old man was admitted to the surgical ward with
hematemesis (vomiting blood). After resuscitation, clinical investigations had
diagnosed portal hypertension.
N.B. : It can also be due to ulcer in posterior wall of stomach because it can erode splenic
artery causing hemorrhage.
questions.explanation: Portal hypertension opens collateral channels, especially lower esophageal varices in a patient with hematemesis; the portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck and ends in right and left intrahepatic branches.

subQuestions.text: a. Explain the cause of hematemesis in this case.
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension forces blood through esophageal portosystemic channels; engorged submucosal veins can become varices and rupture, causing hematemesis.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Cause of hematemesis: portal hypertension “open of Porto systemic shunt” (which
is esophageal varices in this case)

subQuestions.text: b. List other site(s) could be involved in such case.
subQuestions.explanation: Portal hypertension can enlarge portosystemic channels at esophagus, umbilicus, rectum, retroperitoneum, and bare area; these collaterals bypass elevated portal resistance.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Other site could be involved:
- In the wall of the rectum and anal canal(Superior rectal vein & middle and
inferior rectal vein)
- At the umbilicus (para umbilical vein &superficial epigastric)→CAPUT
MEDUSAE
- Bare area of liver (veins inside the liver & veins of the diaphragm)
- posterior abdominal wall( colic veins & posterior abdominal wall)
- Inside the liver (left portal branch& inferior vena cava )

subQuestions.text: c. Describe formation, course & termination of the portal vein.
subQuestions.explanation: The portal vein forms from splenic and superior mesenteric veins behind the pancreatic neck, ascends behind the first duodenum then within the lesser omentum, and divides at the porta hepatis.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
Formation: union of splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein at the level of
L2behind neck of pancreas
Course:ascend in 2 regions :
1. behind 1st part duodenum where bile duct & gastro duodenal artery are anterior
to it and the I.V.C is posterior to it
2. In the free border of lesser oumentum the bile duct & hepatic artery are anterior
to it and epiploic foramen I behind separating it from I.V.C
Termination: divide into left & right portal branches in porta hepatis
( end like an artery)

questions.text: 34. The common bile duct is located:
questions.explanation: The common bile duct descends posterior to the first duodenum and in a groove or tunnel through the pancreatic head before opening into the second duodenum.
options: Behind the head of the pancreas.
To the left of hepatic artery.
In front of the first part of the duodenum.

questions.text: 13. Liver sinusoids are derived from the:
questions.explanation: Hepatic sinusoids develop as vitelline and umbilical veins are incorporated into the growing liver and form vascular channels among hepatocyte cords.
options: Stem of pars hepatica of liver bud.

questions.text: 39. Dilated veins due to opening of portosystemic anastomosis produce the following clinical conditions:
questions.explanation: Raised portal pressure enlarges collateral veins at esophagus, anorectum, and umbilicus, causing esophageal varices, rectal varices, and caput medusae.

questions.text: 45. The primitive pancreas develops by two endodermal diverticulae from the foregut. Their participation in the definitive organ is as follows:
questions.explanation: The dorsal pancreatic bud forms body, tail, and much of the head; the ventral bud forms the uncinate process and lower head.
options: The ventral bud forms the body.
The dorsal bud forms the body.
The ventral bud forms the entire pancreas.
The dorsal bud forms the entire pancreas.
Each bud contributes equally to all parts of the pancreas.

questions.text: 116. Caput medusae signify:
questions.explanation: Caput medusae is the visible network of dilated paraumbilical veins caused by portal hypertension and collateral flow through abdominal-wall veins.

questions.text: 86. Which of the following is the obliterated umbilical vein?
questions.explanation: The umbilical vein closes after birth and persists as ligamentum teres in the free edge of the falciform ligament.

questions.text: 12. The common hepatic duct is derived from the:
questions.explanation: The common hepatic duct arises from the hepatic portion (pars hepatica) of the hepatic diverticulum, which gives rise to liver and intrahepatic ducts.
options: Stem of pars hepatica of liver bud.

questions.text: 46. The pancreatic islets are responsible for the secretion of insulin. Secretion starts at:
questions.explanation: Fetal pancreatic islets begin insulin secretion around the fifth month, before birth; this is distinct from mature postnatal endocrine regulation.

questions.text: 111. Which of the following combinations is not a postal-systemic (portocaval) anastomosis?
questions.explanation: Superior and inferior epigastric veins are both systemic; their portosystemic connection is with portal paraumbilical veins, not with each other.
options: Left gastric veins and esophageal veins
Superior, middle and inferior rectal veins

questions.text: 37. All the following are sites of portosystemic anastomosis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The inguinal canal is not a portosystemic collateral site; recognized connections include esophageal, rectal, paraumbilical, and retroperitoneal channels.

questions.text: 152- fundus of gall bladder lies at line of junction between transpyloric plane and
questions.explanation: The gallbladder fundus projects where the transpyloric plane meets the right ninth costal cartilage, near the lateral border of rectus abdominis.

questions.text: 23. The following structures constitute the extrahepatic biliary apparatus, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic duct joins the biliary tree at the hepatopancreatic ampulla but is not itself part of the extrahepatic biliary apparatus.

questions.text: 2. The pars cystica of the liver bud gives rise to the:
questions.explanation: The pars cystica, an outgrowth of the hepatic diverticulum, forms the gallbladder and cystic duct.

questions.text: 8. The length of the common bile duct is:
questions.explanation: Three inches is about 7.5 cm, the usual approximate length of the common bile duct from hepatic/cystic duct union to duodenum.

questions.text: 49. A patient with portal hypertension showed caput medusae. Which veins (belonging to portal circulation) caused this appearance?
questions.explanation: Paraumbilical veins are the portal limb of the collateral network that becomes visible as radiating abdominal-wall veins in caput medusae.

questions.text: 153- fundus of gall bladder lies at line of junction between transpyloric plane and
questions.explanation: The gallbladder fundus lies near the right ninth costal cartilage where the transpyloric plane meets the right linea semilunaris.

questions.text: 32. The stem of the liver bud gives rise to:
questions.explanation: The liver-bud stalk forms the common bile duct; pars hepatica forms liver parenchyma and pars cystica forms gallbladder/cystic duct.

questions.text: 114-the uncinate process of pancreas developed from
questions.explanation: The ventral pancreatic bud rotates behind the duodenum and forms the uncinate process and inferior part of the head; the dorsal bud forms the rest.

questions.text: ANA16: The bile duct develops from:
questions.explanation: The extrahepatic bile duct develops from the stalk of the hepatic diverticulum, while its cystic bud forms the gallbladder and cystic duct.

questions.text: 2. The fundus of the gall bladder is located opposite the tip of the:
questions.explanation: The gallbladder fundus is marked by the right ninth costal cartilage, near the lateral rectus border.

questions.text: 117-the only endodermal part of liver
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes derive from foregut endoderm in the hepatic diverticulum; capsule, sinusoids, and Kupffer cells arise from mesenchymal/vascular lineages.

questions.text: 25. A gallstone has eroded through the posterior wall of the gallbladder and entered the intestinal tract. Which part of the intestinal tract is likely to initially contain the stone?
questions.explanation: A gallstone can erode through the gallbladder into adjacent transverse colon, forming a cholecystocolic fistula and allowing stone passage into bowel.

questions.text: 38. Portosystemic anastomosis occurs between the following veins EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Splenic and inferior mesenteric veins are both portal tributaries, so their union is not a portosystemic connection; the other pairs connect portal and systemic beds.
options: Esophageal branches of left gastric vein with hemiazygos vein.
Superior rectal with inferior rectal veins.
Epigastric veins with veins along ligamentum teres of liver.
Splenic vein with inferior mesenteric vein.

questions.text: 44. Ligamentum teres (of the liver) represents an obliterated:
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres is the fibrous remnant of the fetal left umbilical vein, which carried placental blood toward the liver.

questions.text: 59. Radiological examination of a female patient reveals a large gall bladder stone. Which of the following is the most likely site of gall stone lodge or impaction?
questions.explanation: A stone traveling through the common bile duct may lodge at the narrow hepatopancreatic ampulla, where biliary and pancreatic secretions enter the duodenum.

questions.text: 1. Caput medusae occurs in the following site of portosystemic anastomosis
questions.explanation: Caput medusae occurs around the umbilicus, where paraumbilical portal veins communicate with superficial epigastric veins.

questions.text: 137- ligamentum teres of liver is obliterated
questions.explanation: The fetal left umbilical vein obliterates to become the ligamentum teres; the right umbilical vein regresses earlier.

questions.text: 71. Which of the following is not a symptom of portal vein hypertension?
questions.explanation: Indirect inguinal hernia results from a patent processus vaginalis or deep-ring weakness, not portal hypertension, which causes collateral venous dilation.
options: Engorged veins of the posterior abdominal wall

questions.text: 154- gall bladder is related developmentally to
questions.explanation: The gallbladder buds from the caudal portion of the hepatic diverticulum, which is foregut-derived.

questions.text: 115-accessory pancreatic duct formed due to persistant
questions.explanation: The accessory pancreatic duct usually represents the persistent proximal part of the dorsal pancreatic duct; the main duct incorporates distal dorsal and ventral ducts.
options: distal part of dorsal pancreatic duct
proximal part of dorsal pancreatic duct
distal part of ventral pancreatic duct
proximal part of ventral pancreatic duct

questions.text: 25. The superior mesenteric vessels:
questions.explanation: SMA vessels cross anterior to the third duodenal part; SMA supplies midgut, arises near L1, and its vein drains to SMV/portal system.
options: Are the vessels of the primitive foregut.
Cross the third part of the duodenum.
Its artery arises from aorta at L3 level.
Its vein drains into the inferior vena cava.

questions.text: 5. During surgery, the ileum can be differentiated from the jejunum by:
questions.explanation: Ileum generally has a thinner wall and less prominent folds than jejunum; jejunum is thicker, with wider caliber and longer vasa recta.

questions.text: 16. The viscus whose mesentry contains 5-6 arterial arcades is the:
questions.explanation: Ileal mesentery contains more arterial arcades than jejunum, with shorter vasa recta; this compact branching pattern helps distinguish distal ileum.

questions.text: Enumerate two differences between the jejunum and ileum
questions.explanation: Jejunum has thicker, more vascular wall, larger plicae/villi, fewer arcades and longer vasa recta; ileum has more fat and Peyer patches. These gradients identify each segment.
questions.modelAnswer:
Feature | Jejunum | Ileum
Extent | Mostly in the upper left part of abd. cavity and umbilical region. | Mostly in the hypogastric region and right iliac fossa.
Diameter | Larger in diameter (4 cm). | Smaller in diameter (3.5 cm).
Thickness of the wall | Thick wall | Thin wall
Mucosa — circular folds (plicae circularis) | Larger and more numerous. | Smaller and few.
Mucosa — villi | Larger and more numerous. | Smaller and less numerous.
Mucosa — lymphoid follicles | Absent in the upper part. Few in the lower part. | Numerous, either solitary or aggregated (Peyer’s patches) that lie in the antimesenteric border.
Mesentery — mesenteric fat | Small amount so mesentery looks nearly translucent and the vessels are clearly seen i.e windows are present. | Greater amount and vessels cannot be seen, so no windows.
Mesentery — arterial arcades | Simple system (from 1-2 arcades). Long vasa recta. | Complicated system (from 3-5 arcades). Short vasa recta.
Mesentery — vascularity | More vascular (red mucosa) | Less vascular.

questions.text: 34. The jejunum and ileum can be differentiated on the basis of the following anatomic features except :
questions.explanation: Jejunum has few arterial arcades and long vasa recta; the statement assigning it numerous 4–5 arcades instead describes ileum.
options: Numerous (4 -5) arterial arcades are associated with the jejunum
The plicae circulares are much more prominent in the jejunum than in the ileum
Fat depositions are generally present throughout the mesentery associated with the ileum
The jejunum is located in the upper left region of the abdominal cavity
Peyer's patches are characteristic of the lower ileum and may be visible on the surface

questions.text: 32. All the following are branches of the ileocolic artery EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Jejunal arteries arise directly from the SMA; the ileocolic artery supplies terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, and proximal ascending colon, not jejunal loops.

questions.text: 12. When compared with the ileum, the upper part of the jejunum has:
questions.explanation: Jejunum has taller, more numerous plicae circulares, increasing absorptive surface compared with the smoother distal ileum.

questions.text:
Question 15: A young man during a quarrel got a transverse cut wound of the
anterior abdominal wall just above the umbilicus and to the left. He put his hand on
the wound and found part of his intestine coming out of the wound.
questions.explanation: A wound above and left of the umbilicus may expose mobile jejunum; identify small bowel by lack of taeniae/haustra and distinguish jejunum from ileum by its thicker wall, sparse arcades, and long vasa recta.

subQuestions.text: a. Which parts of the intestine can protrude through this wound “based on the site of the wound”?
subQuestions.explanation: Jejunum is mobile and may protrude through an abdominal wound; descending colon can also appear depending on wound position and depth.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Part of intestine can protrude: Jejunum (or descending colon.)

subQuestions.text: b. What other structures “other than intestine” may protrude through this wound?
subQuestions.explanation: A full-thickness wound can eviscerate mobile greater omentum and, depending on site, stomach as well as intestine; the omentum commonly protrudes first.
subQuestions.modelAnswer: Other structures may protrude: Parts of greater omentum, stomach.

subQuestions.text: c. How can the doctor identify the part of the intestine coming out of the wound?
subQuestions.explanation: Jejunum has a thicker wall, fewer arterial arcades with long vasa recta, and prominent circular folds; ileum has more mesenteric fat, short vasa recta, and Peyer patches.
subQuestions.modelAnswer:
To identify part of intestine:
Feature | Jejunum | Ileum
External features
1. Diameter | Wider | Narrower
2. Mesentery | Transparent | Opaque (Rich content of fat)
3. Arterial arcades | Simple arcades (1-3); Long Vasa Recta | Complex arcades (3–8); Short Vasa Recta
Internal features
1. Plicae semilunaris | More numerous | Less
2. Payers patches | Absent | Present
Feature | Large Intestine | Small intestine
Length | 1 meter | 6 meters
Caliber | Greater | Smaller
Mobility | Less mobile or more fixed | More mobile
Mesentery | Mesoappendix; Transverse mesocolon; Sigmoid colon | Mesentery for jejunum and ilium
Appendices Epiloicae | Present but absent from caecum,vermiform appendix and rectum | Absent
Taeniae Coli | Present | Absent
Sacculations (Haustrations) | present | Absent

questions.text: 14. All of the following help in differentiating jejunum from ileum EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are more numerous in jejunum than ileum. Ileum has fewer, smaller folds, especially distally, so the statement reverses the usual distinction.
options: Jejunum has thicker wall than ileum.
Plicae circularis are more numerous in ileum than jejunum.
Peyer's patches are found in the ileum.
The mesentry of ileum contains more arterial arcades than jejunum.
The root of mesentry of jejunum is attached at the left side of abdominal aorta.

questions.text: 1. Name the branches of superior mesenteric artery.
questions.explanation: SMA branches include jejunal/ileal arteries, inferior pancreaticoduodenal, middle colic, right colic, and ileocolic arteries, supplying most midgut.
questions.modelAnswer: Jejunal and ileal branches from left convex side; inferior pancreaticoduodenal, middle colic, right colic and ileocolic arteries from right concave side.

questions.text: 91. Primary arterial supply of which region travels via the superior mesenteric artery?
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric artery supplies midgut derivatives, from distal duodenum through proximal two-thirds of transverse colon.

questions.text: Compare: Differences between jejunum and ileum: Table L1
questions.explanation: Jejunum is thicker with larger folds and villi, fewer lymphoid patches, less mesenteric fat, fewer arcades, and longer vasa recta; ileum shows the contrasting pattern.
questions.modelAnswer:
Historical printed comparison table:
Item | Jejunum | Ileum
Extent | Mostly in the upper left part of abd. cavity & umbilical region. | Mostly in the hypogastric region & right iliac fossa
Diameter | Larger in diameter (4 cm) | Smaller in diameter (3.5 cm)
Thickness of the wall | Thick wall | Thin wall
Mucosa: Circular folds (plicae circularis) | Larger and more numerous. | Smaller and few.
Mucosa: Villi | Larger and more numerous. | Smaller and less numerous.
Mucosa: Lymphoid follicles. | Absent in the upper part. Few in the lower part | Numerous, either solitary or aggregated (Peyer’s patches) that lie in the antimesenteric border.
Structures in the mesentery: Mesenteric fat | Small amount so mesentery looks nearly translucent and the vessels are clearly seen i.e windows are present. | Greater amount and vessels cannot be seen, so no windows.
Structures in the mesentery: Arterial arcades | Simple system (from 1-2 arcades). Long vasa recta | Complicated system (from 35 arcades). Short vasa recta.
Vascularity | More vascular (red mucosa) | Less vascular.

questions.text:
Which one of the following arterial branches supplying the small intestine arises from the left convex side of the
superior mesenteric artery?
questions.explanation: Jejunal and ileal branches arise from the left convex side of the SMA; colic and ileocolic branches generally leave its right side.

questions.text: 27. Branches arising from right side of superior mesenteric artery include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Most SMA branches arise from its left side to the small bowel; the ileal/jejunal branches are therefore not right-sided branches.

questions.text: 2. Compare between the jejunum & the ileum.
questions.explanation: Jejunum and ileum differ in wall thickness, folds, lymphoid tissue, mesenteric fat, arcades, and vasa recta: jejunum is thicker with prominent folds; ileum has Peyer patches and more arcades.
questions.modelAnswer: Jejunum: proximal two fifths, upper left abdomen/umbilical region; larger calibre and thicker wall; larger/more numerous plicae and villi; no upper lymph follicles and few lower; little mesenteric fat with windows; 1–2 arterial arcades, long vasa recta and greater vascularity. Ileum: distal three fifths, hypogastrium/right iliac fossa; smaller calibre/thinner wall; smaller/fewer plicae and villi; numerous follicles/Peyer patches on antimesenteric border; more mesenteric fat/no windows; 3–5 arcades, short vasa recta and less vascularity.

questions.text: 15. Peyer's patch are most commonly found in the:
questions.explanation: Peyer patches are aggregated lymphoid follicles concentrated in ileum, especially terminal ileum, where they sample luminal antigens.

questions.text: ANA17: One of the following is a branch of superior mesenteric artery:
questions.explanation: The ileocolic artery is a terminal SMA branch supplying terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, and proximal ascending colon.

questions.text: 7. Compared to the ileum, the jejunum has:
questions.explanation: Jejunum has a thicker wall and larger lumen than ileum, with prominent folds and less mesenteric fat. Ileum has more lymphoid tissue and vascular arcades.

questions.text: 24. As regards the superior mesenteric artery, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The SMA gives the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery; the superior pancreaticoduodenal comes from gastroduodenal artery, so that is the false statement.
options: It arises from the anterior aspect of the aorta.
It passes posterior to the neck of the pancreas.
It passes anterior to the inferior part of the duodenum.
It gives the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.
It gives the middle colic artery.

questions.text: 4. When compared with ileum, the jejunum:
questions.explanation: Jejunum has more prominent plicae circulares for absorption; ileum has more Peyer patches and more complex arterial arcades.

questions.text: 3. The following statements concerning the ileum are true except:
questions.explanation: Plicae are tallest and most numerous in jejunum and diminish toward terminal ileum, where Peyer patches become abundant; the claim reverses this pattern.
options: The circular smooth muscle of the lower end of the ileum serves as a sphincter at the junction of the ileum and cecum
The branches of the superior mesenteric artery serving the ileum form more arcades than those serving the jejunum
Peyer's patches are present in the mucous membrane of the lower ileum along the antimesenteric border
The plicae circulares are more prominent at the distal end of the ileum than in the jejunum
The parasympathetic innervation of the ileum is from the vagus nerve

questions.text: 35. The artery that supplies the midgut region is the:
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric artery supplies midgut derivatives from distal duodenum through proximal two-thirds of transverse colon.

questions.text: 6. Which branch of the superior mesenteric artery gives the appendicular artery?
questions.explanation: The appendicular artery usually branches from the ileocolic artery, which arises from the SMA and reaches the appendix through the mesoappendix.

questions.text: 3. Superior mesenteric artery.
questions.explanation: SMA supplies midgut from distal duodenum through proximal two-thirds of transverse colon. Its branches include intestinal arcades, ileocolic, right and middle colic, and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries.
questions.modelAnswer: Artery of midgut: distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum, caecum, ascending colon and right two thirds transverse colon. Arises from anterior aorta at lower L1, 1 cm below coeliac trunk, behind pancreas, with splenic vein above and left renal vein below. Descends in front of uncinate process and third duodenum, then mesenteric root with vein to its right, curves rightward to right iliac fossa and joins ileal branch of ileocolic artery. Surrounded by superior mesenteric nerve plexus. Branches: Jejunal and ileal branches from left convex side; inferior pancreaticoduodenal, middle colic, right colic and ileocolic arteries from right concave side.

questions.text: 108. Which of the following groups of structures receives its arterial blood supply from the superior mesenteric artery?
questions.explanation: Jejunum, ileum, cecum, and ascending colon are midgut structures supplied by SMA; descending/sigmoid colon and rectum receive IMA/pelvic supply.
options: Ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon
Left colic flexure, descending colon, ascending colon, rectum
Left colic flexure, descending colon, spleen, sigmoid colon
Descending colon, left colic flexure, rectum, sigmoid colon

questions.text: 10. When compared with the ileum, the upper part of the jejunum:
questions.explanation: Upper jejunum has numerous, tall plicae circulares that increase absorptive surface; distal ileum has fewer, flatter folds and more lymphoid patches.
options: Has numerous mucous folds called plicae circularis.

questions.text: 1. When compared with the jejunum, the ileum has:
questions.explanation: Ileum contains prominent aggregated lymphoid follicles (Peyer patches); jejunum instead has taller plicae, longer vasa recta, and fewer arcades.

questions.text: 28. The branches of the superior mesenteric artery include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The left colic artery supplies hindgut and arises from the inferior mesenteric artery, whereas the other listed vessels branch from SMA.

questions.text: 62. The only statement regarding the small bowel which is true is:
questions.explanation: Peyer patches are aggregated lymphoid nodules, most abundant in the distal ileum, where they sample intestinal antigens.
options: The entire small bowel is intra-peritoneal
The jejunum is longer in length, large in diameter, and thinner-walled than the ileum
The muscularis, the muscle layer, provides the strength for the placement of sutures or staples for surgical anastomoses
Peyer's patches are most prominent in the distal ileum
The marginal artery of Drummond provides the blood supply to the duodenum

questions.text: 26. The superior mesenteric artery supplies all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The descending colon is hindgut and receives inferior mesenteric artery supply; SMA supplies appendix, jejunum, ileum, and proximal transverse colon.
options: Right half of the transverse colon.

questions.text: 12. Cancer in which of the following may spread to the superior mesenteric lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: The third duodenal part is midgut-derived and drains to superior mesenteric nodes. Foregut organs drain mainly to celiac nodes; hindgut to inferior mesenteric nodes.

questions.text: ANA17: One of the following is a branch of superior mesenteric artery:
questions.explanation: Ileocolic artery is an SMA branch supplying terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, and proximal ascending colon.

questions.text: 172- which is Not true regarding ilium of small intestine
questions.explanation: Ileum is less vascular and has thinner walls, shorter vasa recta, and more arterial arcades than jejunum; jejunum is the more vascular segment.
options: its wall thickness is less than jugenum
developed completely from Mid gut loop

questions.text: 112. Which of the following statements regarding the posterior abdominal wall is false?
questions.explanation: Quadratus lumborum receives segmental subcostal and lumbar ventral-ramus branches, not the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, which supplies thigh skin.
options: The iliopsoas muscle flexes the hip
The quadratus lumborum muscle receives somatic motor innervation via the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve
The medial and lateral arcuate ligaments serves as attachment sites to the thoracic diaphragm
Lumbar arteries arising from the abdominal aorta, supply blood to the posterior abdominal wall
The cisterna chyli is an enlargement at the inferior end of the thoracic duct

questions.text: 10. The following statements concerning the ureters are true except:
questions.explanation: Ureters pass posterior to the gonadal vessels, so the claim that they pass anterior is false; the vessels cross anteriorly as they descend.
options: Both have three anatomic sites that are constricted
Both receive their blood supply from the testicular or ovarian arteries
Both are separated from the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae by the psoas muscle
Both pass anterior to the testicular or ovarian vessels
Both lie anterior to the sacroiliac joints

questions.text: 95. The following statements about the kidney are true except:
questions.explanation: The kidney receives its arterial supply from the renal artery, a direct branch of the abdominal aorta, not from the celiac trunk.
options: Is in contact with the spleen on the left side
Is in contact with duodenum on the right side
Receives its blood supply from a branch of the celiac trunk

questions.text: 6. The following statements concerning the abdominal aorta are true except:
questions.explanation: The abdominal aorta lies left of the IVC; it enters through the aortic hiatus at T12 and bifurcates anterior to L4.
options: It bifurcates into the two common iliac arteries in front of the fourth lumbar vertebra
It lies on the right side of the inferior vena cava
From its anterior surface arise the celiac, superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric arteries
It enters the abdomen in front of the twelfth thoracic vertebra
The thoracic duct leaves the abdomen through the aortic opening of the diaphragm on the right side of the aorta

questions.text: 8. Which of the following branches of the abdominal aorta arises at the level of L4?
questions.explanation: The median sacral artery typically arises from the posterior aorta near its L4 bifurcation; the celiac, SMA, and renal arteries arise higher.

questions.text: 42. The following are direct tributaries of the inferior vena cava, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lower posterior intercostal veins usually drain into the azygos system, not directly to the IVC; hepatic, renal, and right suprarenal veins enter the IVC directly.
options: The third and fourth lumbar veins.

questions.text: 6. A nerve that emerges from anterior aspect of psoas major muscle is:
questions.explanation: The genitofemoral nerve emerges on the anterior surface of psoas major after forming within the muscle from L1–L2 fibers.

questions.text: Match the artery in the left column with its level of origin in the right column:
questions.explanation: These origins cluster around recognizable vertebral landmarks: SMA at L1, renal arteries near L1–L2, IMA at L3, and aortic bifurcation/median sacral near L4.

subQuestions.text: Common iliac artery.
subQuestions.explanation: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into common iliac arteries at about L4, near the level of the iliac crest.

subQuestions.text: Superior mesenteric artery.
subQuestions.explanation: The SMA arises from the abdominal aorta near L1, just inferior to the celiac trunk.

subQuestions.text: Inferior mesenteric artery.
subQuestions.explanation: The inferior mesenteric artery arises around L3, below the renal arteries and above the aortic bifurcation at L4.

subQuestions.text: Median sacral artery.
subQuestions.explanation: The median sacral artery usually arises from the posterior aorta near its L4 bifurcation, then descends along the sacrum.

subQuestions.text: Renal artery.
subQuestions.explanation: Renal arteries usually arise from the abdominal aorta around L1–L2, commonly at L1–L2 level near the renal hila.

questions.text: 5. The following statements concerning the left suprarenal gland are incorrect except:
questions.explanation: The left suprarenal vein drains into the left renal vein, unlike the short right suprarenal vein, which drains directly to the IVC.
options: It extends behind the inferior vena cava
It is separated from the left kidney by the pararenal fat
Its vein drains into the left renal vein
It is usually located on the upper pole and lateral border of the left kidney
The medulla is innervated by postganglionic sympathetic nerve fibres

questions.text: 3. The branch of the lumbar plexus that emerges from the medial aspect of the psoas major muscle is:
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve emerges from the medial border of psoas major and descends into the pelvis; femoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves emerge laterally.

questions.text: 88. The abdominal aorta:
questions.explanation: The aorta passes through the aortic hiatus with thoracic duct and azygos system, while autonomic aortic plexuses surround it.
options: Is surrounded by the central portion of the diaphragm
Is surrounded by plexus of autonomic nerve fibers

questions.text: ANA19: ALL the following nerves emerge at the lateral border of psoas major muscle except:
questions.explanation: The genitofemoral nerve pierces and descends on the anterior surface of psoas major; the other listed nerves emerge from its lateral border.
options: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

questions.text: Enumerate branches of abdominal aorta and their level
questions.explanation: Aortic branches follow predictable levels: celiac trunk and SMA near L1, renal and gonadal arteries near L2, IMA at L3, and common iliacs/median sacral near L4.
questions.modelAnswer: Unpaired: coeliac upper L1, SMA lower L1, IMA L3, median sacral L4. Paired: inferior phrenic upper L1; middle suprarenal lower L1; renal upper L2; gonadal lower L2; four lumbar pairs opposite corresponding vertebral bodies (fifth may arise from median sacral); terminal common iliac arteries lower L4.

questions.text: 19. Nerves emerging at the lateral border of psoas major muscle include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve exits the medial border of psoas; femoral, lateral femoral cutaneous, ilioinguinal, and iliohypogastric nerves emerge laterally.
options: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh.

questions.text: 47. Which of the following arteries supplies the suprarenal (adrenal) gland:
questions.explanation: The middle suprarenal arteries arise directly from the aorta; superior and inferior adrenal arteries arise from inferior phrenic and renal arteries respectively.

questions.text: 94. The following statements are true about the cisterna cyli except:
questions.explanation: The cisterna chyli is a lymphatic sac continuous superiorly with the thoracic duct, not the IVC; it collects intestinal and lumbar lymph trunks.
options: Receives lymph from nodes draining the posterior abdominal wall
Is in direct continuity with the inferior vena cava
Is a terminal dilation of the thoracic duct
Is generally located inferior to the aortic hiatus

questions.text: ANA19: ALL the following nerves emerge at the lateral border of psoas major muscle except:
questions.explanation: Genitofemoral nerve emerges from the anterior psoas surface, while ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric, and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves emerge laterally.
options: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

questions.text: 7. The following statements concerning the abdominal part of the sympathetic trunk are NOT TRUE except:
questions.explanation: Lumbar sympathetic trunks send gray rami to all lumbar spinal nerves; white rami are limited to thoracic and upper lumbar levels.
options: It enters the abdomen behind the lateral arcuate ligament
The trunk possesses six segmentally arranged ganglia
All the ganglia receive white rami communicantes
Gray rami communicantes are given off to the lumbar spinal nerves
The splanchnic nerves from the thorax join the trunks below the diaphragm

questions.text: 11. Regarding the abdominal aorta:
questions.explanation: The abdominal aorta bifurcates anterior to L4 into the common iliac arteries, which supply the pelvis and lower limbs.
options: It lies on the right side of the inferior vena cava.
It bifurcates in front of the 4th lumbar vertebra.
Its first branch is the renal artery.
It enters the abdomen in front of the 10th thoracic vertebra.
The thoracic duct leaves the abdomen on its left side.

questions.text: 50. The right kidney has the following important relationships except:
questions.explanation: The pancreatic neck/head are not a direct anterior relation of the right kidney; its anterior relations include liver, duodenum, right colic flexure, and small bowel.
options: It is related to the neck of the pancreas
It is anterior to the right costodiaphragmatic recess
It is related to the second part of the duodenum
It is related to the right colic flexure
It is anterior to the right twelfth rib

questions.text: 92. The renal arteries:
questions.explanation: Renal arteries arise from the aorta and supply kidneys; their inferior suprarenal branches also contribute adrenal blood, so the listed statements are all true.
options: Originate directly from the abdominal aorta
Provide arterial blood to the adrenal glands
Provide arterial blood to the kidneys
Usually form four anterior segmental arteries within the hilum of the kidney

questions.text: 103. What structure passes behind the medial arcuate ligament of the abdominal diaphragm:
questions.explanation: Psoas major passes behind the medial arcuate ligament; the aorta and thoracic duct pass through the aortic hiatus, while esophagus passes through the esophageal hiatus.

questions.text: 31. Vertebral level of bifurcation of abdominal aorta is:
questions.explanation: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into common iliac arteries in front of L4, a useful landmark for abdominal imaging and lower-limb arterial anatomy.

questions.text: List Tributaries of IVC and level of IVC
questions.explanation: The IVC forms from common iliac veins at L5 and passes through the diaphragm at T8; tributaries include lumbar, renal, right gonadal/suprarenal, inferior phrenic, and hepatic veins.
questions.modelAnswer: IVC begins from common iliac veins right of L5, ascends right of aorta and through diaphragm central tendon at T8 to right atrium. Tributaries: common iliac, third/fourth lumbar, right gonadal, renal, right suprarenal, inferior phrenic and right/left/middle hepatic veins.

questions.text: 44. The following general statements are incorrect except :
questions.explanation: The aorta ends by dividing into right and left common iliac arteries in front of L4, a key vertebral landmark.
options: The superior and inferior epigastric vessels anastomose on the anterior surface of the rectus abdominis muscle
The inguinal ligament is attached laterally to the anterior inferior iliac spine
The abdominal aorta bifurcates below, in front of the fourth lumbar vertebrae
The foregut ends in the third (inferior) segment of the duodenum
The umbilicus is located approximately at the vertebral level L5

questions.text: Relations of lumbar plexus branches to psoas major
questions.explanation: Lumbar plexus branches emerge around psoas: iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal, lateral femoral cutaneous, and femoral nerves laterally; genitofemoral anteriorly; obturator and lumbosacral trunk medially.
questions.modelAnswer: Lateral psoas border: iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal, lateral femoral cutaneous and femoral nerves. Anterior surface: genitofemoral. Medial border: obturator, accessory obturator and lumbosacral trunk.

questions.text: 45. The following veins drain directly into the inferior vena cava except:
questions.explanation: The inferior mesenteric vein usually joins splenic vein or the splenoportal confluence rather than draining directly to the IVC.

questions.text: 30. Regarding the abdominal aorta, choose one correct statement:
questions.explanation: The left renal vein crosses anterior to the aorta, passing behind the superior mesenteric artery on its way to the IVC.
options: Is crossed anteriorly by the left renal vein.
Enters the abdomen behind the medial arcuate ligament.
The splenic artery is one of its direct branches.
Bifurcates in front of the fifth lumbar vertebra.
The inferior vena cava lies on its left side.

questions.text: 23. Which of the following statements regarding the left ureter is correct?
questions.explanation: The ureter narrows physiologically at the pelvic brim where it crosses the iliac vessels, a common site for ureteric stone impaction.
options: It has the inferior mesenteric vein lying on its lateral side
Its lumen is constricted at the point where it crosses the brim of the pelvis
Its entire arterial supply is derived from the left renal artery
It lies in direct contact with the tips of the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae
It lies within the peritoneal cavity

questions.text: Afferents from which structures that drain into lateral aortic LNs / External iliac LNs
questions.explanation: Lateral aortic nodes receive lymph from gonads, kidneys, suprarenals, ureters, and common iliac nodes; external iliac nodes collect deep lower abdominal-wall and pelvic-organ lymph.
questions.modelAnswer: Lateral aortic nodes receive common iliac nodes, testes/ovaries, uterine tubes/fundus, kidneys/ureters/suprarenals. External iliac nodes receive inguinal nodes, deep infraumbilical abdominal-wall lymphatics, bladder fundus, prostate, cervix and part of vagina.

questions.text: 59. The following statements are true about muscles forming the posterior abdominal wall except:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm contributes to the posterior abdominal wall through its crura and arcuate ligaments, which arch over psoas and quadratus lumborum.
options: The psoas major muscle has a fascial sheath that extends down into the thigh as far as the lesser trochanter of the femur
The quadratus lumborum is covered anteriorly by fascia that forms the lateral arcuate ligament
The iliacus muscles is innervated by the femoral nerve
The transverses abdominis muscles does form part of the posterior abdominal wall
The diaphragm does not contribute to the musculature on the posterior abdominal wall

questions.text: 4. The hilum of the right kidney contains the following important structures, except the:
questions.explanation: The suprarenal gland sits on the superior kidney pole but is separate from the renal hilum, which transmits pelvis, vessels, nerves, and lymphatics.
options: Part of the right suprarenal gland

questions.text: 72. What structure passes behind the medial arcuate ligament of the abdominal diaphragm:
questions.explanation: The aorta passes behind the medial arcuate ligament; the psoas major and quadratus lumborum pass behind their own medial and lateral arcuate ligaments.

questions.text: 43. Which one of the following drains into the inferior vena cava directly?
