questions.text: 38. A major salivary gland:
questions.explanation: The sublingual gland is the smallest major salivary gland and has thin connective tissue partitions; its parenchyma is predominantly mucous.

questions.text: 8. which immunoglobulin is most abundant in saliva
questions.explanation: Secretory IgA is the dominant immunoglobulin in saliva, transported across glandular epithelium to protect oral mucosa.

questions.text: 14. Basket cells
questions.explanation: Basket cells are stellate myoepithelial cells rich in actin and myosin, wrapping acini to squeeze secretions outward.
options: surrounding the serous and mucous acini
stellate in shape with long process
rich with actin microfilament and myosin

questions.text: 4. Mention histological structure that adapt myoepithelium to do its function
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells contract around secretory end-pieces and proximal ducts, helping expel saliva while supporting the acinar basement membrane.
questions.modelAnswer: Myoepithelial cells lie between acinar basal plasma membrane and basal lamina and extend processes around secretory acini and intercalated ducts. questions.text: 20. The salivary duct that is lined with ion transporting cell is named:
questions.explanation: Striated ducts have ion-transporting cells that reabsorb NaCl and secrete K+/bicarbonate, making saliva hypotonic.

questions.text: 40. Which of the following ducts secrete lysozymes?
questions.explanation: Striated duct cells modify saliva by ion transport and release antimicrobial proteins such as lysozyme.

questions.text: 17. which part of the duct system contains longitudinally arranged mitochondria
questions.explanation: Striated ducts have basal infoldings packed with elongated mitochondria, which supply energy for active electrolyte transport and saliva modification.

questions.text: 46. The parotid gland:
questions.explanation: Parotid is a pure serous gland enclosed by a strong fibrous capsule; it does not have abundant mucous acini.
options: is a seromucus gland in humans
Wharton's duct is lined with str. Col. Epithelium

questions.text: 19. Saliva contains
questions.explanation: Saliva contains digestive amylase and antimicrobial secretory IgA, lysozyme, and lactoferrin; these together support digestion and oral defense.

questions.explanation: Basal membrane infoldings with aligned mitochondria create the striations in duct cells and power electrolyte transport.

questions.text: 18. Myoepithelial cells

are not controlled by the autonomic nervous system
prevent salivary acini distension during secretion
well defined around the pancreatic acini

questions.text:
32. Which of the following is considered the functioning secretory
unit of the salivary glands?
questions.explanation: The salivon includes the acinus and its duct system as a functional secretory unit; the acinus alone is only the end-piece.

questions.text: 6. Describe the structure of striated duct in salivary glands with correlation to its function
questions.explanation: Striated ducts modify primary saliva by absorbing sodium/chloride and secreting potassium/bicarbonate; their folded basal membranes support active transport.
questions.modelAnswer: Striated ducts are intralobular, formed by joined intercalated ducts. LM: cuboidal to low columnar cells, central rounded nuclei and acidophilic granular cytoplasm with basal striations. EM: basolateral infoldings partition elongated mitochondria into longitudinal compartments; this provides membrane area and energy for ion transport. They modify saliva by removing sodium/chloride and replacing potassium/bicarbonate; also deliver lysozyme and transport IgA.

questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells contract around secretory end pieces to help empty them and prevent overdistension. They lie between secretory cells and the basal lamina, rather than outside it.
options: are present outside the basal lamina
Prevent distension of secretory acini during secretion

questions.text: 39. The mucous cells have:
questions.explanation: Mucous cells have flattened basal nuclei because accumulated mucin compresses them toward the base; serous cells have rounder nuclei.

questions.text: 40. The serous acini are characterized by:

questions.text: 12. All of the following are characteristic of the salivary glands EXCEPT

questions.text: 33. Serous acini differ from mucus acini in:

questions.text: 29. The minor salivary glands are characterized by:

questions.text: 30. The major salivary glands are characterized by:

cells for squeezing the secretion towards the lumen of acini

questions.text:
37. Myoepithelial cells surrounding the intercalated ducts of the
salivary glands differ from those surrounding the secretory
portion in:
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells around intercalated ducts are elongated and spindle-shaped along the duct, unlike the branched basket-like cells around acini. Both forms contract to assist secretion movement.

questions.text: All about Striated ducts is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Striated ducts are characteristic of salivary glands, not the exocrine pancreas, whose ducts lack the basal transport striations.
options: Present in exocrine portion of pancreas

questions.text: 15. Which of the gland listed below is mixed but predominant serous?
questions.explanation: Human submandibular gland is mixed but mainly serous; sublingual is mainly mucous, parotid purely serous, and pancreas purely serous exocrine.

questions.text: 23. Myoepithelium surround ___ & ___ duct & its cytoplasm contains filaments which are ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells surround secretory acini and the proximal intercalated ducts. Their actin and myosin filaments make them contractile, helping move saliva from secretory units into ducts.

questions.text:
38. Which of the following ducts are surrounded by spindle
myoepithelial cells?
questions.explanation: Spindle-shaped myoepithelial cells embrace acini and intercalated ducts, contracting to help move secretion into the duct tree.

questions.text: HIS2: Which of the following glands has pure serous acini and its stroma is rich in fat cells:
questions.explanation: Parotid gland has serous acini and adult stroma often rich in adipocytes, distinguishing it from mixed/mucous glands.

questions.text: 74. Esophagus, all true except:

esophagus shows longitudinal folds that help in its expansion during swallowing.

questions.text:
75. Reflux of gastric juice due to diminished the lower esophageal sphincter tone with

questions.explanation: Reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus causes GERD; heartburn and erosive esophagitis reflect acid exposure of the mucosa.

questions.text: 81. Meissner's plexus is found in:
questions.explanation: Meissner plexus sits in submucosa and regulates secretion and local blood flow; Auerbach plexus lies between muscularis externa layers.

questions.text:
85. Reflux of gastric juice due to diminished the lower esophageal sphincter tone with
symptoms as heart burn or atypical chest pain.
questions.explanation: Reduced lower esophageal sphincter tone permits acidic gastric contents to reflux into the esophagus, producing heartburn and sometimes chest pain. This pattern defines gastroesophageal reflux disease.

questions.text: 2. The nerve plexus is found in ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Meissner's plexus lies in the submucosa and regulates local secretion and blood flow; Auerbach's plexus lies between muscle layers.

questions.text: Enumerate the different layers of the mucosa of Gastro-intestinal tract.
questions.explanation: GI mucosa consists of epithelium, lamina propria connective tissue, and muscularis mucosae; the latter creates local mucosal movement.
questions.modelAnswer:
The mucosa is the most superficial layer of the wall of the GIT. It is formed of epithelium which varies according to the part of tract; eg. simple
columnar in stomach and intestine, stratified squamous in esophagus. Below the epithelium lies a layer of connective tissue and a layer of smooth
muscle fibers (the muscularis mucosa) which is arranged as inner circular and outer longitudinal fibers.

questions.text: About esophagus, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The esophageal muscularis externa changes along its length: upper third is skeletal muscle, middle third mixed, and lower third smooth muscle. It is therefore not entirely smooth muscle.
options: Glands are present mainly in submucosa
Muscularis externa are formed entirely of smooth muscles.

questions.text: 2. Which type of muscle is lower third of esophagus formed?
questions.explanation: The distal esophagus contains smooth muscle; skeletal muscle is concentrated proximally, with a mixed transition in the middle third.

questions.text: HIS3: Regarding the histological structure of esophagus, choose ONE CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The upper esophageal third contains mainly skeletal muscle for voluntary initiation; middle third is mixed and lower third smooth muscle.
options: It contains Aurbach’s plexus in its submucosa.

questions.text: 14. Which of the following changes in gastroesophageal junction is true
questions.explanation: At the gastroesophageal junction, protective nonkeratinized stratified squamous esophageal lining changes abruptly to the stomach’s simple columnar mucous epithelium.
options: The epithelium changed from stratified squamous to simple columnar

questions.text:
28. A 34-year-old woman visits the clinic because she suffered from

pain for 6 months. She is slightly overweight and currently
smokes. Endoscopy was done and showed erosion of the lower

questions.text: Give short notes on the glands of oesophagus
questions.explanation: Esophageal glands in the submucosa lubricate the lumen; cardiac mucus glands in mucosa near both ends protect against abrasion and reflux acid.
questions.modelAnswer: Cardiac mucus glands in lamina propria at upper oesophagus and lower end near stomach lubricate/neutralize reflux acid. Oesophageal mucus glands scattered in submucosa supply lubricating/protective mucus.

questions.text: 82. (Auerbach' s) plexus found in:
questions.explanation: Auerbach’s (myenteric) plexus lies between the circular and longitudinal layers of the muscularis externa, where it coordinates gut motility. Meissner’s plexus is the submucosal plexus.

questions.text: 3. The glands in esophagus are present in ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Esophageal cardiac glands lie in the lamina propria near the ends, while proper esophageal glands lie in the submucosa.
blanks: Lamina propria at upper/lower ends (cardiac glands)

questions.text: 17. In which layer of gastrointestinal tract the Meissner’s plexus is found?

questions.text: Q17 Mention the structural difference between vagina &esophagus

questions.text: Esophagus,all true except:
questions.explanation: Esophageal submucosal glands occur along its length, and cardiac glands occur near its ends, so the claim that it has no glands is false.
options: muscular tube that conveys the ingested food from the pharynx to the stomach

questions.text: 26. Esophageal cardiac glands are present in:
questions.explanation: Esophageal cardiac glands lie in lamina propria near the lower end and secrete mucus to protect against refluxed gastric acid.
options: Mucosa of the upper end of esophagus.
Mucosa of the lower end of esophagus.

questions.text: 1. Muscularis mucosa is found in
questions.explanation: The mucosa comprises epithelium, lamina propria, and muscularis mucosa. The muscularis mucosa is the thin smooth-muscle boundary between mucosa and submucosa.

questions.text: 1. The main histological layers of GIT are ___, ___, ___ and ___
questions.explanation: The gut wall is organized from lumen outward as mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa, and either serosa or adventitia.

questions.text: HIS3: Regarding the histological structure of esophagus, choose ONE CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The upper esophagus is skeletal muscle and lower esophagus smooth muscle, so muscularis externa changes muscle type across the organ.
options: Its upper third contains mostly skeletal muscle fibers.
Its submucosal glands contain serous acini.
It contains Aurbach’s plexus in its submucosa.
It is lined by simple squamous epithelium.
It shows inner circular and outer longitudinal muscularis mucosa.

questions.text: 4. What is the lining epithelium of esophagus
questions.explanation: The esophagus uses nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium to resist abrasion from swallowed food while keeping its surface moist. It transitions to simple columnar epithelium at the stomach.
questions.modelAnswer: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.text:
19. At which site the Auerbach's plexus is present in the wall of the
gastrointestinal tract?
questions.explanation: Auerbach's myenteric plexus lies between the circular and longitudinal layers of muscularis externa and coordinates motility.

questions.text: 2. Mention the 2 types of nerve plexus in the wall of GIT & their sites.
questions.explanation: Auerbach’s (myenteric) plexus lies between circular and longitudinal muscularis externa; Meissner’s (submucosal) plexus lies in submucosa.

questions.text: Site & structure of esophageal glands:
questions.explanation: Esophageal submucosal glands occur along much of the tube and secrete lubricating mucus. Cardiac glands lie in the mucosal lamina propria near the proximal and distal ends.
questions.modelAnswer:
Submucosal: in most of the length of esophagus
        Mucosal: cardiac glands
                    In the proximal & distal ends of the esophagus

questions.text: 23. In which of the following parts of the GIT, the muscularis   externa contains skeletal muscle fibers?
questions.explanation: The upper esophageal third contains skeletal muscle for voluntary initiation of swallowing; the middle third is mixed and lower third smooth.

questions.text: 27. Mucus secreting glands of the esophagus are present in:
questions.explanation: Esophageal mucus glands occur in both lamina propria (cardiac glands) and submucosa (proper esophageal glands), lubricating and protecting the tube.

questions.text: 24. The lining epithelium of esophagus is:
questions.explanation: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium protects the esophagus from mechanical abrasion by food. A simple columnar lining appears only after the gastroesophageal junction.
options: Pseudostratified columnar ciliated with goblet cells.

questions.text:
18. At which site the Meissner's plexus is present in the wall of the
gastrointestinal tract?
questions.explanation: Meissner's submucosal plexus regulates mucosal secretion and local blood flow, unlike the myenteric plexus that chiefly controls motility.

questions.text:
25. Which of the followings characterizes the lamina propria of the
mucosa of esophagus?
questions.explanation: Esophageal cardiac glands in lamina propria secrete protective mucus; Auerbach and Meissner plexuses lie deeper in muscularis externa and submucosa.
options: It contains Auerbach's plexus of nerves.
It is formed of dense connective tissue.

questions.text: 1. Enumerate the 4 basic layers in gastro intestinal tract and components of each.
questions.explanation: Mucosa contains epithelium, lamina propria, and muscularis mucosa; submucosa contains connective tissue, vessels/glands, and Meissner plexus. Muscularis externa has circular/longitudinal muscle with Auerbach plexus; outer serosa/adventitia permits movement or attachment.
questions.modelAnswer: Mucosa: appropriate epithelium, loose lamina propria with vessels/immune tissue, inner circular/outer longitudinal smooth muscularis mucosa. Submucosa: loose CT, vessels/lymphatics, Meissner plexus, segment-dependent glands and scattered nodules. Muscularis externa: circular and longitudinal smooth muscle with Auerbach plexus between, supplying tone/peristalsis. Adventitia: loose CT with vessels/nerves; mesothelial covering makes serosa, supporting/protecting/free movement.

questions.text: 102. All the followings changes occur at the gastro-esophageal junctions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The muscularis externa changes arrangement at the stomach: an additional inner oblique layer joins the circular and longitudinal layers.
options: Stratified squamous epithelium is replaced by simple columnar epithelium.
Corium becomes wide & contains gastric glands.
Muscularis mucosa passes without any change.
Esophageal glands stop at the region of the fundus.
Muscularis externa passes without any change.

questions.text:
30. All the followings changes occur at the gastro-esophageal
junctions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: At the junction, stratified squamous esophageal lining becomes simple columnar gastric lining, and the stomach adds an inner oblique muscle layer to its muscularis externa.

Muscularis mucosa passes without any change.

questions.text: 3. Enumerate the glands present in esophagus
questions.explanation: Esophageal glands include mucous glands in the submucosa throughout much of the tube and cardiac glands in the lamina propria near both ends; both protect and lubricate the lining.
questions.modelAnswer: Cardiac mucus glands in lamina propria at upper oesophagus and lower end near stomach lubricate/neutralize reflux acid. Oesophageal mucus glands scattered in submucosa supply lubricating/protective mucus.

questions.text: 8. Describe the changes take place in gastroesophageal junction,
questions.explanation: At the junction, stratified squamous esophageal lining changes to simple columnar gastric epithelium; glands and muscle organization also change.
questions.modelAnswer: Stratified squamous oesophageal lining becomes simple columnar gastric pit epithelium; corium becomes occupied by gastric glands; muscularis mucosa continues; submucosal oesophageal glands stop; muscle gains inner oblique layer and thickens; serosa continues from distal oesophagus.

questions.text: 4. The muscle layer of esophagus in upper 1/3 is formed of___ while in lower 1/3 is formed of ___ & in middle 1/3 is formed of ___
questions.explanation: Esophageal muscularis externa is skeletal in upper third, smooth in lower third, and mixed in middle third, reflecting gradual neural/muscle transition.

questions.text: HIS3: Regarding the histological structure of esophagus, choose ONE CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The esophageal muscularis externa is skeletal in its upper third, mixed in the middle, and smooth in the lower third, enabling voluntary initiation followed by involuntary peristalsis.
options: Its submucosal glands contain serous acini.
It is lined by simple squamous epithelium.
It shows inner circular and outer longitudinal muscularis mucosa.
It contains Aurbach’s plexus in its submucosa.

questions.text: 96. Fundic glands have the following features EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fundic glands are straight, branched tubular glands with short gastric pits; they are not highly coiled, unlike some other gland types.
options: Its tubular acini are highly coiled

questions.text:
10. Which of the following differentiates peptic cells from
enteroendocrine cells?
questions.explanation: Chief (peptic) cells package pepsinogen in apical zymogen granules; enteroendocrine cells instead have secretory granules concentrated basally.
options: They are located at the fundic glands.
They have abundant rER and mitochondria.
They have well developed Golgi apparatus.

questions.text: 23. Which of the following enteroendocrine cells secrete serotonin?
questions.explanation: Enterochromaffin (EC) cells release serotonin, which promotes intestinal motility and secretion. G cells secrete gastrin, D cells somatostatin, and L cells peptides such as GLP-1.

questions.text: 39. The fundic gland is lined by all the following cells EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Fundic glands contain chief, parietal (oxyntic), mucous neck, surface mucous, enteroendocrine, and stem cells; “oxyphil” is not a separate gastric cell type.

questions.text: 7. Compare between fundus & pylorus structure
questions.explanation: Fundic glands are straight and occupy most of mucosa beneath shallow pits; pyloric glands are coiled, mucus-rich, and follow deeper pits, while pylorus has a thick circular sphincter.
questions.modelAnswer: Fundic glands in fundus/body: simple branched tubular, straight/perpendicular; narrow short pits occupy quarter mucosal thickness, glands three quarters; stem, surface mucus, neck mucus, chief, parietal and enteroendocrine cells. Pyloric glands: thinner mucosa, wide deep pits half thickness; branched highly coiled tubular glands in remaining half; predominant mucus cells with few parietal, stem and enteroendocrine (EC/D/G) cells. Fundic muscle has three layers (inner oblique, middle circular, outer longitudinal); pylorus has thick inner circular sphincter and outer longitudinal.

questions.text: 85. Oxyntic (parietal) cells show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Parietal cells are packed with mitochondria and contain intracellular canaliculi plus tubulovesicles for acid secretion, but have relatively little rough ER because they are not major protein-secreting cells.

questions.text:
5. Stem cells of the fundus of the stomach are present at which part
of the fundic glands?
questions.explanation: Gastric epithelial stem cells cluster in the isthmus and neck, where they divide and migrate to renew both surface and gland cells.

questions.text: 14. The peptic cell, BY LM : its shape is ___ nucleus is ___, cytoplasm appear ___
questions.explanation: Chief cells are pyramidal with a basal nucleus and basophilic basal cytoplasm; apical zymogen granules store pepsinogen for protein digestion.
blanks: Basophilic with basal striations and apical acidophilic zymogen granules

questions.text: Compare fundic, pyloric & cardiac:
questions.explanation: Fundic glands are straight and contain parietal and chief cells; cardiac and pyloric glands are more mucous-secreting and coiled. Pyloric pits are deeper than fundic pits, whereas cardiac pits are relatively short.
questions.modelAnswer:
All are simple branched tubular glands, present in gastric mucosa.
Row | fundus | pylorus | Cardiac
Pits | Short; ¼ the mucosal thickness | Deep, long & wide; ½ the mucosal thickness | Short; ¼ the mucosal thickness
Glands | Perpendicular on the surface; Divided into isthmus, neck, base; Lined by multiple types of cells | Coiled; Mostly mucous secreting (alkaline mucous) | coiled; Mostly mucous secreting

questions.text:
Site, Structure & function of:
Chief cell
Parietal (oxyntic cell) (3 LM & 3 EM characters)
Mucous neck cell
Mucous surface cell
Enteroendocrine cell
Stem cell
questions.explanation: Chief cells release pepsinogen; parietal cells make acid and intrinsic factor; mucous cells protect the surface, while endocrine cells signal through blood or locally.
questions.modelAnswer: Stem cells in isthmus: short columnar, basal oval nuclei/basophilic cytoplasm and free ribosomes; renew surface/gland epithelium. Surface mucus cells cover surface/pits: columnar, basal oval nuclei, apical PAS-positive mucinogen; RER/Golgi/mitochondria and apical granules with junctional complexes; secrete bicarbonate-rich alkaline insoluble protective mucus. Mucous-neck cells in neck: columnar, basal round nuclei/pale basophilic mucin cytoplasm; RER, Golgi, mitochondria and apical granules; secrete acidic soluble mucus. Chief cells at base: tall columnar, basal rounded nuclei/basal basophilia and apical acidophilic zymogen; abundant RER, Golgi, mitochondria and membrane-bound apical vesicles, junctional complexes; secrete pepsinogen and lipase. Parietal cells in isthmus/neck/base: triangular/round, central round nuclei (sometimes two), deeply acidophilic; intracellular canaliculi/microvilli, tubulovesicular system and abundant mitochondria; Golgi and few RER; secrete HCl and intrinsic factor. Enteroendocrine cells: columnar/triangular with basal round nuclei and narrow apex; RER/Golgi/mitochondria and basal secretory granules; open types reach lumen with microvilli, closed types do not; release hormones into corium/blood.

questions.text:
16. Muscularis externa of the fundus of the stomach differs from
those of other parts of the GIT by the presence of:
questions.explanation: The stomach adds an inner oblique muscle layer to circular and longitudinal layers, improving churning compared with most gut regions.

questions.text: 48. Auerbach's plexus of the stomach is found in:
questions.explanation: The myenteric (Auerbach) plexus lies between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layers of the muscularis externa, allowing it to coordinate gastric contractions.

questions.text: 61. Gastrin hormone
questions.explanation: Gastrin promotes acid secretion and gastric mucosal growth, so both listed actions are correct and the combined choice applies.
options: proliferation of the stem cells of gastric glands

questions.text: 78. Ithmus of fundic (gastric) gland contain the following except :
questions.explanation: Chief cells sit at the fundic-gland base; the isthmus contains surface mucous, stem, and parietal cells.

questions.text: 20. The cardiac gland characterized by which of the followings
questions.explanation: Cardiac glands are predominantly mucous-secreting and help protect the gastroesophageal junction. Long straight glands with many parietal cells are characteristic of the fundus, not cardia.
options: The gland is long and perpendicular to the surface

questions.text: 48. Mucous secretion of the stomach is produced by:
questions.explanation: Surface mucous cells cover the stomach and mucous neck cells line the gland neck; goblet cells are not normal gastric epithelial cells.

questions.text: 87. Cardiac glands of stomach, all true except:
questions.explanation: Cardiac glands have relatively short shallow pits and mainly mucus-secreting glands; half-depth pits characterize the pyloric region instead.
options: present in the narrow band 10-40 mm wide around the esophageal orifice
lined by secreting cells that secrete mucous and few lysozymes
few parietal cells for HCL secretion and some enteroendocrine cells that secrete gastrin.
pits are relatively deep, occupying one half of the thickness of the mucosa

questions.text: 19. One of the specific character of peptic cells is:
questions.explanation: Chief (peptic) cells produce pepsinogen and have abundant rough ER for protein synthesis, with apical secretory granules. Their basophilic cytoplasm contrasts with acidophilic parietal cells.
options: Their presence in all parts of fundic gland

questions.text: Describe the structure function adaptation of the stomach
questions.explanation: Rugae let the stomach expand; its three muscle layers churn food. Parietal cells provide acid and intrinsic factor, chief cells provide pepsinogen/lipase, and endocrine cells regulate secretion; mucus-bicarbonate and rapid renewal protect the lining.
questions.modelAnswer: Rugae permit expansion/reservoir function and sphincters regulate contents. Three fundic muscle directions mix food and enzymes into chyme. Parietal acid helps antibacterial action and intrinsic factor enables B12 absorption; chief pepsinogen/lipase permit digestion; enteroendocrine hormones regulate secretion. Bicarbonate-rich surface mucus/junctions and continuous 4–7-day epithelial renewal protect gastric wall.

questions.text: Ithmus of fundic [gastric] gland contain the following except :
questions.explanation: Chief cells are located at gland bases, not the isthmus; the isthmus contains surface mucous, stem, and parietal cells.

questions.text: 89. Pyloric glands when compared to fundic glands show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Pyloric pits are deeper and wider than the short pits of fundic mucosa; pyloric glands are coiled and mainly mucous-secreting. Thus “pits are shorter” is not a pyloric feature.
options: Their acini are more coiled and branched
The main cell type is similar to mucous neck cells of fundus

questions.text: 49. Enteroendocrine cells are called argentafﬁn because they are stained with:
questions.explanation: Argentaffin endocrine granules reduce silver salts, making silver-based staining useful for visualizing these gut neuroendocrine cells.

questions.text: 89. Neck of fundic (gastric) gland contain the following except :
questions.explanation: Paneth cells belong to small-intestinal crypts, not fundic gland neck; fundic neck contains mucous neck, parietal, and stem cells.

questions.text: 2. All the following statements about the neuroendocrine cells are TRUE EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Gastric enteroendocrine cells release hormones basally toward the lamina propria and nearby cells or blood, rather than emptying directly into the gland lumen. Their signaling can be endocrine or paracrine.
options: their polarity is opposite to that of gastric chief cells
they usually empty their secretion directly into the lumen of the gland
their production of gastrin stimulates acid production by parietal cell
they can secrete hormones which can interact with neighboring cell

questions.text: 13. Which of the following is TRUE about active parietal cells?
questions.explanation: Active parietal cells insert tubulovesicles into the canalicular membrane, increasing microvilli and the surface available for HCl secretion.
options: They are responsible for digestive enzyme secretion.
They share in absorption of vitamin A.
Their EM shows increase in number of microvilli
Their EM shows increase in number of tubulovesicular system.
Their EM shows plenty rER and few mitochondria.

questions.text: 16. The parietal cell, BY LM : its shape is ___nucleus is ___, cytoplasm appear ___
questions.explanation: Parietal cells are large rounded/pyramidal cells with a central nucleus and strongly eosinophilic cytoplasm packed with mitochondria.

questions.text: Describe the microscopic structure & correlated function of parietal cells
questions.explanation: Parietal cells use abundant mitochondria to power acid transport and intracellular canaliculi to provide a large apical secretory surface. Tubulovesicles supply membrane during activation; intrinsic factor supports vitamin B12 absorption.
questions.modelAnswer: Parietal cells lie in all three fundic regions. LM: triangular/rounded shape, central rounded nuclei (sometimes binucleate), deeply acidophilic cytoplasm. EM: C-shaped canaliculi with microvilli, surrounding tubulovesicles, abundant mitochondria, Golgi and few RER. Actin-assisted fusion of vesicles with canalicular membrane during secretion increases microvilli/surface while reducing tubulovesicles. Canaliculi provide acid-secretory surface; mitochondria provide active-transport energy. Cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor needed for B12 absorption.

questions.text: 11. Somatostatin is secreted by
questions.explanation: D cells release somatostatin, which inhibits gastrin and acid secretion; G cells instead produce gastrin.

questions.text: Neck of fundic [gastric] gland contain the following except :
questions.explanation: Paneth cells occur at intestinal crypt bases, not the fundic gland neck; mucous neck, parietal, and stem cells are found there.

questions.text: 41. The parietal cells
questions.explanation: Parietal cells have intracellular canaliculi and secrete both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor. Intrinsic factor is required for efficient vitamin B12 absorption in the terminal ileum.
options: with EM they show intracellular canaliculus

questions.text: 83. Surface mucous cells show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Surface mucous cells secrete alkaline, bicarbonate-rich mucus that shields gastric epithelium from acid and pepsin, rather than acidic mucus.
options: Found in the isthmus of the fundic glands.
Continuous with the covering epith of the stomach

questions.text: 91. In case of atrophic gastritis, deficiency in vitamin B12 result from damage of:
questions.explanation: Parietal-cell destruction removes intrinsic factor, preventing terminal-ileal vitamin B12 absorption and causing pernicious anemia.

questions.text: 22. Pyloric sphincter is made by which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter is a localized thickening of the inner circular layer of the muscularis externa. It regulates gastric emptying into the duodenum.
options: Inner and outer layers of muscularis externa.

questions.text: One of the following is not true about the enteroendocrine cells:
questions.explanation: Enteroendocrine cells release hormones basally into tissue and blood or act locally; they do not deliver all secretion into the gut lumen.

They are of two types open and closed.
They deliver their secretions only in the git lumen.
They are also called argentaffine cells

questions.text: 4. Gastric pits of the fundus occupy......of the mucosal thickness.
questions.explanation: Fundic pits are short and occupy about one-quarter of mucosal thickness; the deeper three-quarters contains the gastric glands.

questions.text: Surface epithelium of gastric mucosa:
questions.explanation: Surface mucous cells secrete bicarbonate-rich, near-neutral mucus that forms a protective gel over gastric epithelium. This barrier shields cells from luminal acid and pepsin.
options: Secretes acidic mucous to form a protective gel
Secretes neutral to alkaline mucus rich in bicarbonate to form a protective gel
Have pale cytoplasm & flattened basal nuclei

questions.text: 56. Which of the following cells line the gastric pit of the gastric gland?
questions.explanation: Gastric pits are lined by surface mucous cells continuous with the stomach surface; chief and parietal cells lie deeper in glands.

questions.text: 91. One of the following is not true about the enteroendocrine cells:
questions.explanation: Enteroendocrine cells release hormones basally into lamina propria/blood or local tissue, rather than secreting only into the gland lumen.
options: They are present in the stomach, small intestine and large intestine.
They are of two types open and closed.
They deliver their secretions only in the git lumen.
They are also called argentaffine cell

questions.text: 97. Zymogen cells of fundic glands show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Chief cells are concentrated toward the base of fundic glands, where they release pepsinogen and gastric lipase. The neck contains mucous neck cells and many parietal cells.

questions.text:
44. A smooth surfaced system of tubules and vesicles is associated with which of the 
following cells?
questions.explanation: Parietal cells contain a tubulovesicular membrane system that expands into microvillus-lined intracellular canaliculi during active acid secretion.

questions.text: During active HCL secretion parietal cell shows:

options: Few short microvilli while tubulovesicular system increases.
Microvilli are prominent numerous while the tubulovesicular system decreases.

questions.text: 6. Describe how structure of stomach is correlated to its function
questions.explanation: The stomach combines expandable rugae and a three-layered muscle coat for storage and mixing, while specialized glands supply acid, enzymes, intrinsic factor, and hormones. Mucus-bicarbonate protection and epithelial renewal limit self-injury.
questions.modelAnswer: Rugae permit expansion/reservoir function and sphincters regulate contents. Three fundic muscle directions mix food and enzymes into chyme. Parietal acid helps antibacterial action and intrinsic factor enables B12 absorption; chief pepsinogen/lipase permit digestion; enteroendocrine hormones regulate secretion. Bicarbonate-rich surface mucus/junctions and continuous 4–7-day epithelial renewal protect gastric wall.

questions.text: HIS4: The Pyloric glands
questions.explanation: Pyloric glands occupy the deeper half of the mucosa beneath pits that take up about half its thickness; they are coiled tubular glands.
options: Occupy half of thickness of the corium.

questions.explanation: Chief (peptic) cells have apical zymogen granules containing pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin. Parietal cells instead have acid-secretory canaliculi and abundant mitochondria.

questions.text: 5. Describe the cells line the fundic gland [site-LM, shape, nucleus cytoplasm- EM]
questions.explanation: Fundic glands contain surface/neck mucus, stem, parietal, chief, and enteroendocrine cells; their positions reflect protection, acid/intrinsic-factor secretion, and enzyme release.
questions.modelAnswer: Stem cells in isthmus: short columnar, basal oval nuclei/basophilic cytoplasm and free ribosomes; renew surface/gland epithelium. Surface mucus cells cover surface/pits: columnar, basal oval nuclei, apical PAS-positive mucinogen; RER/Golgi/mitochondria and apical granules with junctional complexes; secrete bicarbonate-rich alkaline insoluble protective mucus. Mucous-neck cells in neck: columnar, basal round nuclei/pale basophilic mucin cytoplasm; RER, Golgi, mitochondria and apical granules; secrete acidic soluble mucus. Chief cells at base: tall columnar, basal rounded nuclei/basal basophilia and apical acidophilic zymogen; abundant RER, Golgi, mitochondria and membrane-bound apical vesicles, junctional complexes; secrete pepsinogen and lipase. Parietal cells in isthmus/neck/base: triangular/round, central round nuclei (sometimes two), deeply acidophilic; intracellular canaliculi/microvilli, tubulovesicular system and abundant mitochondria; Golgi and few RER; secrete HCl and intrinsic factor. Enteroendocrine cells: columnar/triangular with basal round nuclei and narrow apex; RER/Golgi/mitochondria and basal secretory granules; open types reach lumen with microvilli, closed types do not; release hormones into corium/blood.

questions.text: CAVEOLATED CELLS, all true xcept:
questions.explanation: Caveolated cells are uncommon chemosensory epithelial cells with long microvilli and apical membrane invaginations. They are distinct from the isthmus stem cells that renew gastric epithelium.
options: Rare cells in gastric & intestinal mucosa may be chemoreceptor
Their microvilli are long twice the length of those nearby cells
Apical cell membrane shows deep tubular invaginations (Caveolae).

questions.text: Compare between fundic & pyloric glands with special reference to the structure & types of cells
questions.explanation: Fundic glands contain acid- and enzyme-secreting cells; pyloric glands are mainly mucous and have deeper, wider gastric pits.
questions.modelAnswer: Fundic glands in fundus/body: simple branched tubular, straight/perpendicular; narrow short pits occupy quarter mucosal thickness, glands three quarters; stem, surface mucus, neck mucus, chief, parietal and enteroendocrine cells. Pyloric glands: thinner mucosa, wide deep pits half thickness; branched highly coiled tubular glands in remaining half; predominant mucus cells with few parietal, stem and enteroendocrine (EC/D/G) cells. Fundic muscle has three layers (inner oblique, middle circular, outer longitudinal); pylorus has thick inner circular sphincter and outer longitudinal.

questions.text: 42. Which of the following cell types is present in the gastric glands of the pyloric mucosa?
questions.explanation: Pyloric glands are mostly mucus-secreting cells; unlike fundic glands they have few chief cells and parietal cells.

questions.text: 84. Carcinoid tumor , Is tumor of:
questions.explanation: Gastric and intestinal carcinoid (neuroendocrine) tumors arise from enteroendocrine cells, historically grouped as APUD cells. They can release bioactive peptides and amines.

questions.text: 90. PYLORUS OF THE STOMACH all true except:

questions.text: Describe the microscopic structure and correlated function of entero-endocrine cells
questions.explanation: Enteroendocrine cells are basal-granule cells of gastric/intestinal epithelium; open cells sense luminal contents and hormones act locally or through blood.
questions.modelAnswer: Enteroendocrine/APUD cells occur in gastric glands and intestinal mucosa. Columnar/triangular cells with rounded basal nuclei/narrow apex; RER, Golgi, mitochondria and basal granules. Open cells reach lumen with microvilli as chemoreceptors; closed cells remain against basal lamina. Secretions enter corium then act locally (paracrine) or through blood (endocrine). Gastric A/G/D/EC/ECL cells secrete glucagon/gastrin/somatostatin/serotonin/histamine; intestinal G/S/D/Mo/L/N/VIP cells secrete gastrin/secretin/somatostatin/motilin/enteroglucagon/neurotensin/VIP. Silver-reducing cells are argentaffin; EC-cell tumours are carcinoids.

questions.text: 106. The fundic glands:
questions.explanation: Fundic glands are simple branched tubular glands in the mucosa, not the submucosa. Their pits are relatively short, and chief cells are concentrated toward the gland base.

questions.text:

questions.text: In case of atrophic gastritis, deficiency in vitamin B12 result from damage of:
questions.explanation: Parietal cells make intrinsic factor, which binds dietary vitamin B12 for absorption in the terminal ileum. Their loss in atrophic gastritis can therefore cause B12 deficiency.

questions.text: 94. Carcinoid tumor, Is tumor of:

questions.text: Describe the microscopic structure & correlating function of mucus secreting cells of the stomach
questions.explanation: Surface mucous cells line pits and secrete alkaline bicarbonate-rich gel; neck cells secrete soluble acidic mucus. Both lubricate, but the surface gel shields epithelium from acid/pepsin.
questions.modelAnswer: Surface cells cover gastric surface/pits: columnar with basal oval nuclei and apical PAS-positive mucinogen; RER, Golgi, mitochondria, apical granules and junctional complexes. They secrete highly viscous insoluble bicarbonate-rich alkaline mucus making protective acid-resistant gel. Neck cells are columnar with round basal nuclei and pale basophilic mucin cytoplasm; RER/Golgi/mitochondria/apical granules, secreting soluble acidic mucus when stimulated.

questions.text: 49. In malabsorption syndrome the affected cells are:

mucous secreting glands in the duodenum

questions.explanation: Myenteric (Auerbach) plexus coordinates muscularis externa contractions and peristalsis; Meissner plexus mainly regulates secretion and mucosal activity.

questions.text: Give an account on the structure function adaptation of small intestine
questions.explanation: Plicae, villi, and microvilli enlarge absorptive area; crypts renew and secrete, while Paneth/M cells and Peyer patches support defense and motility mixes chyme.
questions.modelAnswer: Absorption is supported by intestinal length, plicae (mucosa/submucosa), villi and enterocyte microvilli. Digestion/mucus depend on incoming pancreatic/liver secretions, crypts and alkaline Brunner glands. Enterocytes and enteroendocrine cells provide enzyme/hormonal secretion. Paneth lysozyme, M-cell antigen transport, caveolated-cell responses and Peyer patches provide defence; smooth muscle/enteric plexuses mix and propel contents.

questions.text: Glycocalyx (cell coat) on microvilli of enterocytes show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The enterocyte glycocalyx contains enzymes and forms a microenvironment for final digestion; its carbohydrate-rich glycoproteins stain with PAS. It does not propel contents or cause peristalsis.
options: Forms special microenvironment for terminal steps of digestion

questions.text: Describe the structure related to function of Membrane like epithelial cells (M- cells). (1/2 mark)
questions.explanation: M cells over Peyer patches have basolateral pockets that carry lymphocytes and macrophages, allowing them to deliver sampled antigens to immune cells.
questions.modelAnswer: M cells are thin dome-shaped cells in ileal follicle-associated epithelium over Peyer patches. They have darker cytoplasm, few apical microvilli and lysosomes, lateral junctional complexes, and basal membrane invaginations/pockets holding lymphocytes and macrophages. They transfer luminal antigen across the cytoplasm to immune cells, initiating an immune response.

questions.text: 20. M cell is characterized by the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: M cells over Peyer patches transcytose luminal antigens to immune cells; Paneth cells, not M cells, secrete lysozyme and defensins.
options: overly the lymphoid follicles of Peyer's patches
their basal membrane invagination contains lymphocytes and macrophages
they are considered as an antigen presenting cell
they secrete lysozyme with antibacterial activity

questions.text: Describe the structure related to function of Enterocytes. (1/2 mark)
questions.explanation: Enterocytes combine apical microvilli and brush-border enzymes for absorption and terminal digestion with mitochondria for active transport. Tight junctions preserve the epithelial barrier, while basolateral membranes transfer absorbed nutrients to blood or lymph.
questions.modelAnswer: Enterocytes are tall columnar absorptive cells over villi and superficial crypts with basal oval nuclei. Apical microvilli with actin cores and terminal web greatly increase absorptive area; the glycocalyx contains enzymes for terminal digestion. Abundant mitochondria supply transport energy; SER supports fatty-acid absorption, and RER/Golgi are well developed. Tight junctions prevent entry between cells, lateral interdigitations enlarge transport membrane, gap junctions permit regulatory communication, and basolateral folds assist nutrient transfer into capillaries.

questions.text: 6. The most prominent organelles in columnar absorptive cells are ___, ___, ___, ___ & ___ their apical surface show ___ & ___ while lateral surface show ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Enterocytes have energy and protein-synthesis organelles, apical microvilli and terminal web, and lateral junctions that support absorption and barrier integrity.
blanks: Lateral interdigitations (with gap junctions between adjacent cells)

questions.text: 42. All about duodenum is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Duodenal villi are broad and leaf-like and submucosa has Brunner glands; large aggregated lymphoid follicles are typical of ileal Peyer patches.
options: Its villi are broad and leaf like
Its lamina Propria contain large lymphocytic aggregations

questions.text: Q8 Evalute the role of frequent goblet cells in intestine
questions.explanation: Goblet-cell abundance rises distally, supplying mucus that lubricates the increasingly solid intestinal contents and protects the colonic lining as feces move toward the rectum.
questions.modelAnswer:
Its proportion increase as we go from the colon to rectum to lubricate the surface of colon
and facilitate the passage of feces

questions.text: 32. The ileum is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Peyer's patches are prominent lymphoid aggregates in ileum, especially its antimesenteric wall, and are covered by antigen-sampling M cells.

questions.text: 15. The duodenal mucosa is protected from the HCl coming from the stomach by
questions.explanation: Brunner glands in duodenal submucosa secrete alkaline mucus that neutralizes acidic gastric chyme and protects duodenal epithelium.
options: mucous secretion of the goblet cells
lysozyme secreted by the paneth cells

questions.text: 27. Which of the following enteroendocrine cells secrete neurotensin?
questions.explanation: Enteroendocrine N cells secrete neurotensin, particularly in the distal small intestine. G, EC, and D cells instead release gastrin, serotonin, and somatostatin, respectively.

questions.text: 12. Membrane like epithelial cells characterized by having:
questions.explanation: M cells over lymphoid follicles contain basal pockets with intraepithelial immune cells, distinguishing them from absorptive enterocytes.

questions.text: Compare between small & Large intestine
questions.explanation: Small intestine has villi, plicae, Paneth cells, Brunner glands (duodenum), and Peyer patches (ileum); colon lacks villi, has many goblet cells, and forms taeniae/haustra.
questions.modelAnswer: Both have mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa and serosa/adventitia. Small bowel has plicae/villi and brush-border absorption, crypts with Paneth and other differentiated/stem cells, duodenal Brunner glands and ileal Peyer patches. Large bowel has no villi, crypts lacking Paneth but many goblet cells, colonocytes/stem/endocrine cells; submucosa lacks glands, outer longitudinal muscle forms taeniae and serosa appendices epiploicae. Colonocytes absorb water; mucus lubricates faeces.

questions.text:
36. Which of the following cells are considered the stem cells of the
small intestine?
questions.explanation: Crypt-base columnar cells are the principal actively cycling stem cells of small-intestinal epithelium. Their progeny differentiate into absorptive and secretory lineages as they migrate up the crypt-villus axis.

questions.text: 33. Intestinal crypts differ from the villi in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Intestinal crypts are epithelial invaginations containing stem cells; villi are projections with connective-tissue cores and lacteals.
options: They are formed of finger like projection of the corium.
Their cores contain smooth muscle fibers.

questions.text: 25. Which statement about the Paneth cell is false?
questions.explanation: Paneth-cell secretory granules are apical; basal cytoplasm is basophilic from rough ER supporting antimicrobial protein synthesis.
options: Present in the base of the crypt
Its secretory granules are basal in position

questions.text: Give short notes on intestinal villus
questions.explanation: A villus is a mucosa projection with an epithelial covering and vascularized lamina-propria core. Capillaries take up water-soluble nutrients, while its central lacteal absorbs dietary lipids.
questions.modelAnswer: Villus is a 0.5–1 mm finger-like luminal projection with epithelium over lamina-propria core. Core has reticular areolar tissue, lacteal, smooth muscle, fenestrated blood capillary network and immune cells. Epithelium includes enterocytes, goblet, enteroendocrine and M cells. Villi/microvilli enlarge absorption area; lacteal transports fat and core muscle moves villus.

questions.text: 26. Which of the following enteroendocrine cells secrete motilin?
questions.explanation: Intestinal Mo (M) endocrine cells secrete motilin, which promotes interdigestive migrating motor activity.

questions.text: 7. The goblet cell, BY LM: its shape is ___ nucleus is ___, cytoplasm appear ___
questions.explanation: Goblet cells have a cup-shaped mucin-filled apical region and flattened basal nucleus; mucin appears pale because it washes out during routine staining.
blanks: Goblet-shaped: expanded apex and thin basal cylindrical part
Clear apical mucin region and basophilic basal part

questions.text: 11. The M cell is present in ___, their apical surface show ___, lateral surface shows ___ while basal surface show ___ Its function is ___
questions.explanation: M cells over Peyer patches sample luminal antigens and deliver them to immune cells in basal pockets, linking the gut lumen to mucosal immune surveillance.
blanks: Transport luminal antigens to immune cells to initiate immune responses

questions.text: 13. The most prominent ultrastructure of crypt base columnar cells is:
questions.explanation: Crypt-base stem cells have abundant free ribosomes, reflecting active protein synthesis during rapid renewal of intestinal epithelium.

questions.text: Give short account on intestinal glands, describe the microscopic  structure of the cell that characterizes the small from the large intestine
questions.explanation: Intestinal crypts are simple tubular glands containing absorptive, goblet, stem, enteroendocrine, and Paneth cells; Paneth cells at the crypt base secrete lysozyme/defensins and distinguish small bowel from colon.
questions.modelAnswer: Crypts of Lieberkuhn are simple tubular glands occupying full corium thickness between villi. Lining: enterocytes, goblet, oligomucous, Paneth, enteroendocrine, crypt-base columnar stem, caveolated/tuft and M cells. The distinguishing cell is Paneth cell (absent from large-intestinal crypts): Paneth cells lie at crypt bases. Pyramidal cells with indistinct boundaries, basal oval nuclei and basophilic striated basal cytoplasm; acidophilic apical granules. EM: abundant RER, prominent Golgi and large apical membrane-bound zymogen granules. They secrete lysozyme and antimicrobial cryptidins to control intestinal flora.

questions.text: 3. M cells are found in the mucosa of:
questions.explanation: M cells are specialized epithelial cells of the small intestine, especially over Peyer patches in the ileum. They transcytose luminal antigens to underlying immune cells.

questions.text: HIS7: Which one of the following is characteristic feature to Paneth cells?
questions.explanation: Paneth cells reside at crypt bases, where their antimicrobial granules help control microbial populations near intestinal stem cells.
options: They line the base of intestinal glands.

questions.text:
8. Asses the value of:
M-CELL in the intestine
Numerous SER in enterocytes
Lymphatic vessel in core of villi
Smooth muscle in core of villi
Thick cell coat on the enterocytes
Brunner's gland in duodenum
Paneth cell in intestinal gland
Numerous goblet cells in rectum.
questions.explanation: M cells sample antigens; enterocyte SER handles lipid uptake; villus lacteals carry fat and core muscle moves villi. Glycocalyx enzymes finish digestion, Brunner mucus neutralizes acid, Paneth antimicrobials defend crypts, and rectal goblet mucus lubricates stool.
questions.modelAnswer: M cells transport luminal antigens to lymphocytes/macrophages. Enterocyte SER participates in fatty-acid absorption. Villus lacteals transport absorbed fat; core smooth muscle moves villi. Thick enterocyte glycocalyx carries terminal digestive enzymes. Brunner glands secrete alkaline mucus to neutralize acidic chyme. Paneth cells secrete bactericidal lysozyme/antimicrobial peptides. questions.text: Brunner’s glands show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Brunner glands secrete alkaline mucus and urogastrone; lysozyme is classically associated with Paneth cells rather than these glands.
options: Secrete alkaline mucous to protect duodenum against acidity.

questions.text:
3. The absorptive surface of the small intestine is increased by the presence of all the
     following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Rugae are temporary folds of the stomach that flatten as it distends; small-intestinal plicae, villi, and microvilli instead increase absorptive area.

questions.text:
38. A patient came to the clinic suffering from severe diarrhea and
weight loss. After investigation he was diagnosed as having
nutritional deficiency causing malabsorption. Biopsy is taken from
his small intestine. Which of the following structures would likely
be affected?
questions.explanation: Nutrient absorption occurs across the small-intestinal mucosa, where villi, enterocytes, and brush-border enzymes reside. Damage there can cause both malabsorption and diarrhea.

questions.text: 15. The duodenal mucosa is protected from the HCI coming from the stomach by
questions.explanation: Brunner glands release alkaline mucus from the duodenal submucosa, buffering incoming gastric acid and protecting the proximal small intestine.
options: mucous secretion of the goblet cells
lysozyme secreted by the paneth cells

questions.text: 4. Plica circularis are
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are permanent folds of mucosa and submucosa in the small intestine, unlike the muscle-only circular layer.
options: Circular mucosal folds of small intestine
the inner circular muscle layer of small intestine
The outer longitudinal layer of large intestine

questions.text: 13. M cells are found in the
questions.explanation: M cells are specialized epithelial cells of the ileum, especially over Peyer patches, where they transport luminal antigens to underlying immune cells.

questions.text: The jejunum contains which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Jejunum has prominent plicae circulares that increase absorptive surface; Peyer patches are a defining ileal feature.

questions.text:
28. Which of the following cells decrease peristaltic action of small and
large intestine?
questions.explanation: N cells release neurotensin, which increases ileal blood flow and reduces small- and large-intestinal peristalsis. This contrasts with enterochromaffin serotonin, which tends to promote motility.

questions.text: 74. M cell is characterized by the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: M cells transport antigens to immune cells but do not secrete lysozyme; Paneth cells release lysozyme and other antimicrobial peptides at crypt bases.
options: overly the lymphoid follicles of Peyer’s patches
their basal membrane invagination contains lymphocytes and macrophages
they are considered as an antigen presenting cell
they secrete lysozyme with antibacterial activity

questions.text: 2. Mention the lining cells of intestinal gland & describe one of them
questions.explanation: Paneth cells at crypt bases release lysozyme and defensins; their apical granules are acidophilic and rich in antimicrobial proteins.
questions.modelAnswer: Crypts of Lieberkuhn are simple tubular glands occupying full corium thickness between villi. Lining: enterocytes, goblet, oligomucous, Paneth, enteroendocrine, crypt-base columnar stem, caveolated/tuft and M cells. Paneth cells lie at crypt bases. Pyramidal cells with indistinct boundaries, basal oval nuclei and basophilic striated basal cytoplasm; acidophilic apical granules. EM: abundant RER, prominent Golgi and large apical membrane-bound zymogen granules. They secrete lysozyme and antimicrobial cryptidins to control intestinal flora.

questions.text: Brunner’s glands show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Brunner glands occupy duodenal submucosa and secrete alkaline mucus/urogastrone; brush-border disaccharidases are produced by enterocytes.
options: Secrete alkaline mucous to protect duodenum against acidity.

questions.text: 40. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of membrane-like epithelial cells?
questions.explanation: M cells have basal pockets or invaginations containing lymphocytes and macrophages. This arrangement supports antigen transfer from the lumen to immune cells beneath the epithelium.
options: They are most numerous in the jejunum
They are present at the base of the crypts

questions.text: 3. The Paneth cell, BY LM: its shape is ___ nucleus is ___, cytoplasm appear ___
questions.explanation: Paneth cells are pyramidal with a basal oval nucleus; abundant basal RER stains blue, while apical zymogen granules stain pink.
blanks: Basophilic basally with apical acidophilic zymogen granules

questions.text: 44. The villi over the Payer's patches are characterized by being...
questions.explanation: Villi over ileal Peyer patches are short and flattened, creating the dome over lymphoid tissue rather than long absorptive projections.

questions.text: 52. All about Paneth cell is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Paneth cells are characteristic of small-intestinal crypts, especially ileum, not large-intestinal mucosa; they secrete antimicrobial products.
options: Are present in the base of crypts in large intestinal mucosa
Their life span about 30-40 days.[long lived]

questions.text: 30. The enterocytes are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Enterocyte lateral interdigitations increase contact and support transport between neighboring cells; basal infoldings are not the defining feature here.

questions.text: 4. Describe the changes take place in pyloroduodenal junction, rectoanal junction
questions.explanation: At the pyloroduodenal junction, gastric pits and pyloric glands give way to intestinal villi and crypts, with Brunner glands in duodenal submucosa. At the rectoanal junction, columnar lining transitions through stratified epithelia to keratinized skin, and rectal muscle and venous plexuses adapt toward continence.
questions.modelAnswer: Pyloric → duodenal: villi appear; intestinal crypts replace pyloric glands; enterocyte brush border and goblet cells appear; muscularis mucosa continues; Brunner glands appear in submucosa; serosa continues. Rectoanal: Simple columnar proximally → stratified columnar transitional zone → nonkeratinized stratified squamous → keratinized perianal skin; muscularis mucosa subdivides/disappears at rectal columns, submucosa fuses with lamina propria and shows venous plexuses; inner circular thickens as internal sphincter; outer longitudinal passes between sphincters and becomes connective tissue.

questions.text: Content of core of the villous
questions.explanation: A villus core contains loose connective tissue, vessels and immune cells, a central lacteal, and smooth-muscle extensions from muscularis mucosae.
questions.modelAnswer: Areolar connective tissue with reticular fibres, central lymphatic lacteal, smooth muscle from muscularis mucosa, arterial/subepithelial fenestrated capillaries and plasma cells/macrophages/lymphocytes.

questions.text: 32. Intestinal villi differ from the crypts in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Villi are mucosal projections, not tubular glands; their lamina propria contains a central lacteal, smooth muscle, and capillaries, unlike crypts.
options: They are formed of simple tubular glands.
They occupy the whole thickness of the corium

questions.text: 48. (M CELLS) show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: M cells sample luminal contents and occur over lymphoid follicles, including in ileum and appendix. Their key role is antigen transport; antigen presentation is carried out by underlying immune cells.
options: Are found in the epith lining ileum & appendix

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Villi project into the lumen of small intestine to increase absorptive area; colon instead has straight crypts and no villi.

questions.text: 26. The absorption in the small intestine is augmented by:
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares enlarge the mucosal surface and slow chyme, complementing villi and microvilli in intestinal absorption.

questions.text: 27. The Intestinal Villi are lined by one of the following cells:
questions.explanation: Villus epithelium is mainly enterocytes with interspersed goblet and enteroendocrine cells. Parietal and chief cells are gastric gland cells, not intestinal lining cells.

questions.text: 31. The Microfold cells are:
questions.explanation: M cells transport luminal antigens across follicle-associated epithelium to immune cells, initiating mucosal immune surveillance.

questions.text: 16. Intestinal villi are characterized by
questions.explanation: Villus cores contain connective tissue, capillaries, a central lacteal, and smooth muscle; this vascular-lymphatic core supports nutrient uptake.
options: A decrease in the number of goblet cells as descend in the intestine
Central core of CT contains lymphatic vessels & smooth muscle
Covering cells are Paneth cell & stem cell
Being long & slender in the ileum region

questions.text: 17. What is the MOST prominent feature of the apical surface of the epithelial M cells
questions.explanation: M cells have a reduced brush border with short folds rather than the dense, tall microvilli and glycocalyx of absorptive enterocytes. This surface suits antigen sampling.

questions.text: 33. One of the following is true concerning the duodenum:
questions.explanation: The duodenum is about 25 cm long; it also has villi, goblet cells, and Brunner glands, while Peyer patches typify ileum.

questions.text: 13. Structural factors of small intestine that help it in absorption are ___, ___, ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Length, plicae, villi, and brush-border microvilli progressively amplify small-intestinal surface area for absorption.

questions.text: 4. The most prominent EM features of Paneth cells are ___, ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Paneth cells have abundant rough ER and Golgi to synthesize antimicrobial proteins, then store them in large apical secretory granules for release into the crypt.

questions.text: 24. Which of the following structures or cells is ABSENT from the ileum?
questions.explanation: Brunner glands are located in duodenal submucosa, not ileum; ileal mucosa can contain Peyer patches, M cells, and Paneth cells.

questions.text:
39. Which of the following cells are present overlying the Payer's
patches of the ileum, they are dome shaped with basal cavities and
act as antigen transport cells?
questions.explanation: M cells over Peyer patches transcytose luminal antigens to underlying immune cells; their dome-like location distinguishes them from absorptive enterocytes.

questions.text: 2. The submucosa of jejunum contains:
questions.explanation: Jejunal submucosa is connective tissue containing vessels and nerves but lacks the regional specializations of duodenum (Brunner glands) and ileum (Peyer patches).

questions.text: 75. Each of the following statements about Brenner's gland is CORRECT EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Brunner glands are duodenal submucosal mucous glands that empty into crypts; they do not produce enzyme-rich serous secretion.
options: They are characteristic component of the duodenal wall
Produce serous secretion rich in digestive enzyme
They lie in the submucosal layer
They empty their secretion into the crypts of Lieberkühn

questions.text: 5. The intestinal villi are lined with all the following cells EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Paneth cells reside at crypt bases, not on villi; villi are covered mainly by enterocytes and goblet cells with scattered enteroendocrine cells.

questions.text: 18. Absorptive cells of the small intestine
questions.explanation: Enterocytes line the small intestine, bear apical microvilli, and reassemble absorbed fatty acids into triglycerides. These shared features make “all of the above” correct.
options: they are covered on their apical surface by many microvilli
use absorbed lipid to synthesize triglycerides

questions.text:
21. At which site the Gut associated lymphatic tissues "GALT" is
present in the wall of the gastrointestinal tract?
questions.explanation: GALT is concentrated in the mucosa, particularly lamina propria and lymphoid follicles, where it samples antigens from the gut lumen.

questions.text:
37. Oligomucus cells are less differentiated form of which of the
following cells?
questions.explanation: Oligomucus cells are immature, less mucin-rich forms in the goblet-cell lineage; differentiation increases their mucus-secreting specialization.

questions.text: 76. Which of the following structures is absent from the ilium?
questions.explanation: The ileum lacks Brunner glands, which are specific to duodenal submucosa. It still contains Paneth and goblet cells, and Peyer patches are especially prominent there.

questions.text: 9. the structure of enterocytes that responsible for enzyme secretion:
questions.explanation: Golgi apparatus packages newly synthesized proteins and enzymes for secretion; microvilli instead increase absorption and host brush-border enzymes.

questions.text: 10. The organelle which plays an important role in the absorption of lipid is:
questions.explanation: Smooth ER participates in intracellular lipid processing and triglyceride reassembly during enterocyte fat absorption; lysosomes digest material instead.

questions.text: Give short notes on submucosa of small intestine
questions.explanation: Small-intestinal submucosa is connective tissue with blood and lymphatic vessels and nerves. Brunner glands specialize the duodenum, while aggregated Peyer patches characterize the ileum.
questions.modelAnswer: Small-intestinal submucosa is loose CT with vessels, lymphatics and nerves. Proximal duodenum has Brunner mucus glands opening to crypt bottoms, secreting alkaline mucus. Ileum has Peyer lymphoid patches from lamina propria into submucosa, with short/absent villi and M cells above. Jejunal submucosa lacks these glands and patches.

questions.text: The structure related to function of enterocyte/ M-cell
questions.explanation: Enterocytes absorb nutrients and complete terminal digestion at their brush border, while M cells sample and transport antigens to immune cells.
questions.modelAnswer: Enterocytes occur over villi and superficial crypts: tall columnar cells, basal oval nuclei and striated brush border. EM: abundant mitochondria, SER for fatty-acid absorption, RER/Golgi and few free ribosomes; apical microvilli with actin cores and terminal web increase absorptive area, and glycocalyx enzymes perform terminal digestion. Tight junctions prevent paracellular entry; lateral interdigitations enlarge transport surface, gap junctions allow regulation, basal folds facilitate nutrient transfer to blood. They absorb digested food and secrete terminal digestive enzymes. M cells lie in ileal epithelium above Peyer patches: thin dome-shaped/darker cells, few apical microvilli/lysosomes, lateral junctional complexes and basal pockets holding lymphocytes/macrophages. They transport luminal antigens to immune cells.

questions.text: 42. Enterocytes are characterized by which of the followings?
questions.explanation: Enterocytes are columnar absorptive cells whose lateral interdigitations strengthen cell contact and facilitate exchange across the epithelium.
options: Their free borders are covered by cilia.

questions.text:
34. Which of the following cells are specifically present in the crypt of
the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Paneth cells are found at the bases of small-intestinal crypts, where antimicrobial peptides and lysozyme help regulate microbes and protect the stem-cell niche.

questions.text: 10. Peptidase enzyme in small intestine is secreted by:
questions.explanation: Brush-border peptidases are synthesized and released by enterocytes, completing protein digestion at the small-intestinal epithelial surface.

questions.text: 7. Which of the following is FALSE concerning the intestinal villi?
questions.explanation: The large intestine lacks villi; its flat mucosa instead has straight crypts, whereas villi are characteristic of small intestine.
options: they are found in the large intestine
they are composed of epithelium and lamina propria

questions.text: 9. Paneth cells are associated with which of the following glands?
questions.explanation: Paneth cells are specialized epithelial cells at the base of small-intestinal glands (crypts of Lieberkühn), not gastric or esophageal glands.

questions.text: HIS7: Which one of the following is characteristic feature to Paneth cells?
questions.explanation: Paneth cells sit at the bases of Lieberkühn crypts, where they release antimicrobial granules; they do not cover villi.
options: They line the base of intestinal glands.

questions.text: 3. Describe how structure of small intestine is correlated to its function
questions.explanation: Intestinal length and the folds, villi, and microvilli expand absorptive area; crypt secretions, specialized cells, and motility add digestion, defense, and propulsion.
questions.modelAnswer: Absorption is supported by intestinal length, plicae (mucosa/submucosa), villi and enterocyte microvilli. Digestion/mucus depend on incoming pancreatic/liver secretions, crypts and alkaline Brunner glands. Enterocytes and enteroendocrine cells provide enzyme/hormonal secretion. Paneth lysozyme, M-cell antigen transport, caveolated-cell responses and Peyer patches provide defence; smooth muscle/enteric plexuses mix and propel contents.

questions.text: 22. The enteroendocrine cells differ than other cells covering the intestinal villi by having:
questions.explanation: Enteroendocrine cells release their hormones from basal granules toward the lamina propria, where they can signal locally or enter the circulation.

questions.text: Plicea circularis (valves of kerkring) are:
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are circular folds of mucosa and submucosa that slow chyme and increase the small intestine's absorptive surface.
options: Circular folds of intestinal mucosa with core formed of submucosa.
Are mucosal folds found in fundus of stomach.
Are bundles of circular smooth muscles at recto-anal junction
Valves found in the anal canal.

questions.text: 28. One of the following is true concerning the Paneth cells:
questions.explanation: Paneth cells contain apical eosinophilic granules rich in antimicrobial products such as defensins and lysozyme, unlike endocrine secretory cells.

questions.text: 40. Paneth cells are characterized by which of the followings?
questions.explanation: Paneth cells are pyramidal crypt-base cells with eosinophilic apical granules containing antimicrobial products. Their apical pole reaches the crypt lumen.

questions.text: 1. The core of intestinal villi contains ___, ___ & ___
questions.explanation: A villus core contains loose connective tissue with vessels and immune cells, a central lacteal, and smooth-muscle fibers from the muscularis mucosae.
blanks: Areolar connective tissue with reticular fibres, vascular/immune components

questions.text: 44. Intestinal villi contain the following except:
questions.explanation: Villi contain vessels and absorptive/endocrine epithelium, while Paneth cells are restricted to crypt bases rather than villus surfaces.
options: Central lacteal lymph vessels for fat absorption

questions.text: 5. Compare between different parts of small intestine
questions.explanation: Duodenum is recognized by Brunner glands, jejunum by prominent plicae and tall villi, and ileum by Peyer patches with overlying M cells. These regional structures help identify sections.
questions.modelAnswer: Duodenum: broad leaf-like villi, proximal submucosal Brunner mucus glands, no submucosal Peyer patches. Jejunum: long slender villi and developed plicae; submucosa lacks Brunner glands/Peyer patches. Ileum: Peyer patches extending between lamina propria and submucosa, short/absent villi above them and M-cell surface epithelium.

questions.text: 10. The Crypt base columnar cell, BY LM: its shape is ___ nucleus is ___, cytoplasm appear ___ and the most prominent organelle is ___
questions.explanation: Crypt-base columnar cells are short, with a basal rounded nucleus, basophilic cytoplasm, and abundant free ribosomes that support rapid epithelial renewal.

questions.text: 45. The duodenum is characterized by...
questions.explanation: Duodenal submucosa contains Brunner glands, whose alkaline secretion helps neutralize acidic gastric chyme entering the intestine.

its submucosa contains mucus secreting glands.

questions.text:
41. Which of the followings characterizes the crypt base columnar
cells of the intestine?

questions.text: The following cells are involved in carbohydrates digestion & absorption EXCEPT:

questions.text: 29. The APUD cells of the intestine are characterized by:

questions.text: 19. Chylomicrons ,in enterocytes, is finally formed in

questions.text: 46. Jejunum is characterized by....

its submucosa contains mucus secreting glands.

questions.text: 1. Cell cover the intestinal villi is:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are interspersed among villus enterocytes and release mucus to lubricate and protect the intestinal surface.

questions.text: 8. The most prominent organelles in goblet cells are ___, ___, ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Goblet cells synthesize mucin on rough ER, process it through Golgi, and secrete it in apical electron-lucent granules. Mitochondria support this secretory activity.

questions.text: Characteristic features of duodenum/ jejunum / ileum
questions.explanation: Duodenum has Brunner glands; jejunum has long slender villi and prominent plicae; ileum has Peyer patches and associated M cells, with shorter villi.
questions.modelAnswer: Duodenum: broad leaf-like villi, proximal submucosal Brunner mucus glands, no submucosal Peyer patches. Jejunum: long slender villi and developed plicae; submucosa lacks Brunner glands/Peyer patches. Ileum: Peyer patches extending between lamina propria and submucosa, short/absent villi above them and M-cell surface epithelium.

questions.text: 18. Which of the following changes in pyloroduodenal junction is true
questions.explanation: At the pyloroduodenal junction, Brunner glands begin in the duodenal submucosa; the stomach lacks these glands.
options: The epithelium changed from stratified squamoua to simple columnar

questions.text: Peyer,s patches are:

Present in the antimesenteric border of ilium
Covered by complete layer of muscularis mucosa

questions.text: 2. The cells covering the intestinal villi are ___, ___, ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Villus epithelium contains absorptive enterocytes, mucus-secreting goblet cells, enteroendocrine cells, and M cells that sample antigens.

questions.text: 49. Which of the followings characterizes the transition from the pylorus to the duodenum?
questions.explanation: Goblet cells first appear among small-intestinal surface epithelium beyond the pylorus, alongside enterocytes and scattered enteroendocrine cells.
options: Addition of inner oblique layer of muscularis mucosa.
Cardiac glands appear at the submucosa.
Appearance of M cells among the surface epithelium.

questions.text:
31. Plicae circularis of the small intestine involves which of the
following layers?
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are permanent folds formed by both mucosa and submucosa. Villi project only from mucosa, while circular folds increase absorptive surface area.

questions.text: Describe villous epithelium
questions.explanation: Villi are covered by absorptive enterocytes, goblet, enteroendocrine, and M cells. Enterocyte microvilli and glycocalyx increase absorption and complete digestion; tight junctions preserve the barrier, goblet cells secrete mucus, and M cells transport antigens to immune cells.
questions.modelAnswer: Villus epithelium has enterocytes, goblet cells, enteroendocrine and M cells. Enterocytes occur over villi and superficial crypts: tall columnar cells, basal oval nuclei and striated brush border. EM: abundant mitochondria, SER for fatty-acid absorption, RER/Golgi and few free ribosomes; apical microvilli with actin cores and terminal web increase absorptive area, and glycocalyx enzymes perform terminal digestion. Tight junctions prevent paracellular entry; lateral interdigitations enlarge transport surface, gap junctions allow regulation, basal folds facilitate nutrient transfer to blood. They absorb digested food and secrete terminal digestive enzymes. Goblet cells have expanded apical mucin region and narrow basal cytoplasm/oval dark nucleus, with RER/Golgi/mitochondria and pale granules for mucus. Endocrine cells deliver hormones; M cells transport antigens to underlying immune cells.

questions.text: 43. Bruner's glands are present at...
questions.explanation: Brunner glands lie in the duodenal submucosa, a regional landmark distinguishing duodenum from jejunum and ileum.

questions.text: 25. Histological examination of a biopsy from digestive tract shows short finger like projection with mucosal tubular glands and permanent localized aggregation of lymphatic nodules extends to the submucosa. This biopsy could be from

questions.text: transverse corrugations of the large intestinal wall is due to:
