questions.explanation: The space of Disse is perisinusoidal and contains plasma, stellate cells, and hepatocyte microvilli; circulating blood cells remain within sinusoids.

questions.text: Give an account on microscopic structure of hepatocytes
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes are polygonal metabolic cells with sinusoidal, canalicular, and lateral surfaces; organelles support protein synthesis, detoxification, exchange, and bile secretion.
questions.modelAnswer: Hepatocytes are large polygonal cells in anastomosing plates. LM: acidophilic cytoplasm from mitochondria/SER, lipid/glycogen vacuolation and RER basophilic granules; central spherical vesicular nuclei with nucleoli, often binucleate/tetraploid. Sinusoidal surface has many microvilli for exchange in Disse; canalicular surface short microvilli for bile secretion; adjacent-cell surfaces have junctional complexes/desmosomes. EM: abundant mitochondria, RER/free ribosomes, SER, Golgi, lysosomes/peroxisomes, cytoskeletal filaments, glycogen/lipid and lipofuscin. RER/ribosomes synthesize proteins, SER supplies lipid components and detoxification, Golgi/vesicles package secretions; peroxisomal oxidase/catalase detoxify alcohol; mitochondria provide energy. Bile is exocrine secretion; plasma proteins/lipoproteins enter blood via Disse; glycogen, vitamins, iron/copper and lipid are stored.

questions.text: 5. The liver blood sinusoids are lined by:

questions.text: Give an account on hepatic blood sinusoids
questions.explanation: Sinusoids carry mixed portal and arterial blood toward central veins; fenestrated endothelium and Kupffer cells border the channel, with Disse outside.
questions.modelAnswer: Sinusoids are irregular vascular channels between hepatic plates, carrying portal/hepatic arterial blood toward central veins opposite bile flow. Lining: fenestrated endothelial cells and Kupffer macrophages on discontinuous basal lamina. Endothelial sieve plates lack diaphragms and intercellular gaps permit plasma passage to Disse. Kupffer cells are monocyte-derived branched cells with irregular nuclei; EM shows pseudopodia/microvilli, lysosomes, phagocytic/pinocytic vesicles and stored iron particles. They phagocytose microbes and senile RBCs to form bile pigments. Space of Disse lies between sinusoidal lining and hepatocytes and contains filtered plasma, hepatocyte microvilli, type III collagen reticular fibres and vitamin-A-storing Ito cells. It supports sinusoidal architecture, prevents collapse and permits blood–hepatocyte exchange. Ito cells secrete matrix and may become collagen-producing myofibroblasts in fibrosis.

questions.text: 17. Hepatocytes possess all the following surfaces EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes have sinusoidal surfaces facing blood, canalicular surfaces forming bile channels, and intercellular surfaces contacting neighbors. “Portal surface” is not one of the recognized surface domains.

questions.text: Give short notes on Ito cells
questions.explanation: Hepatic stellate cells lie in the space of Disse, store retinoids, and produce collagen when activated during chronic liver injury.
questions.modelAnswer: Ito (hepatic stellate/fat-storing) cells lie in Disse, store vitamin A and secrete extracellular matrix. In pathological conditions such as cirrhosis they become myofibroblasts synthesizing collagen, causing fibrosis and impaired exchange.

questions.text: 17. Ito cells characterized by

questions.text: 87. The space of Disse is

questions.text: Describe the structure of portal lobule/ liver acinus / space of Disse
questions.explanation: The portal lobule is triangular around a bile duct; the acinus is diamond-shaped with perfusion zones, and the space of Disse is the exchange gap between sinusoidal lining and hepatocytes.
questions.modelAnswer: Portal lobule: triangular mass from three classic lobules, central portal area/bile duct and central veins at corners; expresses bile drainage opposite blood flow. Liver acinus is diamond-shaped tissue from two adjacent classic lobules, extending from two portal tracts to two nearest central veins. Central core contains portal-vein/hepatic-artery branches. Zone I is nearest, best supplied, oxidative/protein synthetic; zone II intermediate; zone III furthest/near central veins, least oxygen/nutrients, rich SER for glycolysis/lipid formation/detoxification and first in ischaemic/fatty injury. Space of Disse lies between sinusoidal lining and hepatocytes and contains filtered plasma, hepatocyte microvilli, type III collagen reticular fibres and vitamin-A-storing Ito cells. It supports sinusoidal architecture, prevents collapse and permits blood–hepatocyte exchange. Ito cells secrete matrix and may become collagen-producing myofibroblasts in fibrosis.

questions.text: 10. Describe the structure of hepatic blood sinusoids with reference to space of Disse
questions.explanation: Sinusoids carry mixed portal and arterial blood toward central veins; Kupffer macrophages line their lumen, while Ito cells occupy Disse.
questions.modelAnswer: Sinusoids are irregular vascular channels between hepatic plates, carrying portal/hepatic arterial blood toward central veins opposite bile flow. Lining: fenestrated endothelial cells and Kupffer macrophages on discontinuous basal lamina. Endothelial sieve plates lack diaphragms and intercellular gaps permit plasma passage to Disse. Kupffer cells are monocyte-derived branched cells with irregular nuclei; EM shows pseudopodia/microvilli, lysosomes, phagocytic/pinocytic vesicles and stored iron particles. They phagocytose microbes and senile RBCs to form bile pigments. Space of Disse lies between sinusoidal lining and hepatocytes and contains filtered plasma, hepatocyte microvilli, type III collagen reticular fibres and vitamin-A-storing Ito cells. It supports sinusoidal architecture, prevents collapse and permits blood–hepatocyte exchange. Ito cells secrete matrix and may become collagen-producing myofibroblasts in fibrosis.

questions.text: Give an account on the structure of classic hepatic lobule
questions.explanation: A classic lobule has hepatocyte plates arranged around a central vein, with portal triads at its periphery. Blood flows inward through sinusoids; bile canaliculi drain outward toward ducts.
questions.modelAnswer: Classic hepatic lobule is hexagonal/pentagonal with central vein and peripheral portal tracts containing hepatic arterial, portal venous and bile-duct branches plus lymphatics. Hepatocytes form branching one-cell-thick plates (may be two in young individuals), separated by endothelial/Kupffer-lined sinusoids with Disse outside. Bile canaliculi lie between hepatocytes. Blood flows portal areas → sinusoids → central vein; bile flows oppositely.

questions.text: 9. Describe the structure of hepatocytes with correlation to its function
questions.explanation: Hepatocyte polarity and organelles support multiple roles: sinusoidal microvilli exchange with plasma, canaliculi secrete bile, and RER/SER process proteins and lipids.
questions.modelAnswer: Hepatocytes are large polygonal cells in anastomosing plates. LM: acidophilic cytoplasm from mitochondria/SER, lipid/glycogen vacuolation and RER basophilic granules; central spherical vesicular nuclei with nucleoli, often binucleate/tetraploid. Sinusoidal surface has many microvilli for exchange in Disse; canalicular surface short microvilli for bile secretion; adjacent-cell surfaces have junctional complexes/desmosomes. EM: abundant mitochondria, RER/free ribosomes, SER, Golgi, lysosomes/peroxisomes, cytoskeletal filaments, glycogen/lipid and lipofuscin. RER/ribosomes synthesize proteins, SER supplies lipid components and detoxification, Golgi/vesicles package secretions; peroxisomal oxidase/catalase detoxify alcohol; mitochondria provide energy. Bile is exocrine secretion; plasma proteins/lipoproteins enter blood via Disse; glycogen, vitamins, iron/copper and lipid are stored.

questions.explanation: The canal of Hering is the transition from hepatocyte-lined canaliculi to cholangiocyte-lined ductules, so its wall includes both cell types.
options: Partially by hepatocytes and partially by cholangiocytes.

questions.text: 92. Canals of Herring
questions.explanation: Canals of Hering connect canaliculi to interlobular bile ducts and are lined partly by cholangiocytes, typically simple cuboidal cells.
options: They are spaces between two hepatocytes
Microvilli of hepatocytes project into them

questions.text: 25. Which of the following is TRUE about the lining of the common hepatic duct?
questions.explanation: Large extrahepatic bile ducts are lined by columnar epithelium, whereas smaller ducts are cuboidal and canals of Hering are transitional.
options: Partially by hepatocytes and partially by cuboidal cells.

questions.text: 46. The gall bladder is lined with:
questions.explanation: The gallbladder mucosa is lined by simple columnar absorptive cells without goblet cells. Their microvilli help concentrate stored bile by absorbing water and electrolytes.
options: Simple col. epith. with goblet cells

questions.text: All about Bile is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes produce bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it, then CCK promotes its release into the duodenum.
options: Discharged into duodenum under effect of cholecystokinin.

questions.text: Give an account on intrahepatic biliary passages
questions.explanation: Bile passes from canaliculi to canals of Hering, then ductules and larger hepatic ducts, before reaching common and cystic ducts.
questions.modelAnswer: Intrahepatic: bile canaliculi are hepatocyte-membrane channels with short microvilli and sealed junctional complexes; canals of Herring are lined partly by hepatocytes/partly cuboidal cells; preductules/ductules by cuboidal cells; portal interlobular ducts by cuboidal becoming columnar epithelium in larger ducts.

questions.text: 40. The interlobular bile ducts are lined by:
questions.explanation: Small interlobular bile ducts are lined by simple cuboidal cholangiocytes; larger ducts become columnar. This lining is distinct from hepatocyte-formed canaliculi.

questions.text: 27. Which of the following is TRUE about the lining of the common bile duct?
questions.explanation: The common bile duct has a tall columnar epithelial lining with connective tissue and smooth muscle supporting the larger passage.
options: Partially by hepatocytes and partially by cuboidal cells.

questions.text:
20. Which of the following order of biliary passages is TRUE,
starting from within the liver?
questions.explanation: Bile flows from canaliculi into canals of Hering, then ductules and larger hepatic ducts; extrahepatic ducts carry it onward to the duodenum.
options: Bile canaliculi, canals of Hering, bile duct and cystic duct.
Canal of Hering, bile canaliculi, cystic duct and bile duct.
Bile duct, canals of Hering, bile canaliculi and cystic duct.
cystic duct, canals of Hering, bile canaliculi and bile duct.
Cystic duct, bile duct, canals of Hering, and bile canaliculi.

questions.text: 69. The gall bladder is lined with
questions.explanation: Gallbladder lining is simple columnar epithelium specialized for absorption and bile concentration. Goblet cells and stratified epithelia are not typical.

questions.text: 20. The gall bladder is lined by ___ and their cells show apical ___, lateral ___, and basal ___ indicating active water absorption.
questions.explanation: Gallbladder tall columnar cells absorb water through microvilli and basal infoldings, while junctional complexes prevent leakage between cells.

questions.text: 93. The canals of Herring are lined by:
questions.explanation: Canals of Hering are transitional channels with cuboidal cholangiocytes alongside hepatocytes, linking canaliculi to the duct system.

questions.text: 114. The epithelial lining of Gall bladder is:
questions.explanation: Gallbladder epithelium is simple columnar and absorbs water and electrolytes to concentrate bile. It normally lacks goblet cells.

questions.text: 38. Canals of Hering
questions.explanation: Canals of Hering have a cuboidal cholangiocyte component, connecting hepatocyte canaliculi to the intrahepatic bile duct system.
options: They are spaces between two hepatocytes
Microvilli of hepatocytes project into them

questions.text: 24. Which of the following is TRUE about the lining of the large bile ducts?
questions.explanation: Large bile ducts are lined by columnar epithelium; smaller intrahepatic ducts are cuboidal and the canals of Hering are transitional.
options: Partially by hepatocytes and partially by cuboidal cells.

questions.text: 28. Lining epithelium of the gall bladder is:
questions.explanation: Tall simple columnar cells line the gallbladder and concentrate bile by absorbing water and salts. Goblet cells are not a normal feature of this lining.
options: Pseudo stratified columnar with goblet cells.

questions.text: Give an account on extrahepatic biliary passages
questions.explanation: Right and left hepatic ducts unite as the common hepatic duct; the cystic duct joins it to form the common bile duct, which opens into the duodenum at the ampulla under sphincter of Oddi control.
questions.modelAnswer: Right and left hepatic ducts leave liver and join as common hepatic duct; cystic duct connects gallbladder; common bile duct enters duodenum at ampulla. Right/left hepatic and common hepatic/common bile ducts have simple tall columnar lining and CT with elastic/smooth-muscle support. Cystic duct carries bile in/out of gallbladder; gallbladder itself has tall columnar mucosa. Oddi sphincter regulates ampullary flow.

questions.text: 39. The canals of Hering are lined by:
questions.explanation: Canals of Hering are short transitional passages lined by hepatocytes and cuboidal cholangiocytes, not a uniform stratified epithelium.

questions.text: 45. The common bile duct is characterized by •
questions.explanation: The cystic duct from the gallbladder joins the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct, which carries bile to the duodenum.
options: Lined by simple columnar epith. with goblet cells
Drains bile into the gall bladder
Formed by the cystic & common hepatic ducts

questions.text:
30. Which of the following characterizes the mucous membrane of
gall bladder?
questions.explanation: Gallbladder mucosa has simple columnar absorptive cells and a vascular lamina propria; endocrine cells may occur but are not its dominant feature.
options: The adjacent cells are joined by gap junction.
Enteroendocrine cells may be seen in the lamina propria.

questions.text:
33. Which of the following structures are considered an endocrine
portion of the pancreas?
questions.explanation: The endocrine pancreas is formed by the islets of Langerhans, whose cells release hormones such as insulin and glucagon into blood.
options: Low columnar of inter lobular ducts.

questions.text: 81. The pancreatic acini are controlled by:
questions.explanation: CCK stimulates pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion, while secretin stimulates bicarbonate-rich ductal fluid. Together they coordinate the pancreatic response to a meal.

questions.text: 72. Centro acinar cells of the pancreatic acinus represent
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells mark the beginning of the pancreatic intercalated duct within the acinus and contribute bicarbonate-rich fluid.
options: The initial part of the intercalated duct
The distal part of the interacted duct
The proximal part of the intralobular duct

questions.text: 26. The ultrastructure of pancreatic acinar cells characterized by:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells make digestive enzymes and therefore have abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum for protein synthesis.

questions.text: 13. The centroacinar cells of pancreas secretes:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar and duct cells respond to secretin by secreting bicarbonate-rich fluid, which neutralizes acidic chyme entering the duodenum.

questions.text:
46. Activation of the zymogen granules within the pancreas results in
which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Premature activation of pancreatic zymogens within the gland causes autodigestion and acute necrotizing pancreatitis.

questions.text: 17. The cell membrane of pancreatic acini cells characterized by having ___ in its apical surface, ___ in its basal surface, & ___ & ___ in its lateral surface.
questions.explanation: Acinar cells have apical microvilli toward the lumen, basal CCK/ACh receptors, and lateral junctional and gap complexes.

questions.text:
37. Examination of EM photo of pancreatic acinar cells showing
abundant rER, free ribosomes, prominent Golgi apparatus
indicates that these cells are:
questions.explanation: Abundant rough ER, ribosomes, and Golgi indicate active protein synthesis and packaging. Pancreatic acinar cells use this machinery to make digestive enzyme precursors.

questions.text: 73. which of the following statements concerning the pancreas is not true?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini are pure serous units, unlike mixed salivary acini; therefore they do not form serous demilunes over mucous cells.
options: Its acinar cells contain zymogen granules
Its acinar cells contain a rounded, basally located nucleus

questions.text:
42. Secretion of which part of pancreas neutralizes the acidity of the
chyme?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic intercalated and centroacinar duct cells secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid that neutralizes acidic chyme; secretin stimulates this response.

questions.text:
43. Receptors for cholycystokinin hormone and acetylcholine are
located at which part of pancreatic acinar cell membrane?
questions.explanation: CCK and acetylcholine act on receptors at the basolateral membrane of pancreatic acinar cells, triggering enzyme secretion into the apical lumen.

questions.text: 34. Pancreatic acini are classified as:
questions.explanation: The pancreas is a compound tubuloacinar gland: its branched duct system ends in enzyme-secreting acini.

questions.text: 80. The Centroacinose cells are:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells are pale duct cells extending into the acinar lumen; they mark the beginning of the pancreatic duct system.
options: Flat cells lining the lumen of large ducts
Columnar cells lining the pancreatic acini
Formed by the union of intercalated ducts

questions.text: Centro acinar cells , all true except:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells mark the beginning of pancreatic ducts and contribute bicarbonate-rich fluid under secretin control. They are unrelated to the biliary duct system.
options: Its secretion is controlled by secretin hormone

questions.text: 14. Describe the structure of pancreatic acinar cells
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells synthesize digestive enzymes in basal RER and store them apically as zymogen granules for regulated secretion.
questions.modelAnswer: Pancreatic acini are pure serous units enclosed by basement membrane and reticular fibres, with 4–5 pyramidal cells around small lumen containing pale centroacinar cells. No myoepithelial cells. LM: rounded basal nuclei, basal basophilic striations and apical acidophilic zymogen granules. EM: rich RER/free ribosomes, basal elongated mitochondria, supranuclear Golgi, apical electron-dense membrane-bound granules and short microvilli; lateral junctional complexes/gap junctions; basal CCK/acetylcholine receptors. Acinar cells synthesize digestive protease precursors, amylase, lipases and nucleases. Centroacinar/intercalated duct cells have secretin receptors and add bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize chyme.

questions.text: Give a detailed account on the structure of pancreatic acini
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini are serous enzyme-secreting units of pyramidal cells around a narrow lumen, with basal RER and apical zymogen granules; centroacinar/duct cells add bicarbonate.
questions.modelAnswer: Pancreatic acini are pure serous units enclosed by basement membrane and reticular fibres, with 4–5 pyramidal cells around small lumen containing pale centroacinar cells. No myoepithelial cells. LM: rounded basal nuclei, basal basophilic striations and apical acidophilic zymogen granules. EM: rich RER/free ribosomes, basal elongated mitochondria, supranuclear Golgi, apical electron-dense membrane-bound granules and short microvilli; lateral junctional complexes/gap junctions; basal CCK/acetylcholine receptors. Acinar cells synthesize digestive protease precursors, amylase, lipases and nucleases. Centroacinar/intercalated duct cells have secretin receptors and add bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize chyme.

questions.text: 35. Pancreas differ from parotid glands in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini lack myoepithelial cells, which are found around salivary secretory units. The pancreas also has centroacinar cells and lacks striated ducts.

questions.text: 110. Pancreatic acinar cells , the following is true except:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini secrete protease precursors and other digestive enzymes; pepsinogen is produced by gastric chief cells.
options: Have receptors for cholecystokinin (secreted by enteroendocrine cells in intestine)
Have receptors for cholecystokinin acetyl choline (for autonomic control)
Secrete pepsinogen enzyme for protein digestion

questions.text: 57. Centro acinar cells, all true except:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells are the initial duct cells tucked into the acinar lumen, marking the beginning of the pancreatic duct system.
options: Its secretion is controlled by secretin hormone

questions.text: 56. Pancreatic acinar cells, the following is true except:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells secrete digestive enzymes such as trypsinogen and lipase, not pepsinogen, which is produced by gastric chief cells.
options: Have receptors for cholecystokinin (secreted by enteroendocrine cells in intestine)
Have receptors for cholecystokinin acetyl choline (for autonomic control)
Secrete pepsinogen enzyme for protein digestion

questions.text: 105. Exocrine portion of pancreas show the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The exocrine pancreas has intercalated and larger ducts but no striated ducts; secretin stimulates ductal bicarbonate and CCK stimulates enzymes.
options: Formed of pure serous acini with centroacinar cells
Its duct system is rich in striated ducts
Secretion of bicarbonate is stimulated by secretin hormone.
Secretion of enzymes is stimulated by cholecystokinin

questions.text: 38. Which of the following characterizes the pancreatic acinar cells?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells are polarized enzyme-secreting cells joined by junctional and gap complexes; their rough ER and Golgi synthesize and package digestive enzymes.

questions.text: 19. which of the following statements concerning the pancreas is not true?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini are purely serous and do not form serous demilunes, which are artifacts associated with mixed salivary glands. Their acinar cells have basal nuclei and apical zymogen granules.
options: Its acinar cells contains zymogen granules
Its acinar cells contain a rounded, basally located nucleus

questions.text: 24. The cytoplasm of pancreatic acinar cells has:
questions.explanation: Basal RER makes pancreatic enzymes and stains basophilic; apical zymogen granules are acidophilic and the Golgi lies supranuclear.

questions.text:
36. On examination of EM photo of pancreatic acinar cells shows
abundant:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells have abundant rough ER because they synthesize large amounts of digestive enzymes.

questions.text: 25. The pancreatic acini are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini are small serous end pieces with narrow lumina and pyramidal cells. Their basophilic basal cytoplasm reflects rough ER; apical granules are eosinophilic.
options: Cells show apical basophilia& basal acidophilia

questions.text: 20. The centroacinar cells of the pancreas represent:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells form the beginning of the intercalated duct, extending into the center of each pancreatic acinus.
options: The initial part of intercalated duct

questions.text: 115. Pancreatic acinar cells:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells contain abundant rough ER and Golgi to make and package secreted digestive enzymes.

questions.text:
40. Occasionally found goblet cells and enteroendocrine cells are
found in which of the following parts of the pancreas?
questions.explanation: Occasional goblet and enteroendocrine cells occur in larger pancreatic ducts, especially interlobular and main ducts, rather than the acini or smallest intercalated ducts.

questions.text: 25. Main pancreatic duct is lined with
questions.explanation: The main pancreatic duct is lined by simple columnar epithelium, while smaller intercalated ducts are lower cuboidal cells.

questions.text: 79. The pancreatic acini are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Pancreatic acini are small serous secretory units arranged around a narrow lumen, where apical enzyme granules are released.
options: Cells show apical basophilia & basal acidophilia

questions.text: 18. The pancreatic acinus is surrounded by ___ & ___
questions.explanation: A delicate basement membrane and reticular fiber network support pancreatic acini and separate them from surrounding connective tissue and capillaries.

questions.text: Give short notes on ducts of exocrine pancreas
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells begin the cuboidal intercalated ducts; these drain through larger ducts to the columnar main duct. The pancreas has no striated ducts, and its main duct joins the bile duct near the ampulla.
questions.modelAnswer: Centroacinar cells form invaginated initial intercalated ducts and are low cuboidal/flat squamous with flat nuclei. Short intercalated ducts outside acini are low cuboidal and drain to larger intralobular collecting ducts. Interlobular ducts are low columnar with occasional goblet/enteroendocrine cells; main duct is simple columnar with occasional goblet/enteroendocrine cells. No striated ducts. Main duct joins bile duct to open at ampulla; Oddi sphincter regulates flow and prevents reflux.

questions.text:
41. Apical zymogen granules in the pancreatic acinar cells represent
which of the following?
questions.explanation: Rough ER and Golgi package digestive enzymes into apical zymogen granules, where proteases are stored as inactive precursors.

questions.text: Compare between pancreas and parotid gland regrading CT , type , main duct , presence of striated duct
questions.explanation: Both are serous acinar glands, but pancreas has thin stroma, islets and centroacinar cells, and no striated ducts; parotid has a thick capsule and striated ducts. Pancreatic duct is simple columnar to duodenum; Stensen duct becomes stratified and opens in the vestibule.
questions.modelAnswer: Pancreas has thin capsule/delicate reticular stroma, mixed endocrine/exocrine gland with pure serous acini, centroacinar cells and no myoepithelium or striated ducts; main pancreatic duct has simple columnar epithelium and opens into duodenum. Parotid has thick capsule/septa with adipocytes, pure serous acini with myoepithelium and prominent striated ducts; main parotid duct has stratified columnar then nonkeratinized stratified squamous lining and opens in oral vestibule. Both have intercalated and excretory ducts.

questions.text: About filiform papillae, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Filiform papillae are numerous, more abundant than fungiform papillae, and lack taste buds while retaining tactile nerve endings.
options: They are secondary papillae extend from the primary papillae
Each one has a separate epithelial cap
found on the anterior two thirds of the tongue in oblique transverse rows
No taste buds in filiform papillae, but they contain nerve endings for touch

questions.text: About the nasopharynx, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The nasopharynx contains the pharyngeal tonsil, whereas palatine tonsils sit in the oropharynx; the exception is their stated nasopharyngeal location.

questions.text: Regarding the sensory (gustatory) cells of taste buds, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Taste-bud sensory cells have pale cytoplasm and central positions, with apical microvilli exposed to the taste pore and basal contact with afferent nerves. Peripheral cells are supporting cells.
options: They have pale cytoplasm and darkly stained oval nuclei.
Their apical surfaces contain long microvilli embedded in amorphous glycosaminoglycan material secreted by supporting cells
Their basal parts are connected to the afferent nerve fibers

questions.text: Regarding the sublingual gland:
questions.explanation: The sublingual gland is branched tubuloalveolar, mainly mucous, and contributes roughly five percent of saliva; all statements apply.
options: Contains both mucous and serous cells (mostly mucous)

questions.text: Regarding the parotid gland, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Parotid glands are purely serous, unlike the mixed submandibular and mucous sublingual glands; their prominent striated ducts and mumps association remain true.
options: It is formed mainly of mixed acini

questions.text: Regarding the submandibular gland, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The submandibular gland has prominent striated ducts, so “has no striated ducts” is the exception. Its acini are mixed but predominantly serous.

questions.text: About the esophagus, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The esophagus contains skeletal muscle proximally, mixed muscle in the middle, and smooth muscle distally, so it is not entirely smooth.
options: Glands are present mainly in submucosa
The muscularis externa is formed entirely of smooth muscle
Muscularis mucosa is well developed in the lower half

questions.text: Regarding the esophagus, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Esophageal cardiac glands occur in the lamina propria near both ends, so glands are not absent throughout the mucosa.
options: It is a muscular tube that conveys ingested food from the pharynx to the stomach
The esophagus shows longitudinal folds that help in its expansion during swallowing.
Its muscularis mucosa is formed entirely of smooth muscle
Its mucosa contains no glands in the entire length

questions.text: Regarding the cardiac glands of the stomach, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Cardiac glands are concentrated near the esophageal opening and mainly secrete mucus; pits are generally short. Gastrin-secreting G cells and deep pits characterize pyloric mucosa.
options: Present in the narrow band 10-40 mm wide around the esophageal orifice
Lined by secreting cells that secrete mucous and few lysozymes
Few parietal cells for HCL secretion and some enteroendocrine cells that secrete gastrin.
Pits are relatively deep, occupying one half of the thickness of the mucosa

questions.text: The enterocytes are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Enterocytes occur over villi and superficial crypts; basolateral infoldings and lateral interdigitations support absorption and transport.

questions.text: All of the following about the duodenum are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Duodenal villi have lacteals and Brunner glands, but organized lymphoid aggregates (Peyer patches) are characteristic of ileum.
options: Its villi are broad and leaf like
Its lamina Propria contain large lymphocytic aggregations

questions.text: Regarding the columnar absorptive cells (ENTEROCYTES), all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Enterocytes absorb nutrients and carry a brush border with digestive enzymes, but they do not contain numerous mucous granules. Goblet cells store and release mucin.
options: Present over the villi and in the superficial parts of the crypts.
Each cell has about 3000 microvilli. Each microvillus is about 1 μm long & 0.1 μm in diameter.
Its cell coat contains glycoproteins which act as hydrolytic enzymes

questions.text: The appendix is characterized by:
questions.explanation: The appendix has a poorly defined muscularis mucosae and abundant lymphoid tissue, rather than long crypts and a wide lumen.

questions.text: Regarding the plicae circularis (Kerckring's valves) all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are small-intestinal folds, especially prominent in jejunum; the sigmoid colon has no such mucosal-submucosal folds.
options: The plicae are well developed in the jejunum
Circular mucosal folds around core of submucosa
Increase the intestinal surface area 3 times

questions.text: All of the following about hepatocytes are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes have sinusoidal, canalicular, and intercellular surfaces, but their microvilli project into Disse space and canaliculi rather than forming a conventional brush border.
options: They have long microvilli forming brush borders

questions.text: Regarding Ito cells, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Ito cells store vitamin A and can cause fibrosis when activated, but they are not highly phagocytic like Kupffer cells.
options: hepatic stellate cells that store vitamin A.
In liver cirrhosis, these cells may differentiate into myofibroblasts to synthesize collagen & induce fibrosis.
One of the contents of the perisinusoidal space

questions.text: The liver acinus is characterized by:
questions.explanation: The liver acinus is diamond-shaped between two portal tracts and two central veins; the portal lobule instead centers on a bile duct.
options: A diamond shaped mass of liver tissue
The portal tract is in its center
All the cells drain bile in the central bile duct

questions.text: Regarding the centro acinar cells, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells mark the start of the pancreatic duct system and contribute bicarbonate-rich fluid in response to secretin. They have no role in bile ducts.
options: Its secretion is controlled by secretin hormone

questions.text: Which of the following are called macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are macronutrients because they are required in comparatively large dietary amounts and provide energy or structure.

questions.text: 14- Marasmus is characterized by
questions.explanation: Marasmus is severe energy deficiency with marked wasting and loss of fat and muscle; edema and fatty liver more strongly suggest kwashiorkor.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a simple sugar (monosaccharide)?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide made of glucose and fructose, whereas glucose, fructose, and galactose are single-sugar monosaccharides.

questions.text: The dietary fats are transported to liver as
questions.explanation: Dietary long-chain fats leave enterocytes packaged in chylomicrons, travel through lymph, and then reach the liver via blood.

questions.text:
Energy is provided by 3 classes of nutrients Known as:
___ : 
___  ,  ___  &  ___
questions.explanation: Macronutrients are required in gram-scale amounts and supply energy or structural substrates; carbohydrate, fat, and protein are the three classes.

questions.text: All the following are true about linoleic acid except
questions.explanation: Linoleic acid is an essential omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid and precursor for eicosanoids; it generally lowers LDL and total cholesterol rather than raising HDL.

questions.text: 13- Kwashiorkor disease is characterized by
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency despite relatively preserved calorie intake; impaired lipoprotein export promotes fatty liver.
options: Severe decrease in weight\ height ratio.

questions.text: 11- The highest Score of PDCAAS is
questions.explanation: PDCAAS is expressed from 0 to 1 after digestibility correction, so 1 represents the maximum protein-quality score.

questions.text: all the following is the effect of Fish Oil except
questions.explanation: Fish-oil omega-3 fatty acids can lower triglycerides and thrombosis tendency and support brain and retinal development. They do not increase blood pressure.

questions.text: What are the functions of dietary fat?
questions.explanation: Dietary fat supplies energy, contributes membrane lipids, and provides signaling molecules, so all listed roles are valid.

questions.text: Diets having a high ratio of monounsaturated fatty acids can cause:
questions.explanation: Monounsaturated fats can improve the serum lipid profile when they replace saturated fats, especially by lowering LDL cholesterol.

questions.text: 16- The low glycemic index CHO is below
questions.explanation: The conventional low-glycemic-index category is below 55 on the glucose-referenced scale; foods from 55–69 are intermediate and 70 or higher are high.

questions.text: Which of the following is essential fatty acids
questions.explanation: Linoleic acid is an essential omega-6 fatty acid that humans cannot synthesize because they lack the required desaturase.

questions.text: Discuss the change in metabolism of organic substances during severe starvation.
questions.explanation: During starvation, glycogen falls first, then fat supplies energy and ketones spare protein; late fat depletion drives renewed muscle breakdown.
questions.modelAnswer:
Depletion of food stores occurs, carbohydrates then fat and finally protein.
For protein 3 phases of depletion occurs:
    1. Rapid depletion: to form glucose in liver.
    2. Slow depletion: to allow more fat to be utilized by the body and formation of ketone bodies to
      supply the brain (can cross BBB).
    3. Rapid depletion again: after all fat stores are almost completely depleted no source for energy
      production except protein.

questions.text: Carbohydrates can be divides into 2 general sections. The sections are:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are grouped nutritionally as simple sugars and complex carbohydrates. This classification refers to molecular structure and digestion, not whether a food is single or compound.

questions.text: Symptoms of Kwashiorkor include?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor commonly causes skin and hair changes from protein deficiency; subcutaneous fat loss and severe wasting are more typical of marasmus.

questions.text: Define respiratory RQ and discuss its significance.
questions.explanation: Respiratory quotient (CO₂ produced/O₂ consumed) estimates fuel oxidation: about 1 for carbohydrate, 0.7 for fat, and 0.8 for protein.
questions.modelAnswer:
•  RQ (respiratory quotient) is the ratio of volume of CO2 produced to the volume of O2 consumed
   during the same time.
•   Its significance:
    1. An index for nature of food oxidized at time of estimation: (if fat= 0.7, if CHO=1, if protein=0.8, if
      mixed=0.85) ex. For brain it =1, that means that brain is oxidizing only carbohydrates (glucose).
    2.  Index for transformation of type of food to the other: if CHO is transformed into fat , RQ >1
  CHO rich in O2, into fat poor in O2 and CO2 releases so CO2 increases without increase in O2 from
   respiration so RQ increases. And vice versa.
    3.  Determination of energy output by indirect calorimeter (if we knew that 1L O2 is used to in the
      body to form 4.82 Kcal, we could know the metabolic rate by measuring the num. of O2 liters
     consumed per unit of time) .

questions.text: The deficiency of both energy and protein causes?
questions.explanation: Marasmus reflects severe deficiency of both energy and protein, causing marked wasting. Kwashiorkor is more associated with protein deficiency, edema, and fatty liver.

questions.text: Mediterranean diet rich in olive oil (rich in oleic acid) lower the incidence of ischemic heart disease, oleic acid is
questions.explanation: Oleic acid has one double bond, making it monounsaturated; olive oil is rich in this fatty acid.

questions.text: Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) is the average daily nutrient intake level estimated to meet the requirement of ______ of healthy individuals in a particular life stage and gender group.
questions.explanation: EAR is estimated to meet the nutrient requirement of half of healthy people in a defined age and sex group; RDA covers nearly all.

questions.text: Lactose is formed of
questions.explanation: Lactose is the milk disaccharide composed of glucose and galactose. Sucrose instead combines glucose with fructose.

questions.text: Which of the following is low biological value protein
questions.explanation: Gelatin lacks a balanced essential amino-acid profile, especially tryptophan, so it has low biological value as a protein.

questions.text: Essential amino acids are amino acids that the adult body can synthesize in adequate amounts.
questions.explanation: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized in adequate amounts by the body, so they must be obtained from dietary protein.

questions.text: Which of the following are called macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are macronutrients because they are needed in relatively large amounts and provide energy or essential structural substrates.

questions.text: AMDR are the ranges of intake for a particular macronutrient that is associated with reduced risk of chronic disease
questions.explanation: AMDR describes macronutrient intake ranges associated with adequate nutrition and reduced chronic-disease risk, not a single target amount.

questions.text: The only way to get all the nutrients you need is:
questions.explanation: A varied combination of foods supplies the full range of essential nutrients because individual foods differ in their nutrient profiles.
options: to eat a combination of foods
to eat the same foods over and over again

questions.text: 12- Which of the following is low biological value protein
questions.explanation: Gelatin is low biological value because it lacks a balanced complement of essential amino acids, especially tryptophan. Milk, egg, and soy provide more complete protein.

questions.text: Define the specific dynamic action and explain its causes.
questions.explanation: Specific dynamic action is the post-meal rise in energy expenditure, largely from digestion, absorption, nutrient processing, and storage.
questions.modelAnswer:

Max after 4-5hs. then lasts for 12-14hs.

questions.text: BIO1: Total Energy Expenditure (TEE) include :
questions.explanation: TEE combines resting energy expenditure, thermic effect of food, and physical activity; all three contribute to daily calorie needs.

questions.text: 6- All the following are true about linoleic acid except:
questions.explanation: Linoleic acid is an essential omega-6 fatty acid that supports eicosanoid synthesis and tends to lower LDL and total cholesterol, but it does not reliably increase HDL.

questions.text: CHO are inherently fattening
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are not inherently fattening; long-term energy surplus, regardless of source, drives body-fat gain.

questions.text: Which of the following is caused due to extreme lack of proteins?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results chiefly from severe protein deficiency and classically causes edema; marasmus reflects overall energy deficiency and wasting.

questions.text: Negative nitrogen balance occurs with all the following conditions except
questions.explanation: Exercise generally promotes protein synthesis when energy and amino acids are adequate, so it is not a typical cause of negative nitrogen balance. Starvation, burns, and hyperthyroidism can increase nitrogen loss.

questions.text: Fiber absorbs water like a sponge and helps food move through the large intestine.
questions.explanation: Dietary fiber retains water and adds bulk to stool, helping contents move through the colon and supporting regular bowel movements.

questions.text: AI is set instead of RDA when sufficient Scientific evidence is not available to calculate EAR or RDA
questions.explanation: AI is used when evidence is insufficient to establish an EAR and derive an RDA; it is based on observed or estimated intake.

questions.text: A characteristic feature of marasmus is:
questions.explanation: Marasmus causes severe loss of muscle and subcutaneous fat from energy deficiency. Unlike kwashiorkor, severe hypoalbuminemia and edema are not defining features.

questions.text: BIO2: In naturally occurring unsaturated fatty acids, the double bonds are in the ……….. Configuration.
questions.explanation: Most naturally occurring unsaturated fatty acids have cis double bonds, which introduce bends and affect membrane packing.
options: A mixture of cis and trans conformation

questions.text: Which of the following is precursor for arachidonic acid
questions.explanation: Linoleic acid (an omega-6 essential fatty acid) can be elongated and desaturated to arachidonic acid; alpha-linolenic acid is omega-3.

questions.text: Which of the following Fatty acids increase level of cholesterol in blood
questions.explanation: Palmitic acid is saturated and can raise blood LDL cholesterol when it replaces unsaturated fats. Oleic, linoleic, and linolenic acids are unsaturated.

questions.text: White bread has higher GI than whole wheat bread
questions.explanation: White bread is usually more rapidly digested than whole wheat bread, producing a higher glycemic response and glycemic index.

questions.text:
The DRI consists of 4 dietary reference standards :
___  ,  ___, ___& ___
questions.explanation: DRI includes EAR, RDA, AI, and UL, which respectively guide average needs, near-total coverage, insufficient-data intake targets, and safety limits.

questions.text: When choosing carbohydrates, choose ones low in added _________.
questions.explanation: Choosing foods low in added sugar reduces excess energy intake while leaving room for naturally occurring carbohydrates and fiber-rich foods.

questions.text: Kwashiorkor disease is characterized by
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor impairs hepatic lipoprotein synthesis and export, allowing triglycerides to accumulate in liver cells as fatty liver.
options: Severe decrease in weight\ height ratio.

questions.text: Total Energy Expenditure (TEE) include :
questions.explanation: Total energy expenditure adds resting metabolism, food-induced thermogenesis, and physical activity, whose proportions vary between people.

questions.text: A characteristic feature of Kwashiorkor is:
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor commonly causes fatty liver from impaired apolipoprotein synthesis and lipid export. Marasmus is marked by severe emaciation without the same typical edema.
options: Occurrence in less than 1 year infant

questions.text: Which one of following statements about nitrogen balance is correct?
questions.explanation: Positive nitrogen balance means nitrogen intake exceeds nitrogen loss, as during growth, pregnancy, or tissue rebuilding.
options: Nitrogen balance is the ratio of intake of nitrogenous compounds / output of nitrogenous metabolites from the body.
In nitrogen equilibrium the excretion of nitrogenous metabolites is greater than the dietary intake of nitrogenous compounds.
Positive nitrogen balance means that there is a net loss of protein from the body.
In positive nitrogen balance the excretion of nitrogenous metabolites is less than the dietary intake of nitrogenous compounds.
In negative nitrogen balance the excretion of nitrogenous metabolites is less than the dietary intake of nitrogenous compounds.

questions.text: Which of the following is most variable part in Energy expenditure
questions.explanation: Physical activity varies most from day to day and among individuals, whereas resting metabolic rate is comparatively stable.

questions.text: Adequate intake levels of fibers for adult man is
questions.explanation: The cited adequate intake for adult men is 38 g dietary fiber daily; fiber supports bowel function and is associated with broader metabolic benefits.

questions.text: Which membrane fatty acids are precursors for arachidonic acid?
questions.explanation: Arachidonic acid is synthesized from the omega-6 essential fatty acid linoleic acid through elongation and desaturation.

questions.text: What is the main function of a carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are a major readily available fuel, oxidized to ATP; they can also be stored as glycogen or converted to fat.

questions.text: Saturated fats come from
questions.explanation: Many animal fats are relatively rich in saturated fatty acids, though plant sources such as coconut and palm oils also contain substantial saturated fat.

questions.text: Nutrients are divided into : ___ & ___
questions.explanation: Macronutrients are needed in relatively large quantities, while micronutrients such as vitamins and minerals are needed in smaller amounts.

questions.text: When Intake is more than UL there is decrease potential risk of adverse effects
questions.explanation: The tolerable upper intake level is the highest usual daily intake unlikely to cause harm; exceeding it increases potential risk rather than lowering it.

questions.text: There is an association between sucrose consumption and ___ .
questions.explanation: Sucrose promotes dental caries because oral bacteria ferment it to acids and use it to form sticky extracellular glucans.

questions.text: In naturally occurring unsaturated fatty acids, the double bonds are in the ……….. Conformation.
questions.explanation: Natural unsaturated fatty acids usually contain cis double bonds, which introduce bends and prevent tight packing of their chains.
options: A mixture of cis and trans conformation

questions.text: Lipoproteins are particles synthesized to transport hydrophobic lipid, they are formed of ___ And ___
questions.explanation: Apoproteins and phospholipids form the lipoprotein surface, making hydrophobic lipids transportable in blood. The particle also has a neutral-lipid core of triglycerides and cholesteryl esters.

questions.text: In naturally occurring unsaturated fatty acids, the double bonds are in the ……….. Conformation.
questions.explanation: Naturally occurring unsaturated fatty acids usually have cis-configured double bonds, producing kinks in their hydrocarbon chains.
options: A mixture of cis and trans conformation

questions.text: All the following are the functions of soluble fibers except
questions.explanation: Soluble fiber can bind bile acids and reduce their reabsorption; it also slows gastric emptying and promotes fullness, unlike the selected option.
options: decreases exposure time of the intestines to carcinogens

questions.text:
2- Mediterranean diet rich in olive oil (rich in oleic acid) ) lower
the incidence of ischemic heart disease , oleic acid is
questions.explanation: Oleic acid has one double bond, so it is monounsaturated. Olive oil is rich in oleic acid and is a major source of this fatty-acid class.

questions.text: 3- The dietary fats are transported to liver as
questions.explanation: Chylomicrons carry absorbed dietary triacylglycerol from the intestine through lymph and blood to tissues and ultimately the liver.

questions.text: Fats provide less energy than carbohydrates.
questions.explanation: Fat yields about 9 kcal/g versus roughly 4 kcal/g from carbohydrate, so the statement that fat provides less energy is false.

questions.text: Glycolipids of mammalian tissues are :
questions.explanation: Mammalian glycolipids are chiefly glycosphingolipids, enriched in the outer membrane leaflet and especially abundant in nervous tissue.
options: Present in the outer leaflet of cell membranes.
Widely distributed especially in nervous tissue.

questions.text: Write short notes on the appestat centre & discuss the factors regulating its activity.
questions.explanation: The hypothalamic lateral area promotes feeding and ventromedial circuits contribute to satiety; nutrients and adiposity signals modulate these centers.
questions.modelAnswer:
Appestat centers are in hypothalamus
Row | Feeding center | Satiety center
Site | lateral hypothalamus | ventromedial hypothalamus
If stimulated | Food intake increases | satiety occurs
In excessive stimulation | hyperphagia occurs | aphagia occurs
If injured | fatal anorexia occurs | hyperphagia occurs
Factors regulating its activity:
Long term regulation:
- Nutritional regulation by 2 theories:
a. Glucostate theory: increasing glucose level stimulates satiety center and vice versa
b. Lipostate and aminostate theory: increasing fat and amino acids levels stimulate satiety center and vice versa.
- Body temperature regulation:
Cold temperature stimulates feeding center and vice versa.
Short term regulation:
- Alimentary factors inhibiting feeding center:
(Gastrointestinal filling- oral factors as chewing or swallowing- hormones as calcitonin, insulin & CCK).
- Psychological factors past experience to smell or taste.

questions.text: Regarding cerebrosides, which of the following is not true :
questions.explanation: Cerebrosides are glycosphingolipids made of ceramide linked to one sugar and contain no phosphate. A phosphate-containing sphingolipid is sphingomyelin.
options: They are formed by a glycosidic bond between a hexose & carbon-1 of sphingosine moiety.
They have a phosphate group attached to the primary alcoholic group of sphingosine.
They include glucosyl ceramide & galactosyl ceramide.
Glucocerebrosides are the predominant species in extraneural tissue while galactocerebrosides are mostly in neural tissue.

questions.text: Which of the following regulates lipolysis in adipocytes?
questions.explanation: Hormones raise cAMP and activate protein kinase A, which phosphorylates hormone-sensitive lipase and promotes adipocyte triglyceride breakdown.
options: Activation of fatty acid synthesis mediated by CAMP
Glycerol phosphorylation to prevent futile esterification of fatty acids
Activation of hormone sensitive lipase as a result of hormone stimulated increases in CAMP levels
Activation of CAMP production by Insulin

questions.text: Which of the following adipose derived hormones promotes insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues?
questions.explanation: Adiponectin, unlike ghrelin or resistin, generally improves insulin sensitivity and fatty-acid oxidation in peripheral tissues.

questions.text: A genetic disorder caused by mutation in the hexoaminidase A enzyme:
questions.explanation: Tay–Sachs disease results from hexosaminidase A deficiency, causing GM2 ganglioside accumulation, especially in neurons.

questions.text: For TAG synthesis, glycerol should be in the glycerol 3 P form, glycerol kinase is absent in:
questions.explanation: Adipocytes lack glycerol kinase, so they rely on glycolysis-derived glycerol-3-phosphate to re-esterify fatty acids.

questions.text: A ceramide molecule
questions.explanation: Ceramide is sphingosine linked by an amide bond to a long-chain fatty acid; it is the backbone of sphingolipids and can arise from their hydrolysis.
options: Is formed of a long chain fatty acid,e.g. cerebronic or lignoceric acid in an amide bond with sphingosine
May result from partial hydrolysis of sphingomyelins or glycolipids
is a component of a sulfatide molecule

questions.text: Sphingolipids are released when a membrane is degraded.
questions.explanation: Membrane turnover releases sphingolipid components, which are then degraded or recycled in cellular pathways. Sphingolipids are abundant structural membrane lipids.

questions.text: Triacylglycerol stored in the body as cytoplasmic lipid droplets.
questions.explanation: Stored triacylglycerol accumulates in cytoplasmic lipid droplets, providing a compact energy reserve in adipocytes.

questions.text: Regarding cerebrosides, which of the following is not true
questions.explanation: Cerebrosides are neutral glycosphingolipids with a single sugar and no phosphate; phosphocholine/phosphoethanolamine marks sphingomyelin instead.
options: They are formed by a glycosidic bond between a hexose & carbon-1 of sphingosine moiety
They have a phosphate group attached to the primary alcoholic group of sphingosine
They include glucosyl ceramide & galactosyl ceramide
Glucocerebrosides are the predominant species in extraneural tissue while galactocerebrosides are mostly inneural tissue

questions.explanation: Phospholipids form membrane bilayers and lipoprotein surfaces; specialized species also serve as lung surfactant, signaling precursors, bile cholesterol solubilizers, and coagulation surfaces.

questions.text: Glycolipids are combination of:
questions.explanation: Glycolipids typically consist of a ceramide lipid linked to one or more carbohydrate residues, rather than a glycerol backbone.

questions.text: In sphingomyelins , a fatty acyl radical is connected to the :
questions.explanation: In sphingomyelin, the fatty acid forms an amide bond with sphingosine’s amino group; a phosphocholine or phosphoethanolamine headgroup attaches separately.

questions.text: 8- To form active form of glycerol in adipose tissue we use
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue has little glycerol kinase, so it makes glycerol-3-phosphate from the glycolytic intermediate dihydroxyacetone phosphate to re-esterify fatty acids.

questions.text: In sphingomyelins, a fatty acyl radical is connected to the Primary alcoholic group of sphingosine
questions.explanation: In sphingomyelin, the fatty acid is attached by an amide bond to sphingosine's amino group, forming ceramide.

questions.text: BIO3: Which of the following enzyme is not active in white adipose tissue:
questions.explanation: White adipose tissue has little glycerol kinase, so it relies on glycolytic dihydroxyacetone phosphate to make glycerol-3-phosphate for triacylglycerol synthesis.

questions.text: What is leptin resistance?
questions.explanation: Leptin resistance means high circulating leptin fails to produce the expected reduction in appetite or energy intake, often despite adequate adipose leptin production.
options: Deficiency of leptin caused by a mutation in the leptin gene.
Lack of leptin release from the adipose tissue.
High concentrations of leptin without reduction in energy intake.
Low concentrations of leptin with increased energy intake.

questions.text: Which of the following is the effect of insulin in hormone sensitive lipase
questions.explanation: Insulin suppresses hormone-sensitive lipase by lowering cAMP and promoting dephosphorylation, reducing adipose lipolysis.
options: Insulin activates phosphatase enzyme to dephosphorylates HSL

questions.text: Sialic acid enters in the structure of :
questions.explanation: Gangliosides contain sialic acid in their oligosaccharide headgroup, giving these glycosphingolipids a negative charge.

questions.text: Gaucher disease is due to deficiency of which of the following enzyme
questions.explanation: Gaucher disease is caused by deficient glucocerebrosidase, leading to glucocerebroside accumulation in macrophages. Other lysosomal enzyme deficiencies cause different storage diseases.

questions.text: During increase body weight, all the following will be increased except
questions.explanation: Adiponectin generally falls as adiposity increases, while leptin and insulin resistance tend to rise with greater fat mass.

questions.text: A ceramide molecule :
questions.explanation: Ceramide underlies cerebrosides, gangliosides, sulfatides, and sphingomyelins; together these compounds form major sphingolipid classes.
options: Is formed of a long chain fatty acid ,e.g. cerebronic or lignoceric acid in an amide bond with sphingosine.
May result from partial hydrolysis of sphingomyelins or glycolipids.
Is a component of a sulfatide molecule.

questions.text:
4- Lipolysis in adipose tissue is inhibited by which of the following
hormones?
questions.explanation: Insulin suppresses hormone-sensitive lipolysis in adipose tissue and promotes triglyceride storage. Glucagon and catecholamines favor mobilization of stored fat.

questions.text: Glycolipids of mammalian tissues are
questions.explanation: Mammalian glycolipids are glycosphingolipids, enriched in nervous tissue and largely displayed on the extracellular leaflet of membranes.
options: Present in the outer leaflet of cell membranes
Wicely distributed especially in nervous tissue

questions.text: Increase use of high fructose corn syrup (HFCS) is associated with a rise in obesity
questions.explanation: HFCS use rose during a period when obesity also increased, so the statement describes an observed population-level association. That association alone does not establish HFCS as the cause.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered as the structural parent of all sphingolipids?
questions.explanation: Ceramide, made from sphingosine plus a fatty acid, is the backbone from which complex sphingolipids are derived.

questions.text: Which component is found in all sphingolipids?
questions.explanation: All sphingolipids share sphingosine, a long-chain amino alcohol; phosphate or carbohydrate groups vary among subclasses.

questions.text: Sphingosine is formed from attachment of palmitic acid to which of the following amino acid
questions.explanation: Sphingosine synthesis begins when palmitoyl-CoA condenses with serine, followed by reduction and processing to form the long-chain amino alcohol backbone.

questions.text: Ceramide is:
questions.explanation: Ceramide is sphingosine joined to a fatty acid by an amide bond; adding sugars or phosphocholine forms more complex lipids.

questions.text: Which of the following hormone is not used in the hydrolysis of triacylglycerol into the fatty acids in adipose tissues?
questions.explanation: Insulin suppresses adipose lipolysis, whereas catecholamines activate hormone-sensitive lipolytic pathways; glucagon has little direct adipose effect in humans.

questions.text: Fabry disease is due to deficiency of which of the following enzyme
questions.explanation: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disease caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, with globotriaosylceramide accumulation.

questions.text: Niemann-Pick disease is due to deficiency of which of the following enzyme
questions.explanation: Niemann–Pick types A and B result from acid sphingomyelinase deficiency, causing sphingomyelin accumulation in tissues.

questions.text: Ceramide is an essential component of all the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Lecithin (phosphatidylcholine) is a glycerophospholipid, not a ceramide-based sphingolipid; the other listed compounds contain ceramide.

questions.text: 10. Mention classes of sphingolipids.
questions.explanation: Sphingolipids include sphingomyelin, which carries phosphocholine, and glycosphingolipids, which carry carbohydrate head groups such as cerebrosides, sulfatides, and gangliosides.
questions.modelAnswer:
Sphingomyelin = ceramide + Phosphocholine.
Glycosphingolipids (Glycolipids) = ceramide+ carbohydrates.

questions.text: In Tay-Sachs disease which of the following substrate will be increased
questions.explanation: Tay–Sachs disease is caused by hexosaminidase A deficiency, leading to GM2 ganglioside accumulation in neurons.

questions.text: The enzyme acyl-CoA synthetase catalyses the conversion of a fatty acid to an active fatty acid in the presence of:
questions.explanation: Fatty-acid activation uses ATP and coenzyme A via acyl-CoA synthetase, forming acyl-CoA, AMP, and pyrophosphate before carnitine transport.

questions.text: * Glycolipids include: ___
questions.explanation: Glycolipids are glycosphingolipids with carbohydrate head groups; major classes include cerebrosides, sulfatides, gangliosides, and globosides.

questions.text: In which organ, lipogenesis occur mostly?
questions.explanation: Lipogenesis occurs substantially in both liver and adipose tissue, with the liver exporting synthesized lipid and adipose storing it.

questions.text: * Sphingolipids include: ___ .
questions.explanation: Sphingolipids comprise sphingomyelin and glycosphingolipids, including cerebrosides, gangliosides, and sulfatides.

questions.text: Sphingomyelins yield on hydrolysis the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Sphingomyelin hydrolysis yields sphingosine, a fatty acid, phosphate, and choline. Glycerol is absent because sphingolipids use a sphingosine backbone rather than glycerol.

questions.text: Glycerol kinase is present in
questions.explanation: The liver has glycerol kinase and can phosphorylate glycerol directly; adipose tissue largely depends on glycolysis for glycerol-3-phosphate.

questions.text: In adipose tissue, glucose can be converted into glycerol 3 P through which of the following intermediates:
questions.explanation: Glycolysis produces dihydroxyacetone phosphate, which is reduced to glycerol-3-phosphate for triacylglycerol assembly in adipose tissue.

questions.text: Sialic acid enters in the structure of
questions.explanation: Gangliosides are complex glycosphingolipids that contain one or more sialic acid residues. Cerebrosides have a single neutral sugar and no sialic acid.

questions.text: Fabry disease which of the following substrate increased
questions.explanation: Fabry disease causes alpha-galactosidase A deficiency and accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (ceramide trihexoside).

questions.text: Glycolipids include
questions.explanation: Cerebrosides, gangliosides, and sulfatides are all glycolipid subclasses, differing by sugar composition and charge-bearing groups.

questions.text: Which of the following enzyme is not active in white adipose tissue:
questions.explanation: White adipose tissue has little glycerol kinase, so it cannot efficiently phosphorylate free glycerol. It instead generates glycerol-3-phosphate from glycolytic intermediates.

questions.text: 10- Which of the following is intermediate during synthesis of TAG
questions.explanation: Phosphatidic acid is a central intermediate in triacylglycerol synthesis, formed before diacylglycerol and the final acylation step.

questions.text: BIO 10: Niemann- Pick disease is caused by a genetic defect in which one of the following enzymes?
questions.explanation: Niemann–Pick types A and B classically result from acid sphingomyelinase deficiency, causing sphingomyelin accumulation in lysosomes.

questions.text:
1- Which of the following adipose derived hormones promotes
insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues?
questions.explanation: Adiponectin improves insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues and has anti-inflammatory metabolic effects. Resistin is associated with insulin resistance.

questions.text: Sphingomyelins yield on hydrolysis the following EXCEPT :
questions.explanation: Sphingomyelin yields sphingosine, fatty acid, phosphate, and choline on hydrolysis; it contains no glycerol backbone.

questions.text: Cholesterol does not serve as a precursor for which compounds?
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is a precursor for vitamin D, bile acids, and steroid hormones, but bile pigments arise from heme breakdown.

questions.text: Obesity generally reflects excess intake of energy and is often associated with the development of:
questions.explanation: Obesity increases risk of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with cardiovascular and other metabolic complications.

questions.text: Gaucher disease is due to deficiency of which of the following enzyme
questions.explanation: Gaucher disease results from deficient glucocerebrosidase, leading to glucocerebroside accumulation in macrophages.

questions.text: Ceramide is an essential component of all the following EXCEPT :
questions.explanation: Lecithin contains glycerol and fatty acids rather than ceramide; the other listed sphingolipids share a ceramide backbone.

questions.text: Hepatic lipogenesis is stimulated by:
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes hepatic lipogenesis by increasing glucose use and expression of fatty-acid synthesis enzymes. Glucagon and catecholamines generally oppose this fed-state pathway.

questions.text: Which type of membrane lipid contains sialic acid?
questions.explanation: Gangliosides are glycosphingolipids with one or more sialic acid residues in their carbohydrate headgroup.

questions.text: Activation of fatty acids requires all the following except
questions.explanation: Fatty-acid activation requires ATP, CoA, and acyl-CoA synthetase; carnitine is needed later to transport long-chain acyl groups into mitochondria.

questions.text: Glycolipids are located in the inner leaflet of cell membrane.
questions.explanation: Glycolipids are displayed on the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, where their carbohydrate groups participate in cell recognition and interactions.

questions.text: To form TAG, which of the following is added to Diacyl glycerol:
questions.explanation: Diacylglycerol receives a third fatty acyl group from fatty acyl-CoA to form triacylglycerol.

questions.text: Lipolysis in adipose tissue is inhibited by which Of the following hormones
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes triacylglycerol storage and inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase, reducing release of fatty acids from adipose stores.

questions.text: Glycolipids include :
questions.explanation: Cerebrosides, gangliosides, globosides, and sulfatides are all glycosphingolipid classes, so “all of the above” is correct.

questions.text: Sulfatides
questions.explanation: Sulfatides are sulfated galactocerebrosides abundant in myelin, where the sulfate-bearing headgroup contributes membrane properties.
options: Are present in high amount in myelin
Have a sulfate group attached to sphingosine molety

questions.text: * Sphingolipidoses is: ___
questions.explanation: Sphingolipidoses are lysosomal storage disorders in which defective degradation causes specific sphingolipids to accumulate, often in nervous tissue.
blanks: Accumulation of any type of sphingolipids in many organs specially nervous tissue.

questions.text: Sulfatides :
questions.explanation: Sulfatides are sulfated galactocerebrosides enriched in myelin. Their sulfate is attached to the sugar residue, rather than directly to sphingosine.
options: Are present in high amount in myelin.
Have a sulfate group attached to sphingosine moiety.

questions.text: 9. Mention the name of substrates in sphingosine synthesis & ceramide.
questions.explanation: Sphingosine is synthesized from serine and palmitoyl-CoA; ceramide forms when a fatty acyl-CoA is attached to sphingosine.
questions.modelAnswer:
Sphingosine is synthesized form: Serine+ palmitoyl-CoA.
Ceramide is synthesized form: sphingosine + Fatty acyl-CoA.

questions.text: Which of the following enzyme is not active in white adipose tissue:
questions.explanation: White adipocytes lack significant glycerol kinase, so they cannot efficiently recycle free glycerol; glycolytic DHAP supplies glycerol-3-phosphate instead.

questions.text: Sphingosine is formed from attachment of palmitic acid to which of the following amino acid
questions.explanation: Sphingosine is synthesized from serine and palmitoyl-CoA. Serine contributes the amino-alcohol backbone; subsequent reactions form the long-chain base.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is fat soluble, along with vitamins A, D, and E; B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.

questions.text: The amino acid from which niacin synthesized is
questions.explanation: Tryptophan can be converted into niacin (NAD/NADP precursors), though the conversion yield depends on nutritional cofactors.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Vitamin E deficiency can cause neurologic or hemolytic problems, not pernicious anemia, which usually reflects vitamin B12 deficiency. The other nutrient-disease pairs are standard associations.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false about Ascorbic acid?
questions.explanation: Humans cannot synthesize vitamin C, so dietary ascorbate is required for collagen hydroxylation and antioxidant activity.
options: It is a strong reducing agent
It can be synthesized in the body
Involved in the hydroxylation of prolyl- and lysyl- residues of collagen

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins is an integral component of coenzyme A that allows two carbon units to enter the TCA cycle?
questions.explanation: Pantothenic acid forms part of coenzyme A, whose phosphopantetheine thiol carries two-carbon acetyl units into the TCA cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes require vitamin Biotin for its activity
questions.explanation: Biotin is a coenzyme for carboxylases, including acetyl-CoA carboxylase in fatty-acid synthesis. Transaminases, hydroxylases, and dehydrogenases use different cofactors.

questions.text: To which of the following families panthothenic acid belong?
questions.explanation: Pantothenic acid is vitamin B5, a component of coenzyme A and the acyl carrier protein prosthetic group.

questions.text: The Vitamin C or ascorbic acid prevents’
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy by impairing collagen hydroxylation; rickets stems from vitamin D deficiency.

questions.text: Which of the following is the only water-soluble vitamin with significant toxicity
questions.explanation: High-dose pyridoxine (vitamin B6) can cause sensory neuropathy, making it a notable water-soluble vitamin with toxicity. Other listed vitamins are less commonly toxic at usual doses.

questions.text: Niacin is used in high doses in the ___
questions.explanation: Pharmacologic-dose niacin lowers triglycerides and LDL while raising HDL, though adverse effects limit its routine use.

questions.text: For Very low birth weight infants, which of the following vitamins is used as a supplementation
questions.explanation: Very-low-birth-weight infants may receive vitamin E to protect red-cell membranes from oxidative injury, guided by neonatal protocols.

questions.text: Which of the following TCA cycle enzymes require FAD as a cofactor?
questions.explanation: Succinate dehydrogenase uses FAD to oxidize succinate to fumarate in the TCA cycle and also functions as complex II of the electron transport chain.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes require FMN for its activity
questions.explanation: NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) uses FMN to accept electrons from NADH before passing them to iron-sulfur centers.

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins can be used in treatment of hyperlipidemia
questions.explanation: Pharmacologic niacin can lower triglycerides and LDL while raising HDL, although its lipid use is limited by adverse effects.

questions.text: BIO4: Which of the following diseases is caused by the deficiency of Niacin?
questions.explanation: Niacin deficiency reduces NAD and NADP production and causes pellagra, classically dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia. Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes require vitamin Pyridoxine for its activity
questions.explanation: Alanine transaminase uses pyridoxal phosphate derived from vitamin B6 to transfer amino groups between alanine and pyruvate.

questions.text: Transamination is a process of transfer of a- amino group from a donor amino acid to an acceptor a- keto acid for the formation of a new amino acid and a new keto acid. This process is a reversible process catalyzed by Transaminases that require----- as a coenzyme .
questions.explanation: Pyridoxal phosphate, derived from vitamin B6, carries amino groups during transamination reactions catalyzed by aminotransferases.

questions.text: Antioxidant nutrients are all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Vitamins C and E and beta-carotene can act as antioxidants. Vitamin K’s main role is cofactor for clotting-protein carboxylation.

questions.text: Which of the following Coenzymes is Carrier for CO2
questions.explanation: Biotin carries activated carbon dioxide in carboxylation reactions, including pyruvate carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

questions.text: Collagen Formation is Affected by deficiency of which ofthe following vitamins
questions.explanation: Vitamin C supports proline and lysine hydroxylation during collagen synthesis, so deficiency weakens connective tissue and delays healing.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding Sulfonamides?
questions.explanation: Sulfonamides resemble PABA and competitively inhibit bacterial dihydropteroate synthase, blocking folate synthesis. Humans obtain folate from diet and lack this pathway.
options: Structural analogs of PABA that competitively inhibit bacterial synthesis of folic acid
Structural analogs of PABA that competitively inhibit the human synthesis of folic acid
Structural analogs of PABA that competitively inhibit the bacterial and human synthesis of folic acid

questions.text: The Vitamin C or ascorbic acid prevents
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency prevents adequate collagen hydroxylation and causes scurvy, with impaired connective-tissue integrity and bleeding.

questions.text: Which of the followings which vitamin increases the absorption of iron from the gut?
questions.explanation: Ascorbate enhances non-heme iron absorption by reducing ferric iron to the more soluble ferrous form in the gut.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by the deficiency of Niacin?
questions.explanation: Niacin deficiency causes pellagra because NAD/NADP-dependent reactions fail. Scurvy, rickets, and pernicious anemia reflect deficiencies of other nutrients.

questions.text: Coenzyme A Contain which of the following Vitamins
questions.explanation: Coenzyme A contains pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), which forms its reactive phosphopantetheine portion.

questions.text: Which vitamin is affected by avidin
questions.explanation: Avidin in raw egg white binds biotin and prevents its absorption; cooking denatures avidin.

questions.text: For the patient, who take Isoniazid for TB, we have to give him which of the following vitamin
questions.explanation: Isoniazid can deplete or antagonize pyridoxine, so vitamin B6 is given to prevent neuropathy, especially in people at increased risk.

questions.text: An infant presents with growth retardation, weak muscle tone and lethargy. He is diagnosed with pyruvate carboxylase deficiency. Which of the following vitamins is required as a coenzyme for its action?
questions.explanation: Pyruvate carboxylase is a biotin-dependent carboxylase that adds carbon dioxide to pyruvate to form oxaloacetate.

questions.text: Mitochondrial pyruvate carboxylase needs
questions.explanation: Pyruvate carboxylase uses biotin to carry activated carbon dioxide during conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate.

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins is used therapeutically as a lipid lowering drug?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologic niacin can lower triglycerides and LDL and raise HDL, though adverse effects limit routine use. It is vitamin B3.

questions.text: Which vitamin is a major lipid-soluble antioxidant in cell membranes
questions.explanation: Vitamin E protects polyunsaturated membrane lipids from free-radical chain oxidation, making it the major lipid-soluble antioxidant.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes require vitamin C for its activity
questions.explanation: Vitamin C maintains iron in the reduced state required by collagen prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases; lysyl oxidase instead requires copper.

questions.text: (1619) The aetiology of scurvy is:
