CagA, delivered through the typeIV secretion system, alters the cytoskeleton and triggers oncogenic signals; associated chronic inflammation/metaplasia increases malignancy risk. VacA produces cellular changes and membrane pores, causing gastric mucosal injury, inflammation and cell death. Protease is identified in the current peptic-ulcer section as presumably damaging mucosa and predisposing to inflammation that perpetuates injury.

questions.modelAnswer: HBsAg indicates incubation/acute infection; persistence over 6 months indicates a carrier. Anti-HBs appears after HBsAg disappearance and indicates resolution/immunity. Anti-HBc IgM marks recent acute infection and diagnoses the window phase; anti-HBc IgG persists as evidence of past infection. HBeAg indicates high infectivity; its disappearance is favourable. questions.text: Question 19: Give reason: damage of hepatocytes in hepatitis virus infection. (May 2015)
questions.explanation: HBV usually does not directly kill hepatocytes; cytotoxic T cells recognize viral peptides on MHC I and induce apoptosis through perforin/granzymes or Fas signaling.
questions.modelAnswer:
The primary target of hepatitis virus is the liver. Hepatocytes are infected but without
cytopathic effect. They are damaged because of the attack of CD8+T cytotoxic lymphocytes
(Tc or CTLs). The CTLs react against the antigen associated with MHC class I molecule and
replicate producing effector cells that kill the infected hepatocyte by one of two ways:

  1- Theperforin pathway: Movement of CTL cytoplasmic granules towards the plasma
   membrane in contact with the target cell  fuse with plasma membrane  release
    perforin and granzymes into intercellular space  pores in target cells granzymes
    enter the cell inducing apoptosis.
  2- CD95 or Fas-FasL pathway: activated CTL increase expression of Fas ligand (CD95L) 
    interact with trans-membrane Fas protein (CD95) receptor on target cell surface  cell
    death.

questions.explanation: Poliovirus is primarily neurotropic and is not a standard cause of viral gastroenteritis, unlike rotavirus, adenovirus 40/41, and astrovirus.

questions.text: Which is most correct about rotavirus vaccine :-
questions.explanation: The available rotavirus vaccines are live attenuated oral vaccines, including a pentavalent formulation; antiviral therapy does not replace prevention.
options: Killed human rota virus vaccine is used
Live attenuated pentavalent vaccine is used
Available antiviral drugs can replace vaccine

questions.text: Live attenuated oral rotavirus vaccine include which of the following?
questions.explanation: Oral rotavirus vaccines include monovalent human Rotarix and pentavalent human–bovine reassortant RotaTeq.

questions.text: Rotavirus & Norwalk virus are different viruses, but share which one of the following characteristics?
questions.explanation: Both rotavirus and Norwalk virus spread by the fecal-oral route; their age patterns and genome structures differ.
options: They mainly cause disease in infants and young children
They induce generally mild disease in young children
Infection patterns show no seasonal variation

questions.text: Rota virus infections are considered preventable, mention examples of Rota virus vaccines
questions.explanation: Rotarix and RotaTeq are live oral vaccines that induce mucosal immunity and reduce severe rotavirus gastroenteritis.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. Monovalent RotaRix
2. PentaValent RotaTeq

questions.text: An outbreak of acute viral gastroenteritis occurred in a child-care center, with several very young children exhibiting nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. Which of the following should be applied to diarrheal fluid samples collected from affected children?
questions.explanation: Rotavirus antigen ELISA in stool provides a rapid diagnostic test in young children with acute gastroenteritis.
options: Electron microscopy to detect Norwalk virus
ELISA rapid test to detect Rota virus Ag

questions.text: What is the most important viral cause of epidemic gastroenteritis in adults
questions.explanation: Norovirus commonly causes outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in adults and across all ages, particularly in congregate settings.

questions.text: Describe Rotavirus vaccines
questions.explanation: Rotarix and RotaTeq are oral live attenuated vaccines given in early infancy; schedules differ by product.
questions.modelAnswer: Two live-virus oral vaccines are given in early infancy: Rotarix, a monovalent human vaccine containing the most common serotype, in 2 separate doses; and RotaTeq, a pentavalent human–bovine reassortant with human outer-surface protein genes in nonpathogenic bovine strains, containing five strains and inducing protective intestinal IgA, in a 3-dose series.

questions.text: Mention 3 viral causes of infantile Gastroenteritis adressing the most common one
questions.explanation: Rotavirus is a major cause of infant gastroenteritis; enteric adenoviruses and astrovirus are other viral causes.
questions.modelAnswer:
Rota V. → MC
Adeno V.
Astro V.

questions.text: What is the most important cause of epidemic gastroenteritis in adults?
questions.explanation: Norovirus (formerly Norwalk virus) spreads efficiently person-to-person and through food, causing outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in adults.

questions.text: Which of the following is not done in cases of Typhoid fever epidemics
questions.explanation: Penicillin is not routinely used to eradicate typhoid carriage; source tracing, sanitation, education, and vaccination are key controls.
options: Studies to trace source of infection

questions.text: Oral typhoidal vaccine contains:
questions.explanation: The oral typhoid vaccine contains live attenuated Salmonella Typhi; injectable vaccines use antigen preparations rather than live organisms.
options: Flagellar H Ag of Salmonella typhi
Vi capsular Ag of Salmonella species

questions.text: Enumerate VFs of Salmonella Enterica
questions.explanation: Salmonella virulence includes macrophage survival, Vi capsule in S. Typhi, and phase variation of flagellar H antigens.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. Survival inside MΦ
2. Capsule (Vi Capsule) Typhi, P.T C
3. phase variation of H Ag

questions.text: Discuss how diagnosis of Enteric fever depends on the stage of the disease
questions.explanation: Blood culture is most useful early in enteric fever; stool culture becomes more productive later, and carrier screening uses stool or urine.
questions.modelAnswer:
1st week → Blood Culture
2nd & 3rd week → Stool Culture
chronic carrier → Stool & urine analysis

questions.text: Mention the striking features of Salmonella causing enteric fever
questions.explanation: S. Typhi survives in macrophages and disseminates through lymphatics and blood to reticuloendothelial organs; gallbladder persistence enables chronic carriage and intestinal reinfection.
questions.modelAnswer: Facultative intracellular survival/replication within phagocytic cells is striking. After M-cell invasion, infected macrophages carry organisms to mesenteric nodes; transient primary bacteraemia disseminates them, then reticuloendothelial multiplication and macrophage killing produce secondary bacteraemia. Gallbladder persistence and bile return reinfect distal ileum, producing ulceration and possible carrier state.

questions.text: Mention virulence factors of Salmonella enterica
questions.explanation: Salmonella Typhi survives and replicates within macrophages; its Vi capsule reduces opsonization and phagocytosis.
questions.modelAnswer: Salmonella survives and multiplies inside macrophages. Vi capsule of S. typhi and S. paratyphi C is antiphagocytic.

questions.text: On DCA Salmonella typhi produce :-
questions.explanation: Salmonella does not ferment lactose, so it produces colorless or pale colonies on DCA rather than lactose-fermenting colonies.

questions.text: Salmonella infections can vary according to the specie of the organism, discuss:
questions.explanation: Salmonella serovars differ clinically: Typhi and Paratyphi cause enteric fever, Choleraesuis tends toward bacteremia, and Enteritidis/Typhimurium commonly cause enterocolitis.
questions.modelAnswer: S. typhi/paratyphi cause systemic enteric fever; S. choleraesuis causes bacteraemia with focal lesions such as osteomyelitis/arthritis; S. enteritidis and S. typhimurium cause Salmonella enterocolitis/food poisoning. Humans alone carry typhi; other species occur in animals and humans.

questions.text: Which salmonella produce Vi Ag :-
questions.explanation: The Vi capsular antigen is produced by Salmonella Typhi and some Paratyphi C strains.

questions.text: To diagnose salmonella enteric fever in 1st wk, we isolate ! organism from :-
questions.explanation: Blood culture is most useful in the first week of enteric fever, before organisms become more consistently recoverable from stool.

questions.text: In which of the following sites is Salmonella typhi most likely to be found during the carrier state?
questions.explanation: Chronic S. Typhi carriage often persists in the gallbladder, especially when gallstones provide a surface for bacterial biofilm.

questions.text: The ability of intracellular multiplication inside Macrophages is a characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Salmonella Typhi's ability to survive and multiply within macrophages enables systemic dissemination and prolonged infection.

questions.text: Some typhoid fever patients become chronic carriers, describe how this happens and how can we treat those carriers
questions.explanation: S. Typhi may persist in the gallbladder, especially with gallstones, and seed stool for months; prolonged antibiotics are used, with cholecystectomy considered for refractory carriers.
questions.modelAnswer:
Mechanism: organism Establish chronic inf. in gallbladder
tt: 1. Abs (Ciprofloxacin & Ampicillin); failed → cholecyst[uncertain ending]

questions.text: MIC9: A blood test done to diagnose typhoid fever is:
questions.explanation: The Widal agglutination test detects antibodies to Salmonella Typhi O and H antigens, though interpretation depends on timing and local background titers.

questions.text: Onset of clinical illness in enteric fever occurs after :-
questions.explanation: Enteric fever symptoms emerge after secondary bacteremia distributes Salmonella from reticuloendothelial tissues through the bloodstream.

questions.text: The causative organism of Diarrhea which presents with “Pea soup” Stool is
questions.explanation: “Pea-soup” stool is classically associated with enteric fever caused by Salmonella Typhi, rather than toxin-mediated watery diarrhea.

questions.text: Question 15: Mention three virulence factors of salmonella typhi. (June 2015)
questions.explanation: S. Typhi survives within macrophages, uses Vi capsule to resist phagocytosis, and varies H antigens to evade host immunity.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. Intracellular pathogen (survive&multiply in MQ).
2. Capsule ]antiphagocytic[ (VI).
3. Phase variation of H antigens (from group specific phase1 to species specific ph.2).

questions.text: The best time to perform widal test is in :-
questions.explanation: Widal antibodies usually become detectable after the first week, so testing is more informative in the second or third week.

questions.text: MIC9: A blood test done to diagnose typhoid fever is:
questions.explanation: Widal detects antibodies to Salmonella O and H antigens, but culture or validated molecular testing is more specific and useful early.

questions.text: A 3 year-old child is admitted to the hospital because of fever, & epistaxis with rose spots on the trunk.. He has been constipated for the last 3 days. Her temperature is 39°C, abdominal tenderness on physical examination. What is the best vaccine that would prevent this disease if given earlier to this child?
questions.explanation: Conjugating Vi capsular polysaccharide to protein improves T-cell-dependent immunity and vaccine responses in young children.

questions.text: Salmonella infections can varry according to the specie of the organism, discuss:
questions.explanation: Nontyphoidal Salmonella commonly causes gastroenteritis, while S. Typhi and related serovars cause systemic enteric fever.
questions.modelAnswer:
S. typhimurium & Enteritidis: Enterocolitis & Bloody diarrhea
S. Enterica (Typhi, P.T ABC) → Enteric fever

questions.text: MIC9: A blood test done to diagnose typhoid fever is:
questions.explanation: The Widal agglutination test measures antibodies to Salmonella Typhi antigens; interpretation depends on paired titers and local baseline prevalence.

questions.text: 37 year old female admitted to hospital because of fever ĉ increasing anorexia, headache epistaxis, constipation. Blood cultures are done most likely cause of her illness is :-
questions.explanation: Stepwise fever, anorexia, headache, epistaxis, constipation, and bacteremia suggest Salmonella Typhi enteric fever.

questions.text: The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms depends on multiplication inside macrophages?
questions.explanation: S. Typhi survives and multiplies within macrophages, allowing dissemination to the reticuloendothelial system and persistent infection.

questions.text: Give reason : oral vaccine of Salmonella typhi interrupt transmission of enteric fever
questions.explanation: Oral typhoid vaccine stimulates intestinal mucosal immunity, especially secretory IgA, helping reduce acquisition and onward fecal shedding.
questions.modelAnswer: stimulates GIT immunity (secretory IgA)

questions.text: 42. The ability of intracellular multiplication inside macrophages is a characteristic virulence of which of the following organisms?
questions.explanation: Salmonella Typhi is an intracellular pathogen that survives within macrophages and disseminates through the reticuloendothelial system.

questions.text: To isolate organism in typhoid fever bacteraemia, we use:-
questions.explanation: Blood culture yields Salmonella during early typhoid bacteremia and is plated on general media; selective enteric agars are used for stool isolates.

questions.text: A 27-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of fever with headache, weakness & epistaxis.. She has been constipated for the last 3 days. Her temperature is 39°C, abdominal tenderness on physical examination. Blood cultures are done. What is the most likely cause of her illness ?
questions.explanation: High fever, headache, epistaxis, constipation, and bacteremia are compatible with enteric fever due to Salmonella Typhi.

subjects.name: Parasitology
lectureNames: Trematodes of the liver (Fasciola species & Clonorchis sinensis)
Cestodes of the liver (Echinococcus granulosus & Echinococcus multilocularis)

questions.text: PAR1: What investigation would you recommend for acute fascioliasis diagnosis?
questions.explanation: In acute fascioliasis, immature flukes migrate through liver tissue before eggs appear in stool; antibody testing can detect this early phase.
options: Single stool examination for egg detection

questions.text: Stool examination for detection of eggs in chronic fascioliasis can give false +ve results in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Fasciola eggs in stool can be false positives after raw infected liver ingestion or confused with Fasciolopsis eggs.

questions.text: As regards fascioliasis, the false answer is:
questions.explanation: Fasciola infects humans via metacercariae on aquatic plants, not in fish; fish-borne metacercariae transmit other flukes.
options: It presents by fever, hepatomegaly, anemia and eosinophilia.
Infective stage is encyted metacercaria in fish.

questions.text: 39. Duodenal aspirate examination can be used for the diagnosis of
questions.explanation: Duodenal aspirate may recover Fasciola eggs or Giardia trophozoites, organisms whose stages can be present in upper intestinal contents.

questions.text: Serodiagnosis is better than stool examination in diagnosis of fascioliasis.
questions.explanation: Serology can detect Fasciola infection before adult flukes begin laying eggs and can help identify ectopic disease.
questions.modelAnswer:
1- Diagnosis of acute fascioliasis where there is no eggs in stool & early before liver damage [as antibodies can be detected 2-4 weeks after infection or 5-7 weeks before appearance of eggs in stool].
2- Diagnosis of ectopic lesions.

questions.text: Fascioliasis may be complicated by liver fibrosis
questions.explanation: Migrating immature flukes injure liver tissue, while chronic biliary inflammation and obstruction stimulate ductal proliferation and fibrosis.
questions.modelAnswer: Immature flukes destroy hepatic parenchyma during migration with haemorrhage and eosinophil-mediated inflammation. In the chronic biliary phase, mechanical obstruction and the immune response to fluke-excreted proline promote bile-duct proliferation and fibrosis.

questions.text: Fascioliasis may be complicated by anaemia.
questions.explanation: Migrating immature flukes damage liver tissue and cause blood loss, which can lead to iron-deficiency microcytic anemia.
questions.modelAnswer: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia occur due to blood loss from injured liver tissue by migrating metacercaria.

questions.text: Leptocercus cercaria emerges from which of the following snails ?
questions.explanation: Leptocercous cercariae emerge from Segmentina and Lymnaea snails in the relevant trematode cycles.

questions.text: What is the drug of choice in treatment of chlonorchiasis?
questions.explanation: Praziquantel is the standard treatment for Clonorchis; triclabendazole is used for Fasciola.

questions.text: What is the IH snail of Fasciola hepatica ?
questions.explanation: Lymnaea truncatula is the intermediate snail host for Fasciola hepatica, where larval development precedes metacercarial encystment on vegetation.

questions.text: IH of Fasciola hepatica is:
questions.explanation: Lymnaea truncatula is the intermediate snail host for Fasciola hepatica in its classic life cycle.

questions.text: The most common liver fluke in East Asia is:
questions.explanation: Clonorchis sinensis is the common liver fluke of East Asia and is acquired from raw or undercooked freshwater fish.

questions.text: Vegetables must be kept in water with vinegar for 5 min
questions.explanation: Vinegar washing helps detach or kill metacercariae on raw aquatic vegetables, reducing foodborne Fasciola exposure.
questions.modelAnswer: To get rid of metacercaria → Prevention of fascioliasis

questions.text: What is the Chinese liver fluke ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis sinensis is the Chinese liver fluke, acquired from raw freshwater fish containing metacercariae.

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about encysted metacercaria of Fasciola ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola metacercariae are the infective stage; eggs in stool or biliary specimens are the diagnostic stage.

questions.text: There are limitations of stool examination in diagnosis of fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Before adult flukes produce eggs, stool microscopy may be negative; infected liver ingestion can also cause transient spurious egg passage.
questions.modelAnswer: Stool examination is unsuitable in the prepatent period before eggs are produced. Ingesting infected raw liver can cause spurious egg passage without genuine infection; repeat after one week on a liver-free diet. Fasciola eggs are also difficult to distinguish microscopically from some other trematode eggs, including F. buski.

questions.text: Eating raw cattle or sheep liver may lead to suffocation
questions.explanation: Adult Fasciola in raw liver can attach to pharyngeal mucosa, producing edema and airway obstruction known as Halzoun.
questions.modelAnswer: Raw infected cattle or sheep liver can carry adult Fasciola. Adults attach by suckers to the pharynx, causing severe oedema and mechanical obstruction of the airway (pharyngeal fascioliasis or Halzoun), which can cause suffocation.

questions.text: Cercaria of Clonorchis is:
questions.explanation: Clonorchis has a lophocercous cercaria, adapted to leave the snail and enter a fish second intermediate host.

questions.text: Oriental liver fluke is:
questions.explanation: Clonorchis sinensis is the Oriental liver fluke, acquired by eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish containing metacercariae.

questions.text: Fasciola habitat is:
questions.explanation: Adult Fasciola reside in bile ducts, where chronic infection causes biliary inflammation and obstruction.

questions.text: What is the most common liver fluke in East Asia ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis is the major liver fluke endemic in East Asia, where raw freshwater fish consumption sustains transmission.

questions.text: In human liver, Fasciola worms resides in:
questions.explanation: Adult Fasciola migrate into the biliary tree and reside in the bile ducts, where they feed and can obstruct bile flow.

questions.text: Liver-free diet for 1 week is required before stool examination in suspected fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Dietary restriction of liver before stool testing prevents spurious Fasciola eggs passing from ingested infected liver.
questions.modelAnswer:
To avoid spurious infection (pseudo fascioliasis) false +ve fascioliases due to eating infected
raw liver with passage of eggs in stools undigested

questions.text: Which of the following parasites causes liver rot ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola hepatica causes fascioliasis and “liver rot” in sheep and other herbivores, with human infection acquired from aquatic vegetation.

questions.text: Parasites diagnosed by duodenal aspiration:
questions.explanation: Duodenal aspirate can reveal Giardia trophozoites, Strongyloides larvae, and eggs of Fasciola or Clonorchis, so it can aid diagnosis of all listed parasites.

questions.text: Leptocercus cercaria emerges from:
questions.explanation: Fasciola's leptocercous cercaria emerges from the snail, loses its tail, and encysts as metacercaria on aquatic vegetation.

questions.text: What is the best method for diagnosis in ectopic fascioliasis ?
questions.explanation: Ectopic Fasciola infections may not produce eggs in stool, so antibody serology is more useful than stool examination.

questions.text: Leptocercus cercaria emerges from which of the following snails?
questions.explanation: The lymnaeid snail is the first intermediate host in the Fasciola life cycle; cercariae later leave the snail and encyst on vegetation.

questions.text: Cercaria of Fasciola is:
questions.explanation: Fasciola cercariae are leptocercous, with a simple tail; they encyst on aquatic plants as the infective metacercariae.

questions.text: What is the Clonorchis habitat ?
questions.explanation: Adult Clonorchis flukes inhabit small intrahepatic bile ducts, where chronic irritation can cause obstruction and cholangiocarcinoma.

questions.text: Immunodiagnosis are used in diagnosis of all these parasites, except:
questions.explanation: Serology is especially useful before egg production in acute fascioliasis and for tissue larva migrans; intestinal Trichostrongylus is diagnosed by stool eggs.

questions.text: Liver rot is caused by:
questions.explanation: Fasciola hepatica, the liver rot fluke, migrates through liver tissue and later inhabits bile ducts.

questions.text: For early diagnosis & detection of Fasciola gigantica infection, the best investigations is:
questions.explanation: Antibodies by ELISA can detect acute Fasciola infection before mature flukes produce eggs in stool.
options: Stool examination to detect the eggs.

questions.text: Deep freezing at -30 C is preferred before consuming fish
questions.explanation: Freezing fish sufficiently cold kills Clonorchis metacercariae, which otherwise survive in raw or undercooked freshwater fish and infect the biliary tract.
questions.modelAnswer: to kill metacercaria of Clonorchis → prevent Clonorchiasis

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about life cycle of Fasciola ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola eggs hatch in freshwater; free-swimming miracidia then penetrate the snail, so hatching inside the snail is incorrect.

questions.text: Leptocercus cercaria emerges from:
questions.explanation: Leptocercous cercariae emerge from the Fasciola host Lymnaea and from Segmentina in the Fasciolopsis cycle; both listed snails can release this cercarial type.

questions.text: Triad of acute fascioliasis:
questions.explanation: Acute fascioliasis occurs during larval migration through liver tissue, producing fever, tender hepatomegaly, and eosinophilia before adult biliary obstruction.

questions.text: As regard fascioliasis, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Fasciola metacercariae are acquired on aquatic vegetation, not fish; this distinguishes its transmission from fish-borne flukes.
options: Can be diagnosed by duodenal aspiration
Infective stage is encysted metacercaria in fish

questions.text: Which is not a complication of Fascioliasis?
questions.explanation: Fasciola affects liver and bile ducts, causing fibrosis, cholangitis, cholecystitis, or pharyngeal disease; intestinal obstruction is not a typical complication.

questions.text: Halzoun is due to:
questions.explanation: Halzoun follows ingestion of live adult Fasciola in raw liver; the flukes attach to the pharynx and cause acute swelling or obstruction.
options: Ingestion of raw liver contain living Fasciola adults
Ingestion of raw liver contain dead Fasciola adults
Ingestion of raw liver contain dead Fasciola eggs
Ingestion of raw liver contain living Fasciola eggs
Ingestion of raw liver contain living Fasciola metacercariae

questions.text: Which of the following is true about Clonorchis eggs ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis eggs are operculated, have a small abopercular knob, and contain a developed miracidium; the pair captures these traits.

questions.text: Which of the following parasites is diagnosed by duodenal aspiration?
questions.explanation: Duodenal aspirate can reveal Giardia trophozoites, Strongyloides larvae, or fluke eggs, making it a useful diagnostic sample for all listed parasites.

questions.text: Vegetables must be kept in water with vinegar for 5 mints.
questions.explanation: Vinegar soaking helps remove metacercariae from aquatic plants, reducing the foodborne route of Fasciola infection.
questions.modelAnswer: To get rid of metacercariae & prevent fascioliasis.

questions.text: Ectopic fascioliasis is caused by:
questions.explanation: Ectopic fascioliasis follows ingestion of metacercariae that excyst and migrate to abnormal sites rather than settling in the bile ducts.

questions.text: As regards fascioliasis, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Praziquantel does not treat Fasciola effectively; triclabendazole is the drug of choice for this liver fluke.
options: Infection is by eating contaminated vegetables.
Praziquentel is the drug of choice.
The acute phase of the disease begins 2 months after infection.

questions.text: Halzoun is caused by:
questions.explanation: Halzoun is pharyngeal fascioliasis caused by adult Fasciola attaching to the throat after infected raw liver is eaten.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an intestinal parasite?
questions.explanation: Fasciola is a biliary fluke, while Fasciolopsis, Heterophyes, Metagonimus, and Ascaris inhabit the intestine.

questions.text: A patient suffered from fever, hepatomegaly, eosinophilia & jaundice. Sonar showed leaf-like worm in bile duct. The infective stage of this parasitic infection is:
questions.explanation: Fasciola infects humans after ingestion of metacercariae on aquatic plants or contaminated produce, not in fish or snails.
options: Encysted metacercaria in contaminated Bolti fish
Encysted metacercaria in contaminated Cyprinoid fish
Encysted metacercaria in contaminated pig meat

questions.text: As regards halzoon, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Halzoun follows eating raw infected liver containing immature flukes, which attach to pharyngeal mucosa; metacercariae do not lodge there.
options: Encysted metacercariae are attached to the pharynx.
It is caused by eating raw livers of infected sheep and cattle.
It is treated by gargling with alcoholic drink.

questions.text: What is the 2nd IH of Clonorchis sinensis ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis uses cyprinoid freshwater fish as its second intermediate host; the first host is a freshwater snail.

questions.text: Clonorchis is classified as biological carcinogen.
questions.explanation: Chronic Clonorchis irritation of biliary epithelium from suckers and secretions promotes inflammation and increases cholangiocarcinoma risk.
questions.modelAnswer: Due to mechanical damage caused by suckers, movement & feeding activity of adults on biliary epithelium & chemical irritation by toxic secretory excretory products ► biliary ulceration & tissue damage ► cholangiocarcinoma.

questions.text: Clonorchis habitat is:
questions.explanation: Adult Clonorchis reside in bile ducts; eggs pass into bile and stool, while chronic infection injures the biliary epithelium.

questions.text: All about Fasciola eggs are true except:
questions.explanation: Fasciola eggs are operculated and relatively thin-shelled, and serve as the stool diagnostic stage. Humans acquire infection from encysted metacercariae, so both “thick wall” and “infective stage” are exceptions.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a complication of Fascioliasis?
questions.explanation: Fasciola affects liver and biliary passages; intestinal obstruction is not a typical complication of fascioliasis.

questions.text: Drug of choice in treatment of fascioliasis is:
questions.explanation: Triclabendazole is active against immature and adult Fasciola in the liver and bile ducts; other listed benzimidazoles are less effective.

questions.text: 1st IH of Clonorchis sinensis is:
questions.explanation: Clonorchis eggs are ingested by freshwater snails such as Bithynia or Parafossarulus, its first intermediate hosts.

questions.text: Fascioliasis may be complicated by anemia
questions.explanation: During the acute migratory phase, immature flukes damage hepatic tissue and small vessels, causing blood loss and anemia.
questions.modelAnswer: Migration through hepatic parenchyma causes tissue destruction and blood loss, producing hypochromic microcytic anaemia, especially in children.

questions.text: Stool examination is pitfall in diagnosis of acute fascioliasis.
questions.explanation: During acute hepatic migration, Fasciola worms are immature and do not yet lay eggs, so stool microscopy can be negative despite infection.
questions.modelAnswer: Because in case of acute fascioliasis there is no eggs in stool because adult is not formed yet inside bile duct.

questions.text: Which of the following parasites causes Halzoun ?
questions.explanation: The term Halzoun describes pharyngeal fascioliasis, not intestinal or lung fluke infection.

questions.text: What is the Fasciola habitat ?
questions.explanation: Adult Fasciola flukes occupy the bile ducts, where they cause chronic biliary inflammation and obstruction.

questions.text: Serodiagnosis is preferred in diagnosis of fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Serology detects Fasciola antibodies during tissue migration before egg production; it is especially helpful in acute or ectopic disease.
questions.modelAnswer: Specific antibodies can be detected during the acute hepatic stage, allowing treatment before irreversible liver damage and before stool eggs appear. Serology also helps diagnose ectopic fascioliasis, where eggs are not found in faeces.

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about fasciolias ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola metacercariae encyst on aquatic plants, not fish; ingestion from vegetation is the usual route of human infection.
options: Can be diagnosed by duodenal aspiration
Infective stage is encysted metacercaria in fish

questions.text: Spurious infection (pseudo-fascioliasis) is due to:
questions.explanation: Raw infected liver may contain Fasciola eggs; they pass through stool without developing in the person, creating spurious fascioliasis.
options: ingestion of raw liver contain Fasciola adults
Ingestion of raw liver contain Fasciola sporocysts
Ingestion of raw liver contain Fasciola redia
Ingestion of raw liver contain Fasciola metacercariae
Ingestion of raw liver contain Fasciola eggs

questions.text: Liver-free diet is an important instruction before doing stool examination to a patient suspected to have fascioliasis.
questions.explanation: Raw infected liver can contain fluke eggs that pass through the gut undigested, mimicking active infection on stool microscopy; avoid liver before testing.
questions.modelAnswer: To avoid spurious infection which is false positive fascioliasis as a result of eating raw liver which may be infected with eggs that pass in stool undigested.

questions.text: Snail control is an important measure in control programs of Trematodes.
questions.explanation: Snails host essential larval trematode stages, so reducing snail populations can interrupt transmission between eggs and the next host.
questions.modelAnswer: Control interrupts the life cycles of trematodes ( snails are intermediate hosts for all trematodes ).

questions.text: Clonorchis is considered as biological carcinogen
questions.explanation: Chronic Clonorchis infection inflames bile ducts and increases cholangiocarcinoma risk, making it a biological carcinogen.
questions.modelAnswer: Chronic Clonorchis infection causes persistent bile-duct inflammation and fibrosis; the resulting chronic biliary irritation is associated with cholangiocarcinoma. This explains its biological carcinogen designation.

questions.text: Ultrasonography is important in diagnosis of clonorchiasis.
questions.explanation: Clonorchis damages bile ducts and may cause characteristic cystic, mulberry-like duct dilatation; ultrasound can also visualize mobile worms.
questions.modelAnswer: Ultrasonography shows mulberry-like cystic dilatations of intra-hepatic bile ducts & can show moving adult worms.

questions.text: Snail control is one of the methods of prevention of fascioliasis.
questions.explanation: Fasciola requires a freshwater snail intermediate host; snail control reduces the cercariae that later encyst on edible plants.
questions.modelAnswer: Because all trematodes need snails as intermediate hosts & cannot complete its life cycle without it as snails contain the larval stages of trematodes.

questions.text: Spurious infection (pseudo-fascioliasis) is due to ingestion of raw liver containing which of the following ?
questions.explanation: Spurious Fasciola eggs in stool follow ingestion of raw infected liver containing eggs, not an established infection.

questions.text: No affection of liver parenchyma in clonorchiasis
questions.explanation: Clonorchis metacercariae excyst in the duodenum and ascend the ampulla into bile ducts, rather than migrating through liver parenchyma.
questions.modelAnswer: as Metacercaria migrate directly to blood from Ampulla of Vater

questions.text: Chinese liver fluke is:
questions.explanation: Clonorchis sinensis, the Chinese or Oriental liver fluke, inhabits the biliary tree after humans ingest metacercariae in freshwater fish.

questions.text: What is the Oriental liver fluke ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis sinensis is known as the Oriental or Chinese liver fluke and is acquired from freshwater fish.

questions.text: In Pharyngeal fascioliasis,the parasitic stage that causes suffocation is:
questions.explanation: In Halzoun, adult Fasciola flukes attached to the pharyngeal mucosa after raw liver ingestion can obstruct the airway and cause suffocation.

questions.text: Fascioliasis may be manifested by extrahepatic manifestations.
questions.explanation: Immature Fasciola can migrate beyond the liver and settle in skin, lung, or other tissues, producing ectopic lesions.
questions.modelAnswer: Due to invasion of metacercaria of Fasciola to vital organs other than liver & bile duct as lung, skin & intestinal wall (Ectopic fascioliasis).

questions.text: Triclabendazole is the drug of choice in treatment of fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Triclabendazole is effective against both immature migrating Fasciola and adult flukes in the bile ducts.
questions.modelAnswer: Triclabendazole kills both adult flukes in the bile ducts and immature migrating flukes in hepatic parenchyma, covering both biliary and acute hepatic infection.

questions.text: Lymnaea truncatula snail is more difficult to be controlled than Lymnaea cailliaudi snail.
questions.explanation: Lymnaea truncatula is amphibious and escapes aquatic molluscicide exposure, whereas the aquatic L. cailliaudi is easier to treat.
questions.modelAnswer:
As Lymnaea cailliaudi is an aquatic snail that easily killed by molluscicides
while Lymnaea truncatula is an amphibious snail.

questions.text: Spurious infection occurs in:
questions.explanation: Eating infected liver can cause temporary passage of Fasciola eggs through stool without established infection; repeating stool testing after avoiding liver distinguishes this spurious finding.

questions.text: Clonorchis sinensis infection may be complicated by stone formation.
questions.explanation: Clonorchis adults and eggs irritate bile ducts and can serve as a nidus for pigment stones.

questions.text: What is the type of Cercaria of Clonorchis ?

questions.text: The carcinogenic fluke is:
questions.explanation: Chronic Clonorchis infection is associated with cholangiocarcinoma because persistent biliary inflammation and epithelial injury promote malignant change.

questions.text: Which of the following best characterizes the acute prepatent phase of fasciliasis?
questions.explanation: In the prepatent acute phase, immature Fasciola migrate through hepatic parenchyma, causing tissue injury before eggs appear in stool.

Right substernal stabbing pain is a prominent symptom
Migration of metacercaria damages liver parenchyma

questions.text: Fascioliasis is a zoonotic food-borne disease.

=zoonotic because it can be transmitted from cattle & sheep reservoir hosts to man
food-borne disease because infection occurs by ingestion of encysted metacercaria on

questions.text: Halzoun is due to ingestion of raw liver containing which of the following stages ?
questions.explanation: Halzoun follows ingestion of live adult flukes in raw liver; unlike metacercariae on plants, adults attach locally in the pharynx.

questions.text: Which of the following stages is the cause of ectopic fascioliasis ?
questions.explanation: Ingested Fasciola metacercariae excyst and migrate; if they enter ectopic tissues, they can cause ectopic fascioliasis.

questions.text: Clonorchis sinensis may be fatal.
questions.explanation: Chronic Clonorchis infection irritates biliary epithelium and increases cholangiocarcinoma risk; severe cholangitis or obstruction can also be fatal.
questions.modelAnswer: Because it may cause cholangiocarcinoma which is a fatal form of bile duct cancer & also may cause fatal biogenic cholangitis.

questions.text: Triclabendazole is the drug of choice for treatment of infection by:
questions.explanation: Triclabendazole is active against immature and adult Fasciola, making it the preferred treatment for fascioliasis.

questions.text: One of these control measures is not a control method of fascioliasis:

questions.text: Lymnea truncatula snail is more difficult to be controlled than Lymnea cailliaudi snail.

questions.modelAnswer: Because Lymnea cailliaudi is an aquatic snail & easily killed by molluscicides while Lymnea truncatula is an amphibious snail.

questions.text: Fascioliasis is manifested by obstructive jaundice.
questions.explanation: Adult Fasciola in bile ducts causes inflammation, fibrosis, and mechanical blockage, which can impair bile flow and produce obstructive jaundice.
questions.modelAnswer: Due to presence of adult Fasciola in bile duct which leads to proliferation & fibrosis ► mechanical obstruction of bile duct. Also, inflammatory response due to secreted proline leads to more obstruction of bile duct ► obstructive jaundice.

questions.text: Which of the following is common between the life cycle of both Fasciola & Chlonorchis ?

questions.text: Tunnels in liver parenchyma shown by US are helpful in diagnosis of which of following parasites?
questions.explanation: Fasciola larvae migrate through liver tissue, creating branching tunnel-like tracks visible on imaging.

questions.text: What is the carcinogenic fluke ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis is a carcinogenic biliary fluke linked particularly to cholangiocarcinoma after chronic infection.

questions.text: The Leptocercus cercaria is a stage in the life cycle of the following parasite:
questions.explanation: Fasciolopsis buski has a leptocercous cercaria that leaves its snail host before encysting on aquatic vegetation.

questions.text: Which of the following stages is the cause of pharyngeal fasciollasis (Halzoun) ?
questions.explanation: Halzoun follows ingestion of raw infected liver; adult flukes attach in the pharynx and provoke airway obstruction.

questions.text: What is the drug of choice in treatment of fascioliasis?
questions.explanation: Triclabendazole treats fascioliasis because it is active against both immature migrating flukes and adults in the bile ducts.

questions.text: There is no affection on liver parenchyma in acute Clonorchis sinensis infection as in acute fascioliasis.
questions.explanation: Clonorchis metacercariae excyst in the duodenum and ascend into bile ducts; they do not migrate through liver parenchyma like Fasciola.

questions.text: What is the cause of anemia in fascioliasis ?
questions.explanation: Immature Fasciola migrate through and damage liver tissue, causing bleeding that produces blood-loss anemia rather than marrow suppression.
options: Consumption of blood by adult worms
Blood loss from injured parenchymal tissue

questions.text: Extrahepatic manifestations can complicate fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Migrating Fasciola larvae may become lost and lodge in tissues outside the liver, causing ectopic disease rather than normal biliary infection.
questions.modelAnswer: Immature flukes may migrate out of the intestine but fail to reach the liver. They settle in other tissues and produce ectopic lesions, sometimes at serious body sites.

questions.text: IH of Fasciola gigantica is:
questions.explanation: Lymnaea cailliaudi is the intermediate host snail for Fasciola gigantica in the regional life cycle.

questions.text: Chronic phase of Fascioliasis is manifested by obstructive jaundice
questions.explanation: Adult flukes settle in bile ducts and can mechanically obstruct bile flow; chronic inflammation and fibrosis further worsen cholestasis.
questions.modelAnswer: Adult flukes occupy the bile ducts; mechanical obstruction and chronic inflammatory/fibrotic changes impair bile flow and cause obstructive jaundice.

questions.text: CT scan & MRI are important in diagnosis of clonorchiasis.
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional imaging helps detect biliary masses and characterize suspected cholangiocarcinoma, a complication of chronic Clonorchis infection.
questions.modelAnswer: Because they are important in diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma.

questions.text: All about life cycle of Fasciola are true except:
questions.explanation: Fasciola eggs hatch in water before miracidia enter snails; they do not hatch inside the snail host.

questions.text: Indigestion (dyspepsia) is the main complaint in chronic fascioliasis
questions.explanation: Bile-duct obstruction reduces bile delivery to the intestine, impairing fat digestion and causing dyspepsia in chronic fascioliasis.
questions.modelAnswer:
Due to obstruction of bile duct by adult worms → prevent passage of bile to small intestine &
digestion of fat.

questions.text: Which is not a complication of Fascioliasis?
questions.explanation: Intestinal obstruction is not a usual Fasciola complication because the parasite migrates through liver tissue and later inhabits bile ducts.

questions.text: In acute fascioliasis the best method for diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Serology can detect acute fascioliasis during the prepatent migratory phase, before adult flukes release eggs into stool.

questions.text: What is the type of cercaria of Fasciola ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola cercariae are leptocercous before encysting as metacercariae on aquatic vegetation.

questions.text: Fascioliasis may be manifested by indigestion & fat intolerance.
questions.explanation: Biliary obstruction reduces bile delivery to the small intestine, impairing fat digestion and causing indigestion or fat intolerance.
questions.modelAnswer: Due to obstruction of bile duct by adult worms which prevent passage of bile to small intestine & prevent digestion of fat.

questions.text: IH of Fasciola gigantica is:
questions.explanation: Fasciola gigantica uses Lymnaea cailliaudi as its intermediate host snail.

questions.text: Give reason/interpret the following statements (1mark each): The type and mechanism of anemia in fascioliasis differs from that in fasciolopsis.
questions.explanation: Fasciola larvae damage liver tissue and cause blood loss with microcytic anemia; Fasciolopsis can sequester B12 and impair absorption, causing macrocytosis.
questions.modelAnswer: Fascioliasis: immature flukes destroy hepatic tissue and cause blood loss, producing hypochromic microcytic anaemia. Fasciolopsiasis: intestinal malabsorption, including vitamin B12 deficiency, produces a macrocytic/B12-deficiency type rather than the blood-loss mechanism.

questions.text: Pharyngeal fascioliasis (Halzoun) is caused by:
questions.explanation: Halzoun results when live adult Fasciola from raw infected liver attach to the pharyngeal mucosa.

questions.text: PAR1: What investigation would you recommend for acute fascioliasis diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Antibody testing can diagnose acute fascioliasis before mature flukes produce detectable eggs in stool.
options: Single stool examination for egg detection

questions.text: What is the 1st IH snail of Clonorchis sinensis ?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis uses Bithynia or Parafossarulus snails as first intermediate hosts; fish serve as the second host.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is not a complication of fascioliasis?
questions.explanation: Fasciola affects liver and biliary structures; intestinal obstruction is not a typical consequence, unlike inflammation or ectopic migration.

questions.text: Sanitary aquaculture can prevent infection with which of the following parasites?
questions.explanation: Clonorchis transmission is linked to freshwater fish and aquaculture; sanitation that prevents fecal contamination of fish ponds interrupts its cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about Fasciola ?
questions.explanation: Fasciola is zoonotic, not anthroponotic: livestock are major reservoirs, and humans are accidental hosts.

questions.text: All about encysted metacercaria of Fasciola are true except:
questions.explanation: Metacercariae are the infective stage for humans, whereas eggs are the diagnostic stage; they are encysted on vegetation and are not the stool-diagnostic form.

questions.text: What is the best method for diagnosis in acute fascioliasis ?
questions.explanation: Serology is preferred in acute fascioliasis because immature flukes have not yet matured to egg-laying adults.

questions.text: Mulberry-like cystic dilatation of bile ducts shown by US are helpful in diagnosis of which of following parasites?
questions.explanation: Mulberry-like intrahepatic bile-duct dilatation is characteristic of chronic Clonorchis infection.

questions.text: All about Fasciola are true except:
questions.explanation: Fasciola is zoonotic: livestock and other mammals maintain the cycle, while people are incidental hosts; eggs and metacercariae are diagnostic and infective stages respectively.

questions.text: The Leptocercus cercaria formed of
questions.explanation: Leptocercous cercariae have a head with cystogenous glands and a simple, uncovered tail.
options: head containing penetration glands with simple tail
head containing cystogenous glands with simple tail
head containing penetration glands with tail covered by membrane
head containing cystogenous glands with tail covered by membrane

questions.text: IH of Fasciola hepatica is:
questions.explanation: Lymnaea truncatula is the first intermediate host of Fasciola hepatica in the classic life cycle.

questions.text: What is / are the intermediate host(s) of Echinococcus multilocularis ?
questions.explanation: Rodents are the usual intermediate hosts of Echinococcus multilocularis; humans may be accidental hosts but are not normally part of the transmission cycle.

questions.text: Diagnostic stage(s) of Echinococcus granulosus is/are:
questions.explanation: Humans with Echinococcus granulosus harbor larval hydatid cysts and hydatid sand; they do not carry adult worms.

questions.text: Layers of hydatid cyst are:
questions.explanation: A hydatid cyst comprises the parasite's inner germinal and laminated layers plus the host-derived outer fibrous pericyst.

questions.text: Washing hands after contact with dogs is recommended.
questions.explanation: Dog feces can contain infective Echinococcus or Toxocara eggs; handwashing limits accidental ingestion after contact, especially with contaminated fur or soil.
questions.modelAnswer: Dogs are the DH of Echinococcus & Toxocara & eggs of these worms are infective to man causing hydatid disease & toxocariasis & these eggs are excreted in stool of dogs. So, playing with dogs may cause hydatid disease & toxocariasis.

questions.text: Infective stage(s) of Echinococcus granulosus is/are:
questions.explanation: People acquire cystic echinococcosis by swallowing Echinococcus eggs shed in dog feces; hydatid cysts are the larval stage.

questions.text: All about sterile hydatid cyst are true except:
questions.explanation: A sterile hydatid cyst lacks viable scolices; fluid and antigen may remain, but absence of scolices distinguishes it from fertile cysts.

questions.text: Supervision of persons working in furs manufactures help in control of which of the following parasites?
questions.explanation: Alveolar echinococcosis is acquired from Echinococcus multilocularis eggs, a zoonosis associated with canid definitive hosts and fur-bearing wildlife.

questions.text: Feeding dogs with carcass of sheep, camels & cattle should be avoided.
questions.explanation: Dogs become definitive hosts after eating livestock viscera containing hydatid cysts, so feeding them carcasses sustains transmission.
questions.modelAnswer: Because viscera of dead cattle & sheep may contain hydatid cyst so, dogs become infected with Echinococcus granulosus adults in their small intestine then infect other people with eggs in their stool.

questions.text: What is the most affected human organ by hydatid cyst?
questions.explanation: The liver filters portal blood and is the most common site for Echinococcus granulosus hydatid cysts; the lungs are second.

questions.text: A patient complains of right abdominal mass in the liver. Aspiration from the mass showed clear yellowish fluid. Which of the following is not a control measure of this disease?
questions.explanation: Snails are irrelevant to the Echinococcus life cycle; dog–livestock transmission is interrupted through deworming and safe disposal of infected offal.
options: Preventing dogs from eating carcasses of sheep
Deworming of dogs twice a year
Washing hands after contact with dogs specially puppies

questions.text: Alveolar hydatid cyst behaves like a malignant tumor.
questions.explanation: Alveolar Echinococcus grows by infiltrative budding with little limiting fibrous tissue, resembling a malignant lesion.
questions.modelAnswer: Because it has no laminated or fibrous layers so, its germinal layer is in direct contact with surrounding tissues & germinal cells spread to vital organs & cause formation of secondary cysts away from the original cyst.

questions.text: A shepherd complains of cough and difficulty in breathing with multiple cystic lesions in the lung. Which of the following may be found in aspirate from cysts?
questions.explanation: Hydatid sand contains free scolices and hooklets within hydatid fluid; aspirate from a cyst may reveal these parasite elements.

questions.text: All about osseous hydatid cyst are true except:
questions.explanation: Bone hydatid cysts lack a well-formed fibrous pericyst and laminated layer because rigid bone limits the host response and cyst expansion.

questions.text: Hydatid cyst is larva of:
questions.explanation: A hydatid cyst is the larval metacestode of Echinococcus granulosus, which develops after the oncosphere reaches an organ.

questions.text: Indirect serological diagnosis of hydatid disease is preferred than direct diagnosis by tabbing hydatid cyst fluid through cyst puncture.
questions.explanation: Puncturing a hydatid cyst can spill antigenic fluid and trigger anaphylaxis or disseminate viable germinal material, so serology is safer diagnostically.
questions.modelAnswer: Because rupture of hydatid cyst may lead to anaphylactic shock. Also puncture of hydatid cyst may lead to spread of germinal cells to other organs & formation of secondary cysts.

questions.text: Alveolar hydatid cyst is most commonly found in:
questions.explanation: Echinococcus multilocularis larvae most often establish in the liver, where infiltrative growth resembles an invasive tumor.

questions.text: What are the taken precautions during PAIR ?
questions.explanation: PAIR must be image-guided, performed by experienced clinicians with anesthesia support, and paired with antiparasitic treatment to reduce leakage risks.
options: Should be done by experienced physician.
Should be guided by CT or US.
Patient should receive chemotherapy before & after the procedure.

questions.text: Which of the following isn’t present in hyadatid sand?
questions.explanation: Hydatid sand consists of scolices, brood capsules, and hooklets in fluid; the laminated ectocyst is part of the cyst wall, not the sand.

questions.text: The intermediate host(s) of Echinococcus multilocularis is/are
questions.explanation: Rodents serve as natural intermediate hosts for E. multilocularis; humans are accidental dead-end hosts after ingesting eggs.

questions.text: Most common intermediate host for Echinococcus granulosus is:
questions.explanation: Sheep are the common intermediate host of Echinococcus granulosus; dogs carry the adult tapeworm.

questions.text: Which layer of E.granulosus hydatid cyst is evoked by host immunity ?
questions.explanation: The outer fibrous pericyst is formed by the host response around the parasite's laminated and germinal layers.

questions.text: Dogs should not be present in slaughterhouses.
questions.explanation: Preventing dogs from eating infected viscera stops hydatid cysts from maturing into adult Echinococcus in the canine intestine.
questions.modelAnswer:
to be prevented from eating infected carcasses of cattle & sheep containing hydatid cyst of
Echinococcus granulosus No spread of disease by contact to other people

questions.text: All about osseous hydatid cyst are true except:

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about osseous hydatid cyst?

questions.text: The intermediate host of Echinoccocus multilocularis are:
questions.explanation: Rodents are the normal intermediate hosts of E. multilocularis, with humans occasionally infected as accidental hosts.

questions.text: The most affected human organ by hydatid cyst is:
questions.explanation: Hydatid cysts most often develop in the liver because portal blood delivers ingested embryos there first.

questions.text: Puncture aspiration injection reaspiration [PAIR] is dangerous to the patient.
questions.explanation: Puncturing a hydatid cyst can release antigen-rich fluid and viable protoscolices, risking anaphylaxis and secondary dissemination if handled unsafely.
questions.modelAnswer: Because puncture of hydatid cyst to examine hydatid fluid may be fatal because it may lead to rupture of the cyst & anaphylactic shock.

questions.text: Absence of which of the following components enhances metastatic spread of E.multilocularis?
questions.explanation: Without laminated and fibrous limiting layers, E. multilocularis lesions infiltrate adjacent tissue and spread in a tumor-like pattern.

questions.text: What is the drug of choice in treatment of hydatidosis ?
questions.explanation: Albendazole inhibits parasite microtubules and is the main benzimidazole used for cystic echinococcosis, often alongside procedural management.

questions.text: Why alveolar hydatid cyst is more dangerous than unilocular cyst?

options: Has irregular outline which is not defined from surrounding tissues

questions.text: Indications of chemotherapy for treatment of hydatidosis are:
questions.explanation: Albendazole is used for inoperable, multiple, or recurrent cysts and alongside PAIR or surgery to control viable parasite tissue.

questions.text: During surgical removal of a unilocular hydatid cyst, the cyst has to be enucleated without puncture.
questions.explanation: Avoiding cyst puncture limits antigen spillage that can cause anaphylaxis and prevents viable protoscolices from seeding secondary cysts.
questions.modelAnswer: Because rupture of hydatid cyst may lead to anaphylactic shock. Also puncture of hydatid cyst may lead to spread of germinal cells to other organs & formation of secondary cysts.

questions.text: Larva of which of the following parasites has a malignant behavior ?

questions.text: Alveolar hydatid cyst is more dangerous than unilocular because:
questions.explanation: Alveolar hydatid lesions have irregular, poorly defined margins and infiltrate surrounding tissue rather than remaining a single encapsulated cyst.

It is composed of small irregular cavities
It has irregular outline which is not defined from surrounding tissues

questions.text: Which of the following forms of Echinococcus granulosus develop into adult worms in the small intestine of dogs?

questions.text: Man act as blind intermediate host in hydatid disease.

questions.text: The drug of choice in treatment of hydatidosis is:

questions.text: Alveolar hydatid cyst is commonly found in:

questions.explanation: Albendazole is used for multiple or inoperable hydatid cysts and as an adjunct to surgery or PAIR to reduce viable parasite burden.

questions.text: The larval stage of the following parasite has a malignant-like behavior in human tissue:

questions.text: Anaphylactic shock can be a complication of:

questions.text: Man can act as blind intermediate hosts in infection with:

questions.text: Which of the following are the most important filters for hexacanth embryos of Echinococcus granulosus?

questions.text: Intrahepatic portal hypertension due to slow metastatic spread is a complication of which of the following parasites?

questions.text: The definitive host(s) of Echinococcus multilocularis is/are

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about sterile hydatid cyst ?

questions.text: The intermediate host of Echinoccocus multilocularis are:

questions.text: Feeding dogs with carcasses of sheep & cattle should be avoided.

questions.text: What is / are the definitive host(s) of Echinococcus multilocularis ?

questions.text: Larva has a malignant behavior in:

questions.text: What is / are the infective stage(s) of Echinococcus granulosus ?

questions.text: What is the habitat of Echinococcus granulosus adult worm ?

questions.text: What is / are the intermediate host(s) of Echinococcus granulosus ?
questions.explanation: People and livestock, especially sheep, act as intermediate hosts after ingesting eggs; dogs are the definitive hosts of E. granulosus.

questions.text: Layers of hydatid cyst are:
questions.explanation: Hydatid cysts have an inner germinal layer, an acellular laminated layer, and an outer host-derived fibrous layer.

questions.text: Dogs should be prevented from wandering in slaughterhouses.
questions.explanation: Dogs acquire adult E. granulosus by eating infected livestock viscera; their fecal eggs contaminate environments and expose people and animals.
questions.modelAnswer: To be prevented from eating viscera of dead cattle & sheep which may contain hydatid cyst so, become infected with Echinococcus granulosus adults in their small intestine then infect other people with eggs in their stool.

questions.text: The most common organ affected by hydatid cyst is liver.
questions.explanation: After ingestion, oncospheres first pass through the portal circulation, making the liver the most common site for hydatid cysts.

questions.text: Anaphylactic shock can be a complication of which of the following parasites?

questions.text: As regards hydatidosis, the false statement is:

questions.text: Alveolar hydatid cyst is more dangerous than unilocular hydatid cyst.
questions.explanation: Alveolar Echinococcus grows infiltratively with a poorly defined boundary, allowing progressive invasion of surrounding tissues and organs.
questions.modelAnswer: Because it has no laminated or fibrous layers so, its germinal layer is in direct contact with surrounding tissues & germinal cells spread to vital organs & cause formation of secondary cysts away from the original cyst.

questions.text: Give reason/interpret the following statements (1mark each): The most common presentation of Hydatid disease of long bones is pathological fracture.
questions.explanation: Osseous hydatid cysts lack a strong laminated layer and pericyst, allowing infiltrative, poorly contained growth in bone.
questions.modelAnswer: Osseous hydatid cyst has poorly developed laminated layer and pericyst, allowing uncontrolled growth in bone. The expanding cyst destroys bone and predisposes to spontaneous/pathological fracture.

questions.text: 5. PAIR technique is used for the treatment of

questions.text: What is the 1st Intermediate host of Heterophyes ?

questions.text: A patient from Manzala, developed diarrhea after eating Feseekh in Sham El-Naseem. The infective stage of this parasitic disease is:

questions.text: Miracidium of Heterophyes is not found free in water?

questions.text: What is drug of choice used to treat this case?

questions.text: Which of the following snails is resistant to molluscicides ?

questions.text: Pernicious anemia is caused by which of the following parasites?:

questions.text: Which of the following cestodes has an operculated egg ?

questions.text: Solid cestode larvae:

questions.text: The solid Cestoda larva is:

questions.text: The diagnostic stage(s) of Diphyllobothrium latum:

questions.text: Eradication of water flea is important for control of the following parasite.

questions.text: The fish tape worm is
questions.explanation: Diphyllobothrium latum is the fish tapeworm; its plerocercoid larva encysts in freshwater fish and infects humans when eaten.

questions.text: Destruction of the snails is one of the methods of control all of these parasites except:

questions.text: Which of the following cestodes are vector-borne ?
questions.explanation: All three listed cestodes use arthropods: copepods, fleas, or grain beetles carry their infective larval stages.

questions.text: The cestode which has no gravid segment is:
questions.explanation: D. latum continuously releases eggs through a uterine pore, so it lacks the distended gravid segments typical of many cestodes.

questions.text: Taenia solium is more dangerous than Taenia saginata.
questions.explanation: T. solium eggs can infect humans and develop into tissue cysticerci, whereas T. saginata eggs do not cause human cysticercosis.

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about cysticercus cellulosae ?

questions.explanation: Cysticercus bovis is a fluid-filled larva with an invaginated scolex and no hooks; it is not solid.

questions.text: A patient developed perianal itching after eating pork meat. Stool analysis showed fleshy parts. The most serious complication of this parasitic disease is:

questions.text: Personal hygiene is very important in patient with Taeniasis solium.
questions.explanation: Handwashing prevents ingestion of T. solium eggs from fecal contamination, which can cause cysticercosis even in a person with an adult tapeworm.

questions.text: What is/are the diagnostic stage(s) of Taenia ?
questions.explanation: Taenia species are diagnosed from eggs and gravid proglottids in stool; species identification relies more on segment or scolex features.

questions.text: Which of the following is untrue about cysticercus bovis ?
questions.explanation: Cysticercus bovis is a fluid-filled larva with an unarmed scolex; “solid” is the false feature.

questions.text: Cystic cestode larvae:
questions.explanation: Cysticercus and cysticercoid are cyst-like cestode larval forms; their morphology and intermediate hosts differ among Taenia and Hymenolepis.

questions.text: What is the natural IH of T. solium ?
questions.explanation: Pigs are the normal intermediate host for T. solium, where larvae form cysticerci in muscle.

questions.explanation: Taenia saginata has an unarmed scolex without a rostellum or hooks, distinguishing it from armed T. solium.

questions.text: Infective stage in cysticercosis is:
questions.explanation: Swallowing T. solium eggs releases oncospheres that migrate into tissues and form cysticerci; eating pork cysticerci causes intestinal taeniasis instead.

questions.text: The gravid segment of T.saginata & solium can be differentiated by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Gravid segments of T. saginata have many more lateral uterine branches than T. solium, aiding species identification.

questions.text: Armed tapeworm is:
questions.explanation: Taenia solium has an armed scolex with a rostellum and hooks; T. saginata is unarmed.

questions.text: What is the Pork tapeworm ?
questions.explanation: Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm; pigs are its usual intermediate host, while humans carry the adult worm or accidentally develop cysticercosis.

questions.text: Taenia Infection is associated with perianal dermatitis

questions.explanation: People can carry adult T. solium after eating cysticerci or act as accidental intermediate hosts after swallowing eggs that form tissue cysts.

questions.explanation: Praziquantel is effective against adult intestinal T. solium, though potential cysticercosis risk makes species identification clinically relevant.

questions.explanation: Neurocysticercosis follows ingestion of T. solium eggs; larvae can lodge in the brain and provoke seizures or neurologic symptoms.

questions.text: The normal intermediate host in Taenia solium is

options: Autoinfection in T.solium leading to cysticercosis.
The hooks in Taenia solium scolex leading bleeding.

questions.text: What is the blind IH of T. solium cysticercosis ?
questions.explanation: Humans can become an accidental intermediate host after swallowing T. solium eggs, developing cysticercosis rather than adult tapeworm infection.

questions.explanation: Internal autoinfection by T. solium eggs can cause cysticercosis, and H. nana can multiply through autoinfection within the same host.

questions.text: the infective stage of Taenia saginata is
questions.explanation: Cattle muscle cysticerci (Cysticercus bovis) become adult T. saginata in people who eat undercooked beef.

questions.explanation: T. solium and H. nana can cause internal autoinfection, while Strongyloides larvae can reinvade through intestinal or perianal tissues.

questions.text: The infective stage of Dipylidium caninum is

questions.explanation: Swallowed T. solium eggs release embryos that invade tissues and develop into cysticerci; pork cysticerci instead cause intestinal taeniasis.

questions.text: Man is not the only DH in which of the following cestodes ?

Number of ova within the uterus.

questions.text: The drug of choice for treatment of Taenia solium infection is:
questions.explanation: Praziquantel kills adult T. solium in the intestine, but cysticercosis risk means treatment choice should account for possible tissue infection.

questions.explanation: Humans can be definitive hosts for adult T. solium and H. nana, and intermediate hosts when they ingest their eggs.

questions.text: The cystic larva of Cestoda

To prevent infection with Taenia saginata or Taenia solium as the improperly cooked beef may

it disintegrates the gravid segments → releases eggs → increases the risk of internal
